News.title: Karl Bushby route map – how many miles did he complete in 28-year journey around the world?
News.content:
Next

KARL Bushby is an adventurer who set out on a spectacular journey across the world in 1998.

As his record-breaking journey across the globe is almost over, here we take a look at the route he took and the key moments along the way.

Who is Karl Bushby?

Karl Bushby is a former paratrooper from Hull, born March 30, 1969.



He served with the British Army for 11 years, which included meeting his then wife Angela in Belfast.



The pair had a child together before divorcing in 1995.

Karl’s journey was one that he planned whilst in the army, with former colleagues suggesting it wouldn’t be possible when he told them of his plans.

What was Karl Bushby’s route?

Karl Bushby started his journey in Punta Arenas, Chile in November 1998, when he was 29 years old.

He initially believed the journey would take 12 years, with the plan being to complete an unbroken journey across the world without any motorised transportation.

Only walking and swimming was allowed, and wasn’t allowed to step back into the UK before completing the journey.

The total distance he will eventually cover by the time he arrives in Hull is roughly 36,000 miles.



This includes travelling through 29 countries and four continents, South America, North America, Asia and Europe.

News.title: House of horrors full of animal poo & roaches uncovered after cops find boy, 4, wading alone in pond & arrest parents
News.content:
Next

COPS have uncovered an alleged “house of horrors” full of animal poo and crawling with cockroaches after a four-year-old child was found alone in a pond.

Officers made the stomach-churning discovery in Florida after the boy wearing only a nappy was spotted in a murky retention pond.



Shocking bodycam footage captured the moment deputies rushed to the scene in Deltona after horrified passersby raised the alarm.

“Hey, come here…it’s OK,” an officer can be heard telling the toddler as he plucks him from the water and carries him safely into the back of a patrol car.



Following the rescue, cops entered the boy’s nearby home where they allegedly found “copious animal waste”, rampant black mould and a severe roach infestation.

Officers also discovered a “caged and neglected” dog, which was handed over to Deltona Animal control.

Parents Fermin Medran-Perez, 26, and Jeneixa Rodriguez-Crespo, 24, were arrested and charged with child neglect and animal cruelty.

In a post on social media, Volusia Sheriff’s Office said: “On Saturday morning, deputies responded to a call about an unaccompanied toddler walking around a retention pond in Deltona.

“Deputies in the area heard the call on Live 911 and quickly spotted the child in the water.

“Inside, they found filthy conditions including copious animal waste, a roach infestation and mould.



“Deltona Animal Control responded, taking custody of a caged and neglected dog.

“Both parents were arrested on charges of child neglect and animal cruelty.

“A grandparent took custody of the child and the Department of Child and Families (DCF) was contacted for follow-up.”



The harrowing discovery comes after a mum and grandmother accused of locking a boy in a room allegedly barricaded with wooden boards and zip ties were charged.

The five-year-old was found naked wandering the streets after escaping the real-life “house of horrors”, leading to the arrest of the two family members.

The alleged victim’s mother Jade Shuey, 21, her boyfriend Tucker Heagy, also 21, and grandmother Stephan Schaffner, 42, all were charged.

Investigators claim the youngster was trapped inside a dirty bedroom against his will at a property in Township near Philadelphia.

The room’s doorway was blocked with a baby gate held together with zip ties and duct tape, topped with wooden boards drilled into the frame to prevent escape, police allege.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Food and rubbish were allegedly strewn across the floor, with the walls and window stained with what appeared to be human faeces.

The remainder of the house appeared in “hoarder conditions”, according to Pennsylvania State Police.

News.title: ‘Lad of the Manor’ who inherited £50m estate after DNA test from dead dad GUILTY of breaking man’s leg in wedding brawl
News.content:
PUB ATTACK ‘Lad of the Manor’ who inherited £50m estate after DNA test from dead dad GUILTY of breaking man’s leg in wedding brawl







Next

A FORMER care worker who inherited a £50million estate from his late dad has been found guilty of breaking a man’s leg in a brawl.

Jordan Adlard-Rogers became known as “Lad of the Manor” after he spent decades trying to prove aristocrat Charles Rogers was his biological dad.



He ended up inheriting the sprawling 1,536-acre Penrose Estate in Cornwall after proving he was Charles’ son with a DNA test following his dad.

The 38-year-old has now been found guilty of grievous bodily harm after he punched a man to the ground at a wedding reception.



Truro Crown Court heard Adlard-Rogers was on the dancefloor of a wedding reception when came “face to face” with Sebastian Winzar.

The thug then punched Sebastian to the ground – causing the victim to fracture his leg in two places.



Sebastian spent five days in hospital before returning four days later for an operation to his left shin.

He told the jury he had been catching up with friends at the Out Of The Blue pub in Porthleven when he was attacked.

Sebastian said Adlard-Rogers “came in shouting at me, saying I was a wife beater”, adding: “I don’t know where that came from.”

He continued: “I was shocked and he kept starting on me, so I walked away. He was shouting and just throwing his arms around.



“I went up to him and the next thing I can’t remember.”

The court played CCTV that showed the incident on July 13, 2024.

Robin Smith, defending Adlard-Rogers, claimed the heir was “trying to calm things down” and accused Sebastian of being the “aggressor”.



He said the footage showed Adlard-Rogers “doing a little Irish jig thing” before he suggested going outside with Sebastian.

Adlard-Rogers told jurors he just wanted to “diffuse the situation” and said it was “quite embarrassing on my behalf.”

He added: “I said, ‘If you’re going to talk to me like this let’s talk outside’, because I don’t want to disrespect the wedding venue.”

The wealthy heir claimed he lashed out in self-defence after being threatened and headbutted.

He told the court he had done “the right thing at the right time” when he floored Sebastian.



After the verdict, the judge said all sentencing options were open but warned him to “prepare yourself” for immediate custody when he returns to court on December 11.

Adlard-Rogers made headlines after swapped his modest community support wage for the sprawling country estate in 2019.

He had suspected for years he was Charles’ illegitimate son but was only able to prove it following the lord of the manor’s death aged 62 with a DNA test.



With both the deceased owner’s mother and brother already dead, Adlard-Rogers suddenly became the sole heir to the massive fortune.

The estate makes money from investments in stocks and shares and renting a number of parcels of land to local farmers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Following his inheritance, Adlard-Rogers said he wanted to use his newfound privilege to help local communities.

He said in 2019: “I’ve been at the point of worrying about the next bill and have had a tough start in life but now I’m here I want to help people.”

News.title: Emergency weather alert in Brit holiday hotspot as storm batters Greek island with heavy rain and flooding
News.content:
Next

AN EMERGENCY weather alert has hit a popular Brit holiday hotspot as a powerful storm batters a Greek island with torrential rain and flooding.

Storm Agneta has struck Rhodes with ferocious downpours, turning roads into raging rivers, sweeping away cars and swamping homes.



Terrified residents and tourists were sent an emergency warning at around 3.30am on Monday as storms wreaked havoc across the island.

Authorities urged people in the Archangelos area to stay off the roads as relentless rainfall left parts of the island battling dangerous rising waters.



Schools were forced to shut in Archangelos and Afantou as officials scrambled to protect pupils and teachers from the treacherous conditions.

Firefighters rushed to tackle the chaos, pumping water from three flooded sites, cutting down a fallen tree and moving two people to safety.



Across the Dodecanese islands, emergency crews were bombarded with 18 calls for help as the storm continued to ravage.

On nearby Kalymnos, firefighters were forced to pump away floodwater and remove a fallen tree.

Meanwhile, the eastern Aegean island of Samos was also hammered by the brutal weather, with emergency services receiving 28 desperate calls for assistance.

Crews carried out 10 water-pumping operations as the relentless downpours left parts of the island waterlogged.



The terrifying conditions follow scenes of devastation in central Greece, where floodwaters swallowed streets and submerged cars.

Volos and neighbouring Nea Ionia were among the worst-hit areas on Sunday as roads disappeared beneath torrents of muddy water.

Shocking scenes showed cars submerged up to their wheels as the storm battered the region.



In nearby Nea Anchialos, the Alonaki area was left reeling after raging floodwaters surged through streets, flooded homes and swept away vehicles.

Firefighters in Volos received 12 emergency calls, carrying out seven water-pumping operations and cutting down two trees.

And the nightmare is far from over, with Greece’s National Meteorological Service warning that violent thunderstorms and heavy rain could continue into Tuesday.

A red weather warning was issued as Storm Agneta threatened to unleash further havoc across western and northern Greece and the eastern Aegean islands.

Popular Brit holiday destinations including Corfu and Zante were also in the firing line as the fierce weather system swept across the country.



On Monday, the Ionian islands faced another battering from midday, while heavy rain and thunderstorms were expected to lash Epirus, western Central Greece and the western and southern Peloponnese later in the day.

The Dodecanese islands were also warned to brace for further downpours until late Monday night.

And Tuesday could bring another round of storm chaos, with heavy rain forecast across the Ionian islands until midday and parts of western Greece until the afternoon.



Central and eastern Macedonia, Thrace and islands across the northern and eastern Aegean were also expected to face severe thunderstorms.

Forecasters warned that some areas could even be pelted by hail as the dangerous weather continued to sweep across the country.

Civil Protection officials have urged residents and holidaymakers to take extra precautions as the threat of further flooding looms.

People were warned against attempting to cross swollen streams or flooded roads, either on foot or by car, during storms and for several hours afterwards.

Authorities also advised the public to secure loose objects, clear gutters and avoid outdoor work or activities at sea during thunderstorms.



Tourists caught in hailstorms were urged to shelter inside buildings or vehicles and steer clear of large trees, hanging signs and balconies.

The latest weather nightmare comes just a week after devastating floods tore through parts of Greece, leaving roads impassable and communities cut off.

Platanias, in South Pelion, was among the worst-hit areas after raging torrents severed access to the entire right-hand side of the village.



Emergency alerts were sent to residents’ phones, warning them to avoid basements and ground floors as floodwaters threatened to surge into properties.

One devastated business owner revealed how the deluge had wrecked his oil-storage warehouse, sending huge quantities of his stock spilling across the floor.

He said: “Everything we had inside, cans full of 200 kilos of oil, all spilled.”

Meanwhile, the nearby holiday island of Skiathos was also left battling the aftermath of the destructive storms.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Main roads were rendered impassable as swollen streams and landslides wreaked havoc across the island.



Debris and fallen earth blocked routes, including the main road towards the popular tourist area of Koukounaries, as Greece struggled to recover from the latest wave of extreme weather.

News.title: Walkers urgently pulls crisps from UK supermarket shelves over dangerous health hazard
News.content:
Next

WALKERS has urgently recalled a popular crisp flavour over a potential risk to health.

Customers have been urged “not to consume” the product.

PepsiCo has issued a recall over its Walkers Variety Snacks Sharing Box after the Monster Munch Giants Roast Beef pack was discovered to contain an undeclared allergen on its packaging.



The popular crisp flavour was found to have not labelled wheat (gluten) on the outer packaging of the sharing box.



However, the snack firm noted that individual bags inside the box have been correctly labelled.

As a result, this poses as a potential health risk for anyone with an allergy or intolerance to wheat or gluten, or with coeliac disease.

The affected products include batches with the code 107543, as well as the Best Before dates of November 21, 2026 and January 16, 2027.



Shoppers have been urged not to eat the product, and instead will be able to email customer support for a full refund.

Alternatively, customers will also be able to call the PepsiCo Consumer Care Line for more information.

Walkers has also contacted relevant allergy support organisations, which will notify their members about the recall.

If shoppers begin experiencing symptoms of an allergic reaction – including hives and difficulty breathing – after consuming the product, they are advised to seek medical help immediately.



This recall affects England, Scotland and Wales specifically.

News.title: Moment massive fire tears through 136-year-old golf club as public warned to stay away
News.content:
Next

THIS is the terrifying moment a huge fire tore through a historic golf club as firefighters worked through the night to tackle the flames.

North Wales Fire and Rescue Service rushed to Conwy Golf Club, Wales, at 9.20pm on Saturday and warned the public to stay away.



Footage shows bright orange flames engulfing the clubhouse’s roof on the night of Halloween.

Huge plumes of smoke can be seen rising into the air as the fire consumes the 136-year-old building.



The clubhouse had recently been refurbished with two bars, a 60 seat restaurant, and a lounge with panoramic views of the golf course.

The golf course is very popular in the area and the clubhouse was known for its good food.



Pictures show the extent of the damage, with blackened tiles and warped solar panels the only thing left of the roof.

Fire crews are currently assessing the structure as the cause of the inferno has not yet been determined.



In a statement on social media, Conwy Golf Club said: “It is with great sadness that we must share that a serious fire occurred at the clubhouse last night, resulting in significant damage to the building.

“Thankfully, no one was hurt.

“We are incredibly grateful to the emergency services for their rapid response and hard work throughout the night, and they remain on site dealing with the incident.

“At this stage, the cause is unknown and we will not be speculating while official investigations take place.

“For safety reasons, the golf course and all club facilities are currently closed.



“The emergency services have specifically requested that members, visitors, and the public do not attend the club premises under any circumstances until the site is declared safe.

“Access to the grounds and buildings is strictly prohibited.

“We know this news will come as a huge shock to our members, visitors, and the local community. Our immediate priority is safety and supporting the emergency services.

“We would like to extend a heartfelt thank you to everyone who has reached out today to offer messages of support. It means a great deal to everyone at Conwy.

“We will share further updates as soon as more information becomes available.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Thank you for your patience, understanding, and support during this difficult time for Conwy Golf Club.”

News.title: Millions in Ukraine & Russia warned ‘NUCLEAR warheads have launched’ after emergency apps hacked in ‘huge cyber attack’
News.content:
Next

TERRIFYING hoax emergency alerts warning of nuclear and chemical attacks have been sent to millions of civilians across Russia and Ukraine.

Hackers reportedly issued several bogus announcements through official warning apps and text messaging services to spread panic among the two at-war nations.



Vladimir Putin’s emergency warning system was feared to have been infiltrated by a team of hackers overnight as Russians were sent messages about incoming nuclear warheads.

The panic-inducing alerts appeared on official channels of Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry [EMERCOM] in Moscow, St Petersburg and multiple other regions.



Russians were ordered to stockpile food for three weeks and hide in their cellars – or face being “blown to bits” by bombs at around 2:45am.

Identical messages appeared on official emergency channels and the ministry’s mobile app.

There were also reports of Russians receiving the frightening alerts by SMS as alerts popped up on MAX, Russia’s state-backed messaging service.

Kyiv doesn’t possess any nuclear weapons but Ukrainian hackers are suspected of being behind the cyber attack.



Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry publicly acknowledged the chaos calling it a “massive cyber-attack”.

It claimed the country’s sirens, loudspeakers, television and radio warning systems hadn’t been compromised despite the alert system’s humiliation.

The ministry was working to restore normal service into the early hours.

The nuclear scare came just hours after a similar cyberattack breached Ukraine’s official Air Alert system.

Scared Ukrainians were warned of a radiation hazard followed by a serious incoming nuclear and chemical threat.



Four back-to-back messages read: “Radiation threat. Radiation threat declared in Kyiv.

“Don’t worry, an Oreshnik is overhead! A nuclear alert has been activated across Ukraine.

“Chemical threat. There is a threat of a chemical attack on Kyiv. Don’t go outside.



“Street fighting threat. Street fighting is taking place in Kyiv. Don’t go outside.”

The Ukrainian authorities immediately confirmed their emergency alert service had been targeted by hackers.

The system is crucial for Ukraine as it acts as the main line of defence for civilians against Putin’s drone and missile strikes.

The app is used to warn people in real time of the threat of air strikes from Russia.

People often have only minutes to find shelter with thousands often left running to underground hideouts.



Ukrainian authorities issued a statement saying the system was working normally after midnight.

Hours later, the systems were activated for real as the Kremlin ordered an attack on Odesa, injuring four people.

It comes as a top Russian propagandist claimed Putin is prepared to take a call from Volodymyr Zelensky.

One of Vlad’s key cronies, chief foreign affairs aide Yuri Ushakov, said of the despot: “I believe he would answer, of course. Putin has never once refused to engage in talks.”

Putin has declined calls from Zelensky several times – notably on the eve of the war, February 23, 2022.



On the same day, Ukraine unleashed fury on Russian oil refineries close to Moscow.

Shocking images showed a refinery engulfed in flames and covered by a mushroom cloud after the devastating strike.

A thick blanket of dark, acrid smoke can be seen drifting across the region as the blazes illuminate the sky.

A massive drone swarm targeted an “industrial enterprise” in the Nizhny Novgorod Oblast overnight, governor Gleb Nikitin said.

Ukraine has repeatedly struck Russian oil and gas sites in retaliation for Putin’s relentless attacks on its energy infrastructure.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Donald Trump has been pressuring Kyiv for weeks to stop such attacks, blaming them for the rising cost of diesel.

Elon Musk even temporarily cut satellite internet speeds for Ukrainian terminals after accusing Volodymyr Zelensky of violating Starlink’s terms of service, leaving cities vulnerable to Russian attacks.

News.title: Brit drug dealer, 38, arrested in Colombia after being on the run ‘for two years’ as cops discover hidden gun
News.content:
FUGITIVE SNARED Brit drug dealer, 38, arrested in Colombia after being on the run ‘for two years’ as cops discover hidden gun







Next

A BRIT drug dealer has been arrested in Colombia after allegedly being on the run for two years.

Leigh Elston, 38, who is wanted in the UK, was cuffed by local cops who also seized a gun and silencer he was carrying.



Police found out he was wanted in the UK after identifying him following the arrest.

He was detained near Lleras Park in the upscale El Poblado area in Medellin, Colombia’s second-largest city.



A silencer, two ammunition magazines, 24 cartridges and a gun were taken by cops as they searched his bag.

An appeal had been issued for Elston by Welsh authorities earlier this year.



Gwent Police were seeking information on his location after he allegedly breached his licence conditions and was recalled to prison.

He had previously received a prison sentence of five years and nine months for possession of drugs with intent to supply at Cardiff Crown Court in July 2020.

The convicted dealer is thought to have been on the run since 2024.

It is understood he entered Colombia via Jose Maria Cordova International Airport south-east of Medellin on January 21, 2025.



He allegedly arrived on a 90-day visa that ran out in April that year.

Officials announced an automatic fine for his visa overstay.

They then confirmed he would be deported after he failed to pay the penalty.

It is unclear whether he will face prosecution in Colombia for alleged illegal weapons possession before being extradited to the UK.

It comes after two British fugitives described as alleged members of a transnational drug trafficking gang and agents for the “Irish mafia” were arrested in Medellin last November.



The pair were later named by the National Crime Agency as Liam O’Brien, from Liverpool, and Robert Taylor, from Newcastle upon Tyne.

The NCA said at the time Taylor, 54, was wanted by Northumbria Police after he was sentenced in his absence in February 2024 to seven-and-a-half years in prison for drugs offences and money laundering.

O’Brien, 41, was accused of conspiracy to supply cocaine, heroin, MDMA and cannabis, conspiracy to possess a firearm with intent to endanger life, conspiracy to transfer a prohibited weapon as well as money laundering and perverting the course of justice.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It is still unclear whether or not they have been extradited.

News.title: Energy drinks may be behind heart attack surge among young adults, new study suggests
News.content:
Energy drinks may be behind heart attack surge among young adults, new study suggests

'It’s important for people to know that there may be a risk of cardiovascular harm with these products'

View 2 Images Reports involving energy drinks and supplements were around 4.5 times more likely to include heart attacks, according to the study

Energy drinks may be responsible for a surge in heart attacks among young adults, new research suggests. Products containing high levels of caffeine or other stimulants were associated with more reporting of cardiac arrests and heart attacks - particularly for adults aged 18 to 34, a group not usually considered at high risk.

‌



‌



American researchers found caffeinated energy drinks and stimulant supplements appeared "disproportionately" more often in official reports of serious cardiovascular events, especially among young adults.

‌



Sales of caffeinated energy drinks have more than doubled over the past decade. While research on energy drinks and other stimulant-containing supplements is limited, available evidence indicates that high doses of caffeine are associated with cardiovascular harm.

‌



Healthcare professionals have also described cases of irregular heart rhythms, known as arrhythmias, or sudden cardiac death in people who had consumed the products, many of them young adults with no known heart disease risks.

Consuming up to 400mg of caffeine per day - the equivalent of up to five regular cups of black caffeinated coffee - is generally safe for most adults, according to an American Heart Association (AHA) scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease earlier this year.

However, compared with brewed coffee, some energy drinks contain as much as three times more caffeine per fluid ounce, while some pre-workout supplements contain more than 12 times as much caffeine per fluid ounce. Study author Sai Samayamanthula said: “These products are marketed as everyday pick-me-ups and sold next to soda and bottled water, so most people assume they carry no real risk.

‌



“For many healthy people, if these products are consumed occasionally, the risk is probably small. However, individuals who consume energy drinks or other stimulant-containing supplements regularly can quickly exceed the recommended daily limit for caffeine, so it’s important for people to know that there may be a risk of cardiovascular harm with these products.”

Researchers analysed data from a government safety database to compare reports of adverse reactions related to products containing caffeine and other stimulants compared to regulated foods and dietary supplements such as soft drinks, meal replacement shakes, protein bars, smoothies and vitamins.

‌



The data included 28,345 reports from people aged 13 or older between 2017 and 2025. A total of 854 reports mentioned caffeine or stimulant-containing energy drinks or dietary supplements.

Ensure our latest health headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



Researchers compared them with 27,491 reports about products without caffeine or other stimulants. Cardiac arrest was reported around 11 times more often in connection with caffeine- and stimulant-containing products compared to products without those ingredients.

Reports involving energy drinks and supplements were around 4.5 times more likely to include heart attacks and four times more likely to include ventricular arrhythmias - abnormal rhythm in the heart’s lower pumping chambers - or heart palpitations.

‌



Similar patterns existed between consumption of caffeinated energy drinks and stimulant supplements and reports of other heart conditions, including elevated heart rate, chest pain, and fainting. Just under half (45%) of reports linking caffeine- and stimulant-containing products to cardiovascular events involved adults ages 18 to 34. Similar patterns were observed in reports involving both men and women.

The research team emphasised that the analysis’ design only identified associations between caffeinated products and cardiac events voluntarily self-reported to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and the results can't prove that the products directly caused any heart conditions or events.

‌



View 2 Images Energy drinks have skyrocketed in popularity in recent years

But Mr Samayamanthula, a fourth-year medical student at the University of Virginia School of Medicine, said: “Our findings support the case for more systematic safety monitoring of caffeine- and stimulant-containing products.

‌



"In addition, healthcare professionals should remember to ask their younger patients who have palpitations, chest pain or fainting spells if they recently or regularly consume these products."

The findings are due to be presented at a meeting of the AHA in Chicago next week. Professor Gregory Marcus, chair of the 2026 AHA scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease, said: “This study raises concerns that products with very high amounts of caffeine may be harmful to the cardiovascular system.

Article continues below

“Although there are biological reasons why that connection could be possible, the study does not prove that caffeine products cause these events, because other factors may have influenced the results found in this analysis."

Prof Marcus, who was not involved in the study, added: "More research is needed to understand whether these stimulant products are truly responsible for the reported heart-related events.”

News.title: Man, 19, charged after woman, 36, killed in 'hit-and-run' by car being chased by police
News.content:
Man, 19, charged after woman, 36, killed in 'hit-and-run' by car being chased by police

Harry Gyamsie-Perah has been charged with several offences after a pedestrian died following a collision during a police pursuit in Leeds

View Image The collision is also being investigated by the police watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC)

A 36-year-old woman has tragically died after she was hit by a car being chased by police in Leeds.

‌



A black Vauxhall Corsa collided with the pedestrian on Beckett Street on Thursday morning (October 29). The woman later died in hospital, with West Yorkshire Police saying the fatal collision took place just two minutes after the chase was given the go-ahead.

‌



Harry Gyamsie-Perah, 19, has now been charged with causing death by dangerous driving, using a motor vehicle on a road without third party insurance, failing to stop after a road accident and driving a motor vehicle otherwise than in accordance with a licence.

‌



The collision is also being investigated by the police watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

Gyamsie-Perah, of Coldcotes Garth, Leeds, appeared at Leeds Magistrates' Court on Saturday morning. He was remanded in custody and is next due to appear at Leeds Crown Court on November 27.

‌



West Yorkshire Police said the 19-year-old identifies himself as "black African including black British". A statement from the force reads: "The incident occurred at 9.52am on Beckett Street when a black Vauxhall Corsa was in collision with a 36-year-old pedestrian who later died in hospital.

"A pursuit of the Corsa had been authorised a short time before the collision and the Independent Office for Police Conduct are independently investigating the circumstances of that pursuit. At least two people are understood to have been in the vehicle at the time of the collision and detectives from the Homicide and Major Enquiry Team are urging any occupants of the vehicle to do the right thing and come forward to assist with their enquiries.

Article continues below

"Detectives are also continuing to appeal for anyone who witnessed this incident or who has any relevant dashcam footage to make contact."

News.title: Should you keep chocolate in the fridge? Lindt expert settles the debate
News.content:
Should you keep chocolate in the fridge? Lindt expert settles the debate

It's been an ongoing debate for years, and now, an expert has shared the best - and the worst - places that you can store a bar of chocolate.

View 3 Images Storing chocolate incorrectly can impact its taste and texture (Image: Nazar Rybak via Getty Images)

There's nothing quite like treating yourself to a bit of chocolate after a hard day, or as a much-needed boost when energy levels are dipping. After Halloween, you may well find yourself with lots of chocolate at home, and with the festive season just around the corner, there'll be plenty more opportunities to indulge.

‌



‌



But the question of where chocolate should actually be kept has long sparked heated debate. Some swear by storing it in the fridge, while others find the idea unthinkable.

‌



Now, a Lindt master chocolatier has stepped in to put the argument to rest once and for all - and her verdict couldn't be clearer.

‌



Miquetta de Castro said: "Chocolate is more sensitive to its environment than people often realise, and where it's kept can make a noticeable difference to how it looks and tastes. Here's where it should, and shouldn't, be stored."

View 3 Images Keep your chocolate away from the fridge (Image: Getty)

Worst place to store chocolate

Despite what many people might assume, the fridge is actually one of the worst possible places to keep your chocolate bars. While it may keep them satisfyingly cool, it's a surefire way to compromise both the flavour and texture.

‌



Miquetta explained: "The fridge is one of the worst places to store chocolate, despite how common it is. The cold, damp environment can cause bloom and dull the flavour, and taking chocolate in and out of the fridge repeatedly only makes this worse."

But that's not the only place you should steer clear of when storing your chocolate. Miquetta has also warned Brits about keeping it near any heat-emitting appliances, for obvious reasons.

‌



She explained: "Anywhere warm is a problem for chocolate, whether that's a kitchen counter near the oven, a radiator, or a windowsill that gets direct sun. Chocolate begins to soften and melt at much lower temperatures than people expect, so it needs to be kept somewhere consistently cool."

View 3 Images Chocolate kept in the cupboard will taste so much better (Image: Getty)

‌



Where should you store chocolate?

Rather than stashing it in the fridge or leaving it out on a worktop, the ideal spot for storing chocolate is in a cool, dark cupboard. The expert noted that it should ideally be kept away from direct sunlight, at a fairly steady temperature of around 16-20C.

She warned: "Sudden or frequent changes in temperature are one of the main causes of bloom, so consistency matters more than the exact spot chosen."

‌



Bear in mind, though, that the location in your cupboard you place it is equally important. You'll want to keep chocolate well away from anything with a powerful smell, such as onions, which also thrive best stored in a cool, dark environment.

Miquetta explained: "Chocolate is highly absorbent, so storing it near strong-smelling food like onions, garlic, or spices can genuinely affect its flavour over time. It's best kept somewhere separate from anything with a strong odour, even if that means a different shelf or cupboard entirely."

Article continues below

If this is something that worries you, storing your food in an airtight container or wrapper should help shield it from any unwanted odours in the surrounding area.

News.title: 'Perfect for Christmas Day dinner' new Aldi gadget similar to Dunelm out Thursday
News.content:
'Perfect for Christmas Day dinner' new Aldi gadget similar to Dunelm out Thursday

Shoppers keen to make a start on their Christmas Day preparations may be impressed by the new gadget

View 3 Images The new range will be coming out on Thursday (Image: Getty)

With November now here, many UK households will be thinking ahead to Christmas. To help people start their Christmas shopping and preparations early, Aldi is releasing a range of festive items and gadgets this week.

‌



‌



For many people, cooking a roast dinner on Christmas Day isn't easy. But one device landing in Aldi stores across the UK is designed to offer Brits a helping hand. From Thursday, November 5, customers will be able to buy the store's new Ambiano Warming Plate for £24.99.

‌



In the product description, Aldi says: "From dinner parties to everyday meals, keep food warm with ease." The silicone mat is designed to help keep food warm, from keeping side dishes heated to keeping gravy piping hot while the turkey roasts in the oven. Aldi lists the mat's key features as follows:

‌



Adjustable temperature from 40°C to 100°C with easy-to-read digital display

One to eight-hour timer for convenient use

Automatic shut-off after 8 hours

Child lock function

Water and oil resistant silicone surface

Flexible, rollable design

Includes Velcro Storage Strap

60 x 40cm warming area (approx.)

180cm power cord (approx.)

Three year warranty

View 3 Images Ambiano Warming Plate (Image: Aldi)

How can Aldi's gadget be useful at Christmas?

The gadget could be seen as a useful tool for Christmas Day because it directly solves the classic holiday problem of keeping multiple side dishes hot simultaneously. During a roast, oven space is always at a premium, as the turkey or main roast typically occupies most of the oven. By placing a warming mat on your countertop, you can take out side dishes like roast potatoes, stuffing, and pigs in blankets early and keep them piping hot without overcrowding your oven.

‌



It may also be perfect for a buffet-style dinner or for families who enjoy going back for second helpings. You can place your serving bowls and even your gravy jug directly on the mat on the dining table, ensuring the food stays steaming hot throughout the meal.

The mat also packs away neatly once the celebrations are over. Unlike traditional metal buffet warming trays, which are notoriously bulky and clutter up kitchen cupboards, the silicone mat can simply be wiped clean, rolled up into a compact shape, and tucked away.

‌

What is Dunelm's similar warming mat like?

Aldi's £24.99 Warming Mat is similar in design to Dunelm's £30 model. Shoppers can find Dunelm's Portable Roll-Up Food Warmer in stores and online for £30.

‌



Dunelm says: "Keep meals warm and ready to enjoy with the Portable Roll-Up Food Warmer. Its rollable design makes it compact, space-saving and easy to store when not in use, whilst three temperature settings let you choose the right level of heat. Complete with heat insulation, it offers a versatile temperature range from 60 to 98 degrees to suit everything from gentle warming to hotter dishes."

How is Aldi's warming mat similar to Dunelm's version?

These two food warmers are similar in their core design, size, and main purpose. Both products move away from traditional, bulky metal warming trays in favour of a modern, flexible silicone surface. This means they both offer a space-saving roll-up design that allows you to easily fold or roll them away into a drawer when you are finished using them.

‌



In terms of physical size, they are almost identical, measuring roughly 60cm by 40cm, which gives you plenty of surface area to keep multiple dishes, pots, or takeaway boxes warm at the same time. They both feature built-in heat insulation to protect your tabletop and are designed to be easily wiped clean with a damp cloth.

‌



Are there any differences?

Despite their similar appearance, there are a few key technical differences in how they operate. The Aldi Ambiano version is slightly more advanced, as it features a digital display that lets you precisely adjust the temperature between 40°C and 100°C. It also comes with extra safety features, including an adjustable one to eight-hour countdown timer, an automatic shut-off function, and a child safety lock.

On the other hand, the Dunelm version uses a simpler control system. It has three fixed temperature settings ranging from 60°C to 98°C, and it does not mention a digital screen or a built-in timer.

Opting for Aldi’s version could help shoppers save money. At a retail price of £24.99, the Aldi warmer is £5 cheaper upfront than Dunelm’s £30 model. In addition to the lower purchase price, Aldi includes a three-year warranty with the appliance. Her fiancee is urging anyone with information to come forward

News.title: Aeroplane engineer says there is 'cunning hijack plan' behind missing MH370 flight
News.content:
Aeroplane engineer says there is 'cunning hijack plan' behind missing MH370 flight

Egyptair Chief Engineer Ismail Hamad has shared what he believes to be the "cunning plan" behind the disappearance of MH370 — one of aviation's greatest unsolved mysteries

View 4 Images Relatives of passengers onboard the missing Malaysia Airlines flight MH370 met this year (Image: PEDRO PARDO, AFP via Getty Images)

An aviation expert and engineer revealed the "cunning plan" behind the most infamous aircraft disaster in history - the vanishing of flight MH370.

‌



The ill-fated Boeing 777, carrying 227 passengers and 12 crew members, disappeared on March 8, 2014, while travelling from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing.

The aircraft continues to lie at the centre of aviation's most horrific mystery and is the deadliest individual incident involving a missing aircraft.

Recent efforts by marine robotics company Ocean Infinity function on a "no find, no fee" basis, with devastated grieving relatives anxiously awaiting answers. The initial search was mounted off the Perth coastline in 2018.

Additional searches have taken place in 2025, and earlier this year, reports the Daily Star.

View 4 Images The search for missing Malaysia Airlines flight MH370 rages on (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Following the January suspension and March re-launching of the search, Ismail Hamad, Chief Engineer at Egyptair, told The Daily Star: "Had the aircraft flown toward the southern Indian Ocean using the autopilot system reliant on Inertial Reference Systems (IRS) of navigation, it would have been located during the initial search off the coast of Perth, Australia.

"This conclusion is based on a simple integration of satellite data and fuel consumption equations for the aircraft without even accounting for the other factors such as the weather conditions and the crosswinds which their effects are precisely corrected by the autopilot system and its laser gyroscope aids which are highly sensitive in determining direction and maintaining the aircraft's orientation without being affected by any external factors."

Hamad claimed there was a simple, yet horrific plan that explains the tragedy. He said: "In my opinion, the [hijakcer]'s method of vanishing with the aircraft was far more cunning in planning but simple and easy to execute. He relied for heading on the aircraft's standby magnetic compass which is a primitive in work. That makes the pilot himself uncertain of his exact landing location as a result of the impact of weather conditions and operational factors on the aircraft, not to mention the compass's inherent deviation from the Earth's magnetic north."

View 4 Images The flight vanished over a decade ago

While several conspiracy theories continue to circulate, Hamad remains firmly convinced that a "hijacker" was behind the incident, with the critical question being where the plane went down when their plot fell apart.

He explained: "If the hijacker was looking for the perfect crime that would remain a mystery for a hundred years, he would have to land on one of the abandoned airstrips or lakes in the maze of the Philippine archipelago, which consists of 7,641 islands.

"Such airstrips are spread out and end in the sea, lakes or swamps, and not fly in a straight line to fall into the waters off the city of Perth, in an area that can be predicted by calculating the rate of the fuel consumption."

Hamad added: "Whatever the pilot's experience he would not be able to fly easily and accurately in a straight line on such a long straight route, above an open area of water, at night for such long hours".

The engineer pointed out that navigating from the Malaysian coastline towards the southern Indian Ocean would indicate a crash site near Perth.

View 4 Images The plane and 239 people on board vanished from radar screens (Image: Supian Ahmad/NurPhoto/REX/Shutterstock)

He said if the pilot had GPS technology at their disposal, they could have navigated through the Philippines islands "if they knew them and their cities' lights well".

Hamad emphasised that inputting basic spatial coordinates into the autopilot computer presents considerable difficulties.

He explained: "Likewise, a pilot alone would not be able to continue flying a big aircraft like B777-200 for nine hours since take-off until vanishing, including the three hours on average it takes to check the condition of the aircraft and its documentations before the taking off according to the aviation regulations."

Hamad concluded that without autopilot systems or navigational aids, relying solely on the aircraft's magnetic compass, the search zone ought to be narrowed down to the stretch between the Malacca strait and the Perth coastline when taking into account "all those stresses".

News.title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to her dead baby
News.content:
Warning: This article contains themes and images some readers may find upsetting.

A pregnant woman whose baby had died was sent home from hospital still carrying the child and told to make an appointment later in the week to give birth.

Danielle Brown, 31, from North Tyneside, had already been wrongly discharged despite having the life-threatening condition pre-eclampsia and had returned because she was still unwell.

After insisting on returning to the maternity unit, she was finally seen and doctors discovered her baby had died. Danielle would later describe the silence, the screen turned away from her, and turning to her partner to say: "I think she's gone."

Being sent home with Danielle carrying the baby was "horrible", her partner said, "lying in bed and holding that belly" knowing their baby was not alive.

The Newcastle Hospitals NHS Trust said it fully accepted "aspects of the care we provided fell short" and offered a "heartfelt apology".

Danielle and her 34-year-old partner Anthony Miller had been delighted to learn they were having a baby girl.

"I was just over the moon, I couldn't be happier," Anthony said.

They decided to call their daughter Maisie.

But, seven months into her pregnancy in February 2023, Danielle woke up feeling unwell. Her face was swollen, as were her hands and feet - all potential signs of pre-eclampsia, external, which can be life threatening to both mother and baby.

News.title: Iran killed her teenage daughter - now she is facing up to the regime
News.content:
Sevda was killed on 9 January as she and Samira took part in huge demonstrations on the outskirts of the capital Tehran which had begun the previous month. They had been sparked by economic discontent, before escalating into calls for an end to the country's Islamic Republic.

Though Samira denies she was especially political then, she says her daughter was. Sevda's idols were two other young women - Mahsa Amini, whose death in custody after an alleged violation against the mandatory headscarf triggered mass protests, and Nika Shakarami, who was killed during a subsequent uprising against Iran's strict Islamic dress code for women.

"She kept them alive in her thoughts and always wanted to continue their path [of resistance]," Samira says.

The day before Sevda was killed, the numbers protesting had been particularly high. Samira says she and Sevda had responded to a call by Reza Pahlavi, the exiled son of Iran's last shah (king), for demonstrations.

"The security forces had lost control," she says.

The swell in numbers had spooked Iran's government, and the following day a shoot-to-kill order was announced, Samira says. But she had thought it just an empty threat.

"They lied so much in Iranâ¦ We couldn't imagine a massacre of that scale."

And they were reassured, she says, by US President Trump's promise that he had their backs.

He had told US media on 8 January: "I have let [the Iranian authorities] know that if they start killing people, which they tend to do during their riotsâ¦ we're going to hit them very hard."

But nevertheless the crowds appeared smaller on the 9th, Samira says.

Sevda seemed to know the risks, she says. Her daughter took off her earrings and gave them to her grandmother. She also shared her phone passcode with Samira.

The mother and daughter gathered with the rest of the protesters. Sevda then stood on a dustbin and began leading a chant.

"It seemed there were more forces than people," Samira says of the area where they were. "I don't know how, within one day, they gathered so manyâ¦ Basijis and IRGC [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps] forces."

The IRGC defends the country's Islamic establishment, and the paramilitary Basij Resistance Force are volunteers for the IRGC.

"A sniper fired from the roof of a building on our right. The bullet must have come from the rooftop. The bullet went through her heart. I couldn't even scream. I just stared at Sevda - her body lying lifeless. Blood was gushing out her mouth and nose. I couldn't believe it, I couldn't believe she was dying. Her eyes were still looking at me."

Samira says she managed to get Sevda to hospital and she was told they were operating on her, but then the door opened and she saw Sevda had been zipped into a body bag.

News.title: Democrats have high hopes for US midterms - but are the polls right?
News.content:
The Democratic Party has high expectations as it heads into these pivotal US midterm elections.

A historically unpopular Republican president, an American public unhappy with the rising costs of food and bills, and months of favourable polls point to a good night for them on Tuesday.

Democratic candidates lead in well over the 218 seats needed to flip control of the lower chamber of Congress, the House of Representatives, the polls suggest. And they are tied or narrowly ahead in the key Senate races.

A recent New York Times poll had the Senate race in South Carolina, a state Donald Trump won by 18 percentage points in 2024, as a tie. Recent CNN surveys put the Democrats ahead in Texas, Kansas and Maine.

But are the polls accurate?

Recent US political history is littered with examples where public opinion polls, even ones just days before an election, were off the mark. Trump outperformed predictions on his way to White House victories in 2016 and 2024. His narrow defeat in 2020 came after most surveys indicated a more comfortable win for Democrat Joe Biden.

Earlier this year, polls suggested Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was poised for a double-digit win in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. Instead it was 1%. In Wisconsin's Democratic primary for governor, the candidate that had a polling lead that approached 20 points lost by a fraction of a percent.

News.title: How 20-year-old Kimi Antonelli 'blew everyone away' to make Formula 1 history
News.content:
Just after Kimi Antonelli clinched his first title to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen were united in their assessment of the 20-year-old's achievement.

"Incredible," they both said. Coming from the two most successful champions on the current grid, the men who are first and third in the all-time list of F1 record-holders, it meant something.

That Antonelli shared the Mexico City Grand Prix podium with these two titans meant something, too.

To Antonelli, firstly, who said: "I will definitely frame the picture and put it in my house because it's just an incredible moment. And as well to see so much respect from two incredible drivers who have done the history of the sport is truly special and a moment that will live and will always be remembered."

So, too, though, for its symbolism. Antonelli seems destined to join them among the list of all-time greats of the sport, judging by the scale of his achievement this year.

"There are going to be others," said 1996 world champion Damon Hill, commentating for BBC Radio 5 live.

"I don't see anything else other than him getting better and better. He's going to have to go through hard times as well, but no one is going to doubt his incredible talent."

No one indeed. Not any more, anyway.

News.title: Lifestyle guru Martha Stewart says she 'really screwed up' with homeless Halloween costume
News.content:
Veteran lifestyle guru Martha Stewart has admitted she "really screwed up" by dressing as a homeless person for Halloween.

The 85-year-old US entrepreneur and personality has deleted a photo of herself wearing torn clothes and dirt on her face, holding a sign saying: "I am hungry help me!!"

She posted a statement on Sunday saying she was "distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention".

That was followed by a fuller apology. "It's hard to admit when you've really screwed up. My earlier statement didn't go far enough. I know many people are suffering economically. Wearing a costume like I did was insensitive and not funny. I am very sorry."

Stewart had captioned her original Instagram photo: "My QVC candles are perfect for Halloween!!!"

The post received a swift and sharp backlash.

"This sartorial take on a homeless person is a lot. Insulting? Demeaning? Confusing? All of the above," PR expert Molly McPherson wrote, external.

One person wrote on social media: "Why in the hell would you even think about wearing that as a costume?"

Another said: "Why would she do that? Who did she think would find that funny? Billionaires?"

Arguably the original lifestyle influencer, Stewart started a catering business in the 1970s and rose to fame in the 1990s when she started her own magazine, Martha Stewart Living.

She later became a billionaire, albeit briefly, when her media empire Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia was floated on the stock market in 1999.

But in 2004 she was sentenced to five months in prison after she was found guilty on a number of charges related to an insider trading scandal.

She has since attempted to rebuild her brand, starring in her own reality television show, expanding her food products and teaming up with rapper and friend Snoop Dogg for a television series.

In 2015, she sold Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia for more than $350m (Â£220m).

News.title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E
News.content:
A similar "early warning" system to identify acutely ill adults, including those with sepsis, is already in use in emergency and general NHS hospital wards.

More than 90 hospitals across England have been using the alert system in children's wards, with different age-appropriate assessments available for babies through to teenagers.

The NHS has already said it will expand Martha's Rule to all hospital emergency departments in England. The rule gives patients, families and carers the right to request a rapid review if they are worried that a patient's condition is getting worse and their concerns are not being responded to.

The initiative is named after Martha Mills, who died aged 13 in 2021 after developing blood poisoning, or sepsis, in hospital following a bike accident.

A coroner ruled that her family's concerns about her worsening condition were not listened to and she would probably have survived had she been moved to intensive care earlier.

Martha's parents Merope and Paul came up with the idea of the rule in a bid to change the culture that contributed to her death.

A&E units will have a dedicated phone number that can be called to trigger an urgent review of a patient's care.

Duncan Burton, chief nursing officer for England, said the new early warning system for children in emergency departments was an "important next step in improving care for children and young people across England for this winter - and beyond".

He added: "In fast-paced emergency departments, staff need to spot quickly when a child's condition is deteriorating.

"This standardised approach will help them recognise the warning signs, communicate concerns, and make timely decisions when every moment matters."

The early warning system for children, PEWS, is a collaboration between NHS England and the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health and the Royal College of Nursing.

News.title: King to address slavery in Antigua as PM says he is open to possible UK apology
News.content:
King Charles III is to speak with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" on the lasting pain of the transatlantic slave trade during the final leg of his Caribbean tour in Antigua, Buckingham Palace has said.

The King will address Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday in a speech that will touch on the issue.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham earlier wrote in the Guardian, external that he was "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in slavery - a change in the government's stance.

It is understood the Palace was told in advance of Burnham's comments in an opinion piece on Friday night, and that the King has not made any changes to his speech in light of them.

The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations.

Burnham has previously stuck with the policy of his predecessors and stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments.

In an address to the nation to mark Antigua and Barbuda's independence day, Prime Minister Gaston Browne said the history of slavery was painful and "its consequences have not disappeared with the passage of time".

He said the country's pursuit of reparatory justice deserved "seriousness, sensitivity and sustained international engagement".

Browne went on to say that his government was having these conversations in bilateral discussions with the UK and other Commonwealth countries at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described "endless talk about apologies" as a "distraction" from solving current problems.

She told BBC Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "The transatlantic slave trade happened centuries ago. It is time for the Commonwealth to start looking forwards, not endlessly backwards."

The King will make his speech at the CHOGM.

He "will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit", a Palace spokesperson said.

"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond."

When asked about the King's reaction to the prime minister's comments, the spokesperson said it would "not be appropriate" for the King to address matters of policy relating to the government's position.

The Caribbean tour has again thrust the King into the difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.

On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech in which he spoke of the "suffering of the past".

In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion, where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.

Buckingham Palace said it was a moment for the King to learn more about the history of slavery and resistance. His engagements have also covered the environment, opportunities for young people and trade relationships with the UK.

News.title: Virgin Media O2 set to cut thousands of jobs to reduce costs
News.content:
Thousands of Virgin Media O2 staff are facing redundancy as the telecoms firm attempts to save money in the face of billions of pounds of debt and tougher competition.

The broadband provider has not finalised the number of roles to be cut but it is likely be a sizeable chunk of its 16,000-strong workforce, the BBC understands.

Virgin Media O2 has billions in debt on its balance sheet and is tackling both smaller providers as well as giants like BT, which has agreed a deal to acquire rival TalkTalk, which Virgin Media O2 has firmly opposed.

The company declined to comment. Prospect, a union which represents Virgin Media O2 staff, said the cuts were "disappointing and very unsettling".

Noel McClean. deputy general secretary at Prospect, said the union was "committed to supporting our members through what is a difficult time, as well as also working with employers to explore ways to mitigate the number of redundancies and ensure retraining and redeployment of staff affected".

The majority of the affected staff are in roles that are not customer-facing and a number of senior leadership changes are already under way, the BBC has been told.

Virgin Media O2 is also expected to review its use of contractors and suppliers in conjunction with the job cuts.

As of 30 June, Virgin Media O2's total liabilities stands at Â£27.2bn while it holds assets worth Â£45.9bn, according to the firm's latest accounts.

Meanwhile, the company is dealing with fierce competition from cheaper "altnets" like Hyperoptic, Community Fibre, Gigaclear and YouFibre.

Virgin Media O2 had attempted to respond to this growing threat by buying altnet competitor Netomnia for Â£2bn via nexfibre, a joint venture owned by Virgin Media O2's owners.

However, the Competition Markets Authority (CMA) has provisionally found competition concerns in the deal, external, with a final decision to come in December, sparking anger from Virgin Media O2.

News.title: Henry Nowak's family tell of trauma of seeing son handcuffed as he lay dying
News.content:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced an independent review into the murder, led by former lord chancellor Alex Chalk, which will look at "any missed opportunities to intervene".

Henry, 18, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, was a first-year accountancy and finance student at the University of Southampton when he was murdered.

He was stabbed five times as he walked home from a night out with friends from his football team in Southampton on 3 December 2025.

Digwa, 23, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years.

It took officers another 24 hours to identify Henry's body and tell his family.

"I jumped out of bed and I saw the police car on our driveway," said Katie.

"One of the police officers was holding his hat in his hand, and I just knew straight away that something horrific had happened."

She said Mark fell to his knees when he heard the news.

"He let out a cry that I'll never forget," she said.

"I just remember saying 'it's Henry' and breaking down in tears," Mark said. "It's just unbelievable pain."

News.title: Karl Bushby 'overwhelmed' at Humber Bridge welcome
News.content:
British adventurer Karl Bushby crossed the Humber Bridge through thick mist on the final leg of his 31,000-mile (49,890 km), 28-year trek from South America to Hull.

Bushby left Chile in 1998 to head home to the UK without breaking two self-imposed rules: not to return until he had fully completed his feat - and not to use transport to advance.

The adventurer said he was "absolutely overwhelmed" by the crowds who lined the bridge.

Bushby, a former paratrooper, is due to complete the challenge on Monday and will be met by his mother, his son and granddaughter when he arrives in Hull.

News.title: Reeves says UK's future should be inside the EU
News.content:
Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK's future should be inside the EU, and that Brexit has made the country "poorer, weaker and less secure".

In her first major intervention since leaving the Treasury, Reeves said she welcomed debate around the UK's relationship with Europe.

At the last election, Labour's manifesto said a Labour government would stay outside the EU and make Brexit work.

But Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there needs to be an honest discussion about what the future relationship looks like.

The Conservatives have said there is no desire to rerun the Brexit debate and Reform UK's Nigel Farage has said there is no mandate to pursue closer EU ties.

Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

Burnham has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, which is next due by 2029.

In the Sunday Times, external, Reeves wrote: "No-one in the Treasury ever doubted where my instincts were. I do believe Britain's future lies in the European Union."

She said supporters of rejoining the EU had to "make the argument, demonstrate tangible benefits and to get the next steps right".

Reeves added that at the forthcoming UK-EU summit, she hoped for confirmation of the youth mobility scheme she has been pushing for since she was in office.

She also said she was hoping for "progress towards entry" into the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) scheme.

Announced last March, SAFE is part of an EU-wide effort to rearm after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

A defence pact agreed with the EU last May paved the way for UK-based defence companies to be part of projects funded by SAFE.

In her piece for the Sunday Times, Reeves also sought to defend her record in office.

She wrote about the need for governments to be "braver" in building big infrastructure projects and "clear eyed" about the risks and benefits AI would drive in advanced economies.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said she "can't even believe we are reopening" the Brexit debate.

She told BBC One's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "This is not something that is needed in order to cut welfare, in order to spend money on defence.

"We are having yet another Westminster bubble argument about the EU when it is time for us to actually start using the opportunities, fix mistakes that have been made and go into the future."

Badenoch added: "I do not want to indulge Andy Burnham's fantasies about redoing the referendum because he doesn't have a plan for what to do today."

Burnham told Badenoch during the most recent session of Prime Minister's Questions that he was focused on "getting a better deal for Britain, that is my responsibility".

The next UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November.

News.title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain
News.content:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is expected to announce her final decision on immigration rules for legal migrants next week.

She had proposed to extend the wait for permanent settlement from the current five years to 10 with some lower-paid migrants facing a 15-year wait. The BBC understands the proposals are likely to be revised for most of those currently working in social care.

The home secretary was concerned about the number of people who would be eligible for permanent residency after a period of very high net migration under the previous government.

Mahmood has faced opposition from within the government for proposing to impose new rules on migrant workers already in the UK.

Before she rejoined the cabinet, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner described the proposals as "un-British" because they sought to change the rules for people who had come to the UK in good faith.

In particular, many lower-paid social care workers were facing a wait of up to 15 years rather than five.

But the BBC understands that social care workers already in the UK are now likely to be exempt from the longer wait.

But as originally proposed, it is likely most other workers will have to live and work in the UK for 10 years before being eligible for permanent settlement. That can be reduced if they contribute to their local communities or have higher incomes.

The government's consultation on the proposed reforms has drawn 200,000 responses.

The Home Office will not comment on Mahmood's final decisions until they are presented to Parliament in the coming week.

In September, a Conservative spokesperson said: "Shabana Mahmood has caved in to pressure from Angela Rayner and her open borders MPs and will shred her own plans to reform indefinite leave to remain."

"This is a slap in the face to British taxpayers who will have to subsidise low-skilled, low wage migrants."

Permanent residence, or indefinite leave to remain, gives a person the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like and apply for benefits if they are eligible.

News.title: Bonnie Tyler Christmas single to be released as husband says he misses her every day
News.content:
Tyler was born in a Neath council house where she grew up with a love of music before being discovered by talent scout Roger Bell in a Swansea club.

After finding fame she was dubbed "the female Rod Stewart" for her husky vocals, and launched a career that spanned 50 years.

In August, fans travelled to Swansea to line the streets as a celebration of life service was held for Tyler at Swansea Minster.

"The only time she ever had off was during Covid, and even then she was still on Zoom doing interviews all the time," said Sullivan.

"Between live shows she would stop by David Mackay's studio to work on all these new songs.

"I know she would want people to hear them, and I am so proud of everything she left behind."

After her last record contract expired, Tyler began self-releasing songs, with Yes I Can released on New Year's Day 2025, and then Only Love in March 2026, shortly before she became unwell.

News.title: The new UK university rules coming into force this month
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Students from overseas looking to study at a UK university will have to prove they have enough money to cover living costs for each month of their course.

From 30 November, the UK Home Office is increasing the financial maintenance requirement for international students applying under the student visa route.

Applicants studying in or outside London will now need to show they have higher funds to cover their living costs in the UK.

Here, the Independent breaks down what these rules mean for international students:

From 30 November, the UK Home Office is increasing the financial maintenance requirement for international students applying under the Student visa route ( Getty/iStock )

What is changing for international students?

Students will have to prove they have more than £360 extra to study per year in London under the new rules.

Currently students studying in London need to show they have £1,529 for each month of their course, up to a maximum of nine months.

But from 30 November this figure will rise to £1,570 — that’s an increase of £369 for the year.

For a course lasting nine months or longer, the maximum amount will therefore increase from £13,761 to £14,130.

Students studying outside London currently need £1,171 per month.

This will increase to £1,203 per month, bringing the maximum nine-month requirement from £10,539 to £10,827 — which is £288 extra.

Are these funds separate from course fees?

The maintenance requirement funds are separate to course fees, which must be held in addition to this cost.

Immigration lawyers at Morgan Smith highlight that the student visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge are also separate costs.

Students should account for each of these expenses when calculating the overall cost of studying in the UK.

Applications submitted on or after 30 November will need to show they can afford the higher amount.

How can students meet the new requirement?

Students will need to provide evidence that they have enough maintenance money combined with tuition fees for one academic year and that must be held for at least 28 consecutive days before applying.

The final day of this period must be within 31 days of the date the Student visa application is submitted.

The money can be held in the student’s own account or in a parent’s account or students can rely on a student loan or official financial sponsorship.

Those who have been living in the UK with valid immigration permission for at least a year on the date of their application do not normally need to prove that they meet the financial requirement.

News.title: Karl Bushby: Man who spent 28 years walking the globe given hero’s welcome as he completes quest in Hull
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A British man who has been circumnavigating the globe on foot since 1998 has arrived back in his home town of Hull after crossing the Humber Bridge through thick mist.

Karl Bushby, from Hull, who started his epic journey in Chile 28 years ago, was “overwhelmed” by the crowds who lined the bridge on the final leg of his 31,000-mile (49,890 km) journey.

"[I'm] just absolutely overwhelmed," he said on Sunday when he spoke to BBC Radio Humberside.

"And we're not even home yet,” he said referring to himself and his cart, called The Beast, which Mr Bushby has been pushing for 28 years.

"This is my Wilson," he said, a reference to a volleyball that Tom Hanks's character talked to in the film Cast Away.

open image in gallery Mr Bushby started his epic journey in Chile 28 years ago ( Getty )

"I'm just a homeless guy pushing a shopping trolley, and the next thing you know is this," he said, pointing to the crowds lining the bridge.

He told the broadcaster the bridge is “almost symbolic” and has always been an “iconic landmark” in his eyes.

The 57-year-old former paratrooper has travelled through 29 countries, self-imposed rules that meant he did not use any transport and could not return home until he had completed the challenge.

He has trekked across the Darién Gap as fighting raged between the Colombian government and Marxist guerrillas, made the first ever recorded crossing of the Bering Strait on foot from east to west and became the first person to swim 184 miles across the Caspian Sea. He crossed into Europe last year and arrived at the English Channel last month.

Mr Bushby is due to complete the challenge on Monday and will be met by his mother, his son and granddaughter when he arrives in Hull.

open image in gallery The former paratrooper has travelled a total of 50,000km through 29 countries ( Getty )

Mr Bushby swam the English Channel and walked onto Shakespeare beach, south of Dover on Monday afternoon 5 October. But he initially wanted to walk along the Channel Tunnel rather than swim to Dover, however, his request was denied due to safety concerns and maintenance work.

But even getting permission for the swim across the Channel proved difficult. That’s because the French only allow cross-channel swims to depart from the UK and not from France.

Mr Bushby had to secure special permission from the French government and co-ordinated with both French and UK coastguards and did not publicise exactly when it would take place for security reasons.

After 20 hours in the water and three days at sea battling strong winds, Mr Bushby finally made it home and was welcomed to shore by his father, brothers and some friends.

"[It] feels good to have UK soil under my feet after all these years,” he told ITV news.

"It hasn’t been easy, and that’s part of the point - proving I’m more capable than I give myself credit for. All of us can accomplish more than we will ever imagine,” he added.

open image in gallery Mr Bushby only expected the journey to take 12 years when he set off in 1998 ( Getty )

Throughout his journey he was hit by visa restrictions, the 2008 financial crash which cost him his sponsors, the Covid-19 pandemic causing multiple lockdowns and geopolitical uncertainty.

The adventurer’s incredible world hike, officially titled Goliath Expedition, followed his 12 years in the army. The question of how far one could go stretched into “this ridiculous line all the way from the UK down to the bottom of South America”, he told The Times.

He left his mothers house 28 years ago and expected the journey to only take 12 years, now his journey is almost over.

Which Vodafone deal is best for you?

More than 240 banks owned by Lloyds Banking Group are facing closures between May 2026 and March 2027, as more customers move online.

Lloyds Banking Group, which also owns Halifax and Bank of Scotland, will be closing 17 branches — nine Lloyds banks and eight Hallifax branches — moving away from in-person services as more customers use online banking.

It comes as the banking group closed 23 branches in October, in Birmingham, Nottingham and Southampton. It’s also closed three Halifax branches. Over the summer 95 branches were closed across its high street network.

Lloyds Banking Group said on its website: “When making changes to our branch network, we always look to understand the impact on our customers – including how they continue to access banking services.

“Because of this, we may sometimes have a Community Banker visit the area after the branch closes. Or as part of an independent review a Banking Hub or Deposit Service may be set up in a nearby location.

“We follow Financial Conduct Authority guidance when announcing closures.”
