News.title: What the tax-free income allowance rise means for you
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The amount side-hustlers can earn without paying tax is set to rise by £2,000, giving a boost to Vinted and eBay sellers.

About 1.4 million people who make extra cash from reselling clothes, offering dog-walking services and tutoring could benefit from the change, which was announced in the Budget.

Side-hustle culture has seen a boom in recent years as households are faced with rising bills and food costs.

Last year, 2.6 million people made money selling items on eBay, Vinted and Etsy, according to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) — but in 2024 that figure was just 450,000.

However, there is a limit on how much money side-hustlers can make before paying tax.

open image in gallery Side-hustlers can earn £2,000 more without paying tax ( Getty/iStock )

What tax rules have changed?

The chancellor, John Healey, announced in the budget that the amount Britons can earn from a side hustle without paying tax would rise from £1,000 to £3,000 in April 2027.

Last year rules came into force requiring platforms, such as eBay, to inform HMRC about how much their sellers made. HMRC now has data on sellers who made more than 30 sales or £1,700 (€2,000) on any platform over the past year.

How much do you need to make to start paying tax?

From April, anyone who earns more than £3,000 in a tax year from making or buying things to sell for a profit, as well as any other side hustles, will need to inform HMRC. The tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April.

This is the amount earned before factoring in expenses, not just the profit.

According to HMRC, side-hustlers may have to pay tax if their total income, including their main job, is above the basic personal allowance of £12,570.

Currently those who have earned £1,000 or less from their side-job do not need to inform HMRC and from April those who earn £3,000 or less will not need to let them know.

open image in gallery HMRC now has data on sellers who made more than 30 sales in the past year ( Getty/iStock )

Invest at least £100 in Stocks or ETFs of your choice. Get fractional shares worth £50! Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

Invest at least £100 in Stocks or ETFs of your choice. Get fractional shares worth £50! Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

How do you inform HMRC?

To inform HMRC of any side-hustles, sellers will need to register for Self Assessment as a sole trader.

That’s because HMRC likely classifies these side hustles as “trading”.

Traders need to register by October 5.

What is classed as selling for a profit?

Buying items at a cheaper price from a car boot sale or charity shop with the intention of selling the item for more money, would be classed as selling for a profit by HMRC.

Other examples include upcycling second-hand furniture, buying wholesale bundles of vintage clothing and reselling them individually online.

HMRC also gave the example of selling downloadable art prints or bespoke pet portraits.

Anyone earning more than £3,000 on selling these items would need to inform HMRC.

What do you not pay tax on?

Although upcycling and reselling in bulk is classed as selling for profit, selling unwanted belongings like clothes or old toys is not and you don’t usually need to tell HMRC.

HMRC only needs to know about it if a single item sells for more than £6,000 and most old clothes, shoes and toys are not worth anywhere near this figure.

How do you know if it’s a hobby or a side hustle?

A side hustle is a way of earning extra money outside your main job, usually on a self-employed or freelance basis.

It’s different from a second job. Working for an employer, such as in a bar or shop, is usually be paid through PAYE, with tax deducted automatically. With a side hustle, people are generally responsible for declaring any taxable income themselves.

A side-hustle has grown bigger than being just a hobby if a seller is making more than £1,000 a year according to HMRC. But in April this figure will increase to £3,000.

News.title: Meet the woman who can teach you to write the ‘perfect’ letter – and change your life
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A letter lives beyond us, outside of time and space; it’s like a time capsule.” This is one of multiple pearls of wisdom I furtively note down mid-conversation with Frish Brandt, a self-titled “letter midwife” and author of a new book, Unfinished Business: How to Write the Five Essential Letters of Your Life.

What, you may well ask, is a letter midwife? “Someone who helps you give birth to your letter, helps you find the words, find the shape – because the truth is many of us are reluctant to put our thoughts on paper and to share them with someone else,” explains Brandt.

A teacher of essential letter writing at Stanford University’s School of Medicine, and to individuals and institutions around the world, she first developed her practice while working in hospices and palliative care. It was here that the unparalleled power of letter writing first became apparent; so many of her clients had things they wanted to say before the end, whether it be an “I’m sorry” or “I miss you”, “Thank you” or “I love you”. Specifically in end-of-life care, the message was often “Goodbye”. Letters felt like the natural medium for this process of letting things go, making things right and tying up loose ends.

Brandt’s book is a practical and sensitive guide, giving helpful prompts for each type of letter – though they often end up morphing from one to another, “I’m sorry” naturally evolving into “I miss you”, for example – and outlining how to structure them while accessing your own unique voice.

The aim is to be authentic, rather than slick. “This is not about writing a perfect letter; this is about writing your letter,” emphasises Brandt. For those who struggle with the form, she suggests finding a quote, poem or song lyric as a way in, or recording a voice memo stream of consciousness detailing what you want to say first.

open image in gallery Message received: writing a letter is a world away from sending a WhatsApp ( Getty/iStock )

Is using AI cheating? “You can use AI as a thought partner – it’s great for looking for quotes.” But writing a letter involves exercising a specific intellectual and emotional muscle that using AI completely bypasses, says Brandt: “You can’t just watch a fitness YouTube video and get fit. You can’t watch a cooking show and taste the food. You have to do the work.”

A letter is completely distinct from other forms of communication – the way it endures, forever preserving a moment, a feeling, a relationship, in amber. Unlike our myriad modern digital comms, “letters linger”, says Brandt.

I remember flicking through albums of memories with my granny towards the end of her life: photos from different eras alongside, much more compellingly, letters from my late grandad. Whenever he went away for work, he would write to her – missives that were mainly practical but always included a line of affection hidden among the logistics. Physical proof of a marriage underpinned by quiet devotion and abiding love, decades after the fact.

Modern life has given us a multitude of mediums through which to talk, but they have none of the sticking power or gravitas of a letter. WhatsApp, emails, social media DMs – all offer a quick dopamine hit but no real substance. “It’s like the difference between fast food and nutritious food,” says Brandt. “A meal made with kindness and intention and shared with friends is just… different.”

This is not about writing a perfect letter; this is about writing your letter

Think about the last time you received a letter – a genuine, heartfelt piece of mail from a loved one – and the distinction rings true. The feeling of excitement it evokes, the capacity to move us, the realisation that somebody cared enough to source pen and paper, sit down, arrange their scrambled thoughts – heck, even pay for a stamp and go to the trouble of finding a letter box – is a world away from someone pinging over an emoji. “It’s really about love,” says Brandt.

It is also the perfect antidote to loneliness, the current stats on which are bleak. People feel more disconnected than ever; according to the ONS’s public opinions and social trends survey in January, almost a quarter (23 per cent) of adults reported feeling lonely often, always or some of the time. Young people are particularly susceptible, with the AXA Mind Health Report finding that Brits under the age of 34 were twice as likely to experience loneliness as the over 55s.

Brandt has time and time again witnessed the transformative power of the written word, and its capacity to foster connection in ways that previously seemed impossible.

open image in gallery A letter is 'about love', according to Frish Brandt ( Getty/iStock )

She tells me about a dying woman whose dearest wish was to reconcile with her estranged parents. They had previously ignored the woman’s every attempt to make contact, including a surprise visit to their New York home at Christmastime.

A letter was the last-chance saloon. “She heard about my work and asked me to help her write to them,” says Brandt. “By chance, I was travelling to New York a few weeks later and asked if I could deliver it for her.” Forty minutes later, the woman received a loving email from her parents; it was, she said, the happiest day of her life.

Even if they hadn’t responded, the letter had already worked its own internal miracle. “She told me that just by writing it, she felt complete,” recalls Brandt. “She had said what she wanted to say.”

In fact, that’s a common theme in the book: we might initially think that a letter is for the recipient, and it is, “but by engaging in this process, we have just experienced the secret truth that the letter is, in fact, first for us, the letter writer,” Brandt concludes.

The book, she’s keen to stress, is just as much for the living as for the dying – and you shouldn’t wait till the end is nigh to share what’s important with those who mean the most (least of all because we may not be given the luxury of time for final words if we pass suddenly and unexpectedly).

The letter is, in fact, first for us, the letter writer

“There’s no time like the present – and there’s no present like a letter,” as Brandt puts it. In fact, just a few minutes into our chat, she asks if I have anyone in mind to write to. Flustered, I garble about having to think about it.

In response, she gently prompts me: “The way the game goes is, you’re on a plane with severe turbulence or you’re crossing the street and a taxi comes really close to you and you think, ‘Oh God, why didn’t I tell my mother/my brother/my friend/my uncle that I really love them, or I’m really sorry about that thing? That’s the essence of it.”

The game works – someone does pop into my head, a good friend who I let down earlier this year by not being present during a dark time. The shame I felt slowly ballooned as the months passed until it became simply too big to address. I left it too long to acknowledge my behaviour in the “normal” fashion – a paltry text feeling far too lightweight to convey the depth of feeling that’s accumulated by this point. A letter, though – that feels intentional, vulnerable enough, to perforate my shame balloon.

I feel a spark of childlike glee as I buy letter-writing paper, read Brandt’s chapter on apologies for inspiration, and set about inking my thoughts quick-sharp before I have time to second-guess myself. I try not to overthink it; I aim for honesty over excuses. Reading back, it’s not a perfect letter – but it is my letter.

There’s a lightness after I’ve finished. Brandt is right – as much as the letter is for my friend, the process was equally transformative for me. It’s as if I’ve finally put down a boulder I just spent the last six months needlessly yanking around after me. It makes me start thinking about other people I could write to: people I’ve lost touch with, acquaintances whose acts of kindness deserved a thank you, loved ones to whom I rarely explicitly express that love.

But before all of them, it’s only right that my second letter is to the letter midwife herself: a quick thank you, for quite possibly changing my life for the better.

‘Unfinished Business: How to Write the Five Essential Letters of Your Life’ by Frish Brandt is published by Particular Books on 27 October 2026 at £20.

News.title: Arsenal nous frustrates Liverpool as 14-year Anfield hoodoo ends with statement win
News.content:
It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

News.title: Tears flow for Antonelli after becoming youngest champion in F1 history
News.content:
Welcome to our coverage for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. Today could be the day for Kimi Antonelli, the day he becomes a Formula One world champion. In fact it is very likely. All he needs to confirm the drivers’ championship is to finish ninth or higher. If George Russell or Lewis Hamilton do not claim victory then he is champion whatever happens. Given his season so far, it is difficult to see the title fight going to Brazil next week.

What chance of a decent race here today? The first few laps are often entertaining as the pack bunches up and there are plenty of chances to overtake early on. Generally the top four teams have been close together (last week in Austin excluded) and it is possible to overtake here, though it is not exactly easy.

Qualifying yesterday as an intriguing and close session. Hamilton secured his first grand prix pole for Ferrari, by just 0.009sec from the Mercedes of George Russell, with Charles Leclerc of Ferrari a little behind him in third. Then came Max Verstappen, Antonelli, Norris, Hadjar and Lindblad. Liam Lawson was disqualified on a technicality.

Ferrari have been an up-and-down team this season but have been strong without really delivering on it fully in the last few rounds. Could they secure a third victory of the season today? They do not really need to worry about losing second in the constructors to Red Bull or McLaren and Mercedes are too far out of reach in any case.

In any case, the biggest story is likely to be Antonelli’s coronation in Mexico. Hamilton has won titles here before for Mercedes, will the Italian give the Silver Arrows another fiesta in Mexico City? The race starts at 8pm GMT and we will be here for all the build-up, live updates and reaction from it.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton becomes oldest driver to claim pole position in 44 years
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, obviously. The big story this weekend is that Jimi Antonelli is almost certain to become the youngest world champion in Formula One history. To guarantee it he needs just two points, but if George Russell or Lewis Hamilton fail to win here then the title is his whatever he does. It has been a superb, strong and consistent season from the man who began the year as a teenager. He has not quite been faultless, but he has not been far away.

There are other stories floating around the paddock, too. Notably, Esteban Ocon has been dropped by Haas today for final practice, qualifying and the race, to be replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the weekend. Whether Ocon will continue in any other races has yet to be confirmed but you have to say that it seems extremely unlikely. More on that later.

Another line is the ongoing tension between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen after their crash in FP2 yesterday. It was certainly a strange one in which neither driver backed down, which resulted in contact, debris being strewn across the track and a red flag. Both drivers seemed unrepentant, though admitted it was clumsy. Lawson and Verstappen each receive a one-place grid penalty for the incident, which feels about right given how silly and unnecessary it all was.

But what about the competitive order on track? Since the summer break, and a little before in fairness, things have been unpredictable at the top. Mercedes have still, on average, been the best team but Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren have all had their moments.

What happened in final practice? It was Lando Norris who topped the timesheets by just 0.001sec ahead of Mercedes’ Antonelli. Charles Leclerc was a further tenth or so back for Ferrari followed by Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren, who was 0.195sec off his team-mate’s pace. Then came Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Isack Hadjar, Lawson and Arvid Lindblad. All drivers were within 0.6sec off Norris, which promises a close qualifying session. Let’s hope we get it.

News.title: Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points
News.content:
Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

News.title: Alex Mitchell injury blow for England but Northampton dig deep to win
News.content:
England were dealt a fresh blow ahead of their Nations Championship opener with Australia after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off early in Northampton’s victory over Gloucester.

Mitchell left the field gingerly 20 minutes into the action after picking up a suspected hamstring injury following an innocuous coming-together with Gloucester winger Will Joseph.

The Saints scrum-half has suffered a series of hamstring issues this year – this would be a fourth time he has picked up a problem – and he looked visibly disappointed as he limped off.

He suffered a left leg hamstring tear during England’s Six Nations defeat to Ireland which left him sidelined for two months and, in a cruel twist of fate, sustained another on his right leg during an England three-day training camp in Bagshot last May. He suffered the injury for a third time in England’s 73-8 rout of Fiji in July.

With Mitchell’s club-mate, Archie McParland, nursing an unspecified knock that forced him to miss Saints’ high-stakes clash with Gloucester, Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies next Sunday. McParland was the third-choice scrum-half in England’s Nations Championship squad, but Steve Borthwick may be forced to look elsewhere if Mitchell’s prognosis is serious.

News.title: Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

News.title: Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City
News.content:
This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

News.title: Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick
News.content:
The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham soars to incredible Real Madrid milestone as England star leaves Zinedine Zidane trailing in his wake
Sports.content:
Next

JUDE BELLINGHAM reached another Real Madrid goalscoring milestone at the weekend.

The 23-year-old netted his 50th goal for Los Blancos against Racing Santander on Sunday.



He achieved the feat in his 154th match, beating Real Madrid icon Zinedine Zidane to the tally.

The Frenchman, who spent five years at the Bernabeu at the end of his career, scored 49 goals for the LaLiga giants in 227 appearances.



It means Bellingham reached the half-century mark in 73 fewer games.

The England international joined Real Madrid in a huge £115million transfer from Borussia Dortmund in 2023 and has won five major trophies.



He was one of three scorers against Racing Santander on Sunday.

Kylian Mbappe broke the deadlock from the penalty spot in the 11th minute before Bellingham netted the second shortly after.

Yan Diomande then made it three in the 36th minute as Los Blancos cruised to a 3-0 win.

Speaking after the match, Bellingham said: “We played very well. It was very important to win after the victory at Camp Nou, so we are very happy.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Reaching 50 goals with Real Madrid is very special. Not only for me and my dreams but also for the team.

“It’s very important for all players to score goals and make a difference in games. Sometimes it will be Mbappe, Vini Jr, Arda Güler, or me.

“But the important thing is that everyone helps the team. That’s the most important thing.”

Sports.title: Man Utd are entering a new era of player power with Michael Carrick a dead man walking despite support of fans
Sports.content:
Next

WHETHER Manchester United were playing Chelsea or Cheltenham or Chatham Town on Saturday, they needed a new face in the dugout.

United have not experienced a doom loop like this since 1984 and have come full circle again. Michael Carrick, like his old colleague and friend Ole Gunnar Solskjaer five years ago, is a dead man walking allowed to limp on for a few more days or weeks.



With Solskjaer, United matchgoers resorted to turning on a club legend to force his dismissal. When the 1999 Treble hero approached the away end at Watford after a 4-1 humbling in November 2021, he was specifically and loudly booed.

In front of the Sir Elton John Stand, Solskjaer was just about still standing. The following morning, he filmed a tearful exit interview at Carrington.



United supporters would rather not stoop to such a level. Hence why they are singing Carrick’s name almost as regularly as when his chant took off at Loftus Road in February 2013, back when United were homing in on a 20th title.

The lyrics “It’s Carrick, you know, it’s hard to believe it’s not Scholes” could now be interpreted as a reference to Scholes’ 31-day go at management with Oldham Athletic.



Carrick’s song was aired at full-time against Chelsea, another 2-0 loss with ten men and a ninth game without a win for United. Few followings would put their hands together for the manager, never mind bellow his name.

One friend in the Shed End at Stamford Bridge abstained from the happy clapping. He did not sing and did not boo. There will have been others like him.

If Carrick was subjected to the angry soundtrack that the United players were at full-time against Bournemouth eight days ago, would he still be in charge? It is doubtful.

This is absolutely not a pop at United’s away following, by a distance the best in the country. Their support was noted by the club’s X account as it clutched at a straw on Saturday.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The detached hierarchy are responsible for this farce and Saturday was another reason why they are not fit for purpose. They are conflating supporting with backing. No right-minded United matchgoer believes Carrick should stay.

United supporters should not have to round on a former playing great to force him from office and this is more evidence that the decision-makers lack knowledge of United matters.

Director of football Jason Wilcox spoke to Solskjaer about a potential return in January. If Wilcox spoke to a matchgoer or a journalist, he would have quickly known that Solskjaer is a manager and not a head coach, the title Ineos insist on as part of their dogmatic structure.

Wilcox should have known that Solskjaer left the coaching to Carrick and Kieran McKenna during his stint at United between 2018-21. Perhaps that was how the process played out and resulted in Wilcox plumping for Carrick.

Carrick’s position became more untenable when the teamsheets were printed at Chelsea, with the inevitable confirmation that Bruno Fernandes would start.



Fernandes was dropped against Bournemouth and did not come on when he should have at half-time with United 2-0 down. It was a “pure football” decision and he was fit. Then Fernandes reported at Carrington the next day – a day off – for treatment.

Deep down, Carrick maybe thought he would never have to pick Fernandes again. Only United’s power brokers then demonstrated the most remarkable loss of nerve witnessed in top-tier football and afforded Carrick another stay of execution.

So Fernandes was back in the team against Chelsea and back in his preferred position, with Youri Tielemans dropped for the first time. The manager needs the players more than the players need him.



The list of probable wantaways is growing. A change of scenery is probably in the offing for Fernandes next year and Lisandro Martinez, a full-blown liability, is taking a leaf out of compatriot Cristian Romero’s playbook ahead of a likely exit.

United have a curious relationship with Argentines. Supporters flock at their feet yet they often have their hands burnt. Gabriel Heinze tried to join Liverpool, Carlos Tevez went to City, Angel di Maria went awol and Alejandro Garnacho was bombed out. Martinez has missed 93 United games through injury.

Ruben Amorim protected squad harmony by insisting on a ‘bomb squad’ for those with one foot out of the door. Yet Marcus Rashford, who would rather be elsewhere, was eased back into the fold with no fuss under Carrick. That severely undermined Carrick’s authority.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

United probably do not even know that they are ushering in a new era of player power. When it existed under Solskjaer and Ralf Rangnick, who both had the air of a substitute teacher, United won nothing in three-and-a-half years. Now they are 17th.

At least they can’t play Cheltenham or Chatham if they do go down.

Sports.title: ‘Enjoy this one, Gooners’ – Liverpool fans fume as Gravenberch likes Arsenal star’s Instagram post after Anfield win
Sports.content:
Next

LIVERPOOL fans were left fuming as Ryan Gravenberch liked an Arsenal post following his team’s heartbreaking loss to the reigning Premier League champions.

The Gunners beat the Reds at Anfield for the first time since 2012 after Kai Havertz led them to a 1-0 victory on Sunday.

Gravenberch, 24, was left on the bench by Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola but still found himself in the thick of it.



That is because the midfielder liked an Instagram post from Arsenal star Jurrien Timber about the result after full-time.



Timber, 25, published an image of himself from the derby clashing with Gravenberch‘s team-mate Alexis Mac Allister during a heated confrontation.

The versatile defender issued the following caption on his Instagram: “Proud of the team! Enjoy this one, Gooners.”

And Liverpool fans noticed Gravenberch gave the thumbs up to his Netherlands team-mate’s post.

As expected, that didn’t land well among the Merseysiders’ faithful who quickly took to social media to vent their frustrations.

One fan tweeted: “I don’t care if Gravenberch is friends with Timber. And I don’t care if Gravenberch is upset he didn’t play vs Arsenal, you don’t go liking Arsenal pictures after a Liverpool loss.”

Another gasped: “Why is Gravenberch liking this?”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



A third wrote: “That’s disgusting.”

This fan sent the following message to Liverpool’s decision-makers: “Sell.”

That one echoed: “Hopefully the club get rid of all the deadwood in the summer.”

And a comment read: “Should be a disciplinary ban from the club.”

Gravenberch and Timber have a long history with each other as they spent two years playing together at Ajax until 2022 and have been part of the Netherlands’ national team since 2021.



It is not yet clear if the post was liked directly by the Liverpool star or a third-party person, such as PRs.

Sports.title: Fans fume as footage emerges of grinning Gabriel and referee at half-time of Arsenal’s controversial win at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

FANS were left furious after footage of Gabriel Magalhaes and referee Andy Madley emerged on social media following Liverpool’s 1-0 loss to Arsenal on Sunday.

The Reds dropped points against the Gunners following a decisive goal from Kai Havertz in the first half.



However, they felt they deserved more from the game after being denied a penalty in the 21st minute.

Jurrien Timber pulled the shirt of Alexander Isak while a cross was being sent into the box.



Ex-referee Mark Halsey told SunSport that it was a “clear penalty” because it prevented a goalscoring opportunity.

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola felt the same and said: “Honestly, yes, we have to tell them to go down because they’re not going to call it otherwise.

“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it.

“I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear pull.”



Fans later noticed a moment between Gabriel and the referee at half-time.

The pair appeared to share a joke in the tunnel before going out for the second half.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Gabriel then gave Madley a fist bump before walking out to the pitch.

Fans took to social media to react, with one person writing: “This referee clearly had a favourite. Liverpool got robbed in broad daylight.”

Another said: “Couldn’t be more blatant.”



While a third commented: “He shouldn’t have been joking…”

However, others appeared to suggest it was just an innocent moment.

One fan wrote: “One laugh in the tunnel and suddenly everyone’s a body language expert…”

Another said: “Ref isn’t allowed to talk to players now?”

And another added: “There’s absolutely nothing wrong with this.”



Arsenal fans also felt hard done by with some decisions on Sunday.

In the opening minute, Trey Nyoni avoided a booking for a clumsy challenge on Martin Odegaard.

He also avoided a yellow card for a late challenge on Havertz.

The result saw Arsenal move three points clear at the top of the Premier League table.

Sports.title: ‘We’ve done it’ – Mikel Arteta declares ‘mission accomplished’ as Arsenal end 14-year Anfield curse with Liverpool win
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA hailed his Arsenal stars after they completed their mission and conquered Anfield for the first time in 14 years.

Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher labelled Alexis Mac Allister a “joke” in a heated end to the game after the midfielder tried to get Noni Madueke sent off following a clash of heads.



Reds boss Andoni Iraola and captain Virgil van Dijk were both fuming after the 1-0 defeat because Alexander Isak was denied a first half penalty, despite Jurrien Timber pulling his shirt.

Kai Havertz’s 16th minute goal secured Arsenal’s first top-flight win at Anfield since 2012 and sent them three points clear at the top of the Premier League.



Arteta said: “I’m extremely proud. That’s the challenge and mission you want to accomplish.

“I love it when it’s something we have not done for many years. It was the same with Chelsea away and Manchester United away.



“To be able to beat all of those [teams], that’s the purpose and motivation and why we do what we do.

“I had the feeling that now was the moment. We were going to have to dig deep, have an element of luck at times, and for sure a lot of quality in key moments. We have done it.”

Arsenal had to weather the storm after Declan Rice teed up Havertz for the game’s only goal.

And a feisty finish led to Madueke and Mac Allister squaring up to each other.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Arsenal players were unhappy after Mac Allister slapped captain Martin Odegaard on the head when he was on the ground.

The Liverpool midfielder then threw himself on the deck when Madueke confronted him, which angered Carragher.

The Reds legend said: “It’s a joke from Mac Allister and it’s got to stop.

“I want Liverpool to win the game, but I’m delighted he [Madueke] didn’t get sent off.

“We have really got to be calling people out and saying, ‘this is embarrassing’. It’s ridiculous and it’s got to stop. I can’t stand it.



“If someone puts their head back and butts, then red card. But if it’s head-to-head and they touch, the other one goes down and the player gets sent off, as a game, call your own people out on it.”

Liverpool’s best spell came in the first half after Arsenal took the lead.

Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar with a free-kick, and Isak had a penalty shout waved away after Timber pulled his shirt when the striker tried to get on the end of a cross.



The Swede did not go down and, asked if he would tell him to do so in the future, Iraola said: “Yes, definitely.

“That’s the problem we have with the game, because he doesn’t dive and go to the floor. The shame is that we have to tell our players to dive.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Van Dijk shared the view of his manager and added: “We have 50 cameras, why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras?

“Everyone has seen it. In the end it wasn’t given and we lost the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal.”

Sports.title: ‘I don’t forget’ – Piero Hincapie aims dig at Virgil van Dijk after Arsenal’s win at Liverpool as fans hail ‘petty king’
Sports.content:
Next

PIERO HINCAPIE appeared to aim a cheeky dig at Virgil van Dijk after Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0.

Kai Havertz‘s 13th minute strike was enough to earn the Gunners their first win at Anfield since 2014.

Hincapie, 24, came on as an 84th minute substitute for Christos Tzolis to help see out the victory.



After the match, the Ecuadorian posted pictures from the contest to his Instagram page, captioned: “I don’t forget..”



Initially, the carousel appeared to include a close up image of the gold Premier League badge on his shirt sleeve, denoting Arsenal‘s status as champions.

This appeared to be a jab at Virgil van Dijk, who posted a similar picture of himself after Liverpool’s 0-0 draw at the Emirates in January.

Arsenal fans loved Hincapie’s post, with one calling him a “petty king”.



While a second jibed: “What goes around, comes around.”

A third gushed: “I like how petty we are”.

Although another added: “One is a UCL winner, the other one can’t say”.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The picture of Hincapie’s sleeve mysteriously vanished from the post within a couple of hours.



Declan Rice commented on the post with a smiling emoji.

And Ezri Konsa added two flame emojis and a heart.

Hincapie’s post swiftly received more than 100,000 likes.

Arsenal’s win saw them return to the top of the Premier League table.

The Gunners are three points clear of Manchester City, after Enzo Maresca‘s side lost 1-0 to Brighton on Saturday.

Sports.title: ‘Embarrassing’ – Carragher blasts Mac Allister for ‘joke’ falling theatrics vs Arsenal and demands ‘this has to stop’
Sports.content:
Next

JAMIE CARRAGHER launched a scathing attack on Alexis Mac Allister after trying to get Noni Madueke sent off.

The Argentine, 27, could not stop Liverpool falling to a 1-0 defeat against Premier League table-toppers Arsenal.



And Mac Allister was involved in a major flashpoint after sparking a huge bust-up.

The midfielder screamed at Martin Odegaard and tapped the back of the grounded Arsenal skipper’s head.



Mac Allister, who missed out on a new deal in the summer, then threw himself to the floor when Madueke’s head brushed his.

But Carragher blasted the former Brighton man after attempting to reduce Arsenal to ten men.

The Anfield legend, 48, told Sky Sports: “I want Liverpool to win the game, but I’m delighted he [Madueke] didn’t get sent off.

“We have really got to be calling people out and saying, ‘this is embarrassing’.

“It’s ridiculous and it’s got to stop. I can’t stand it. If someone puts their head back and butts, then it’s a red card.

“But if it’s head-to-head and they touch, the other one goes down and the player gets sent off, as a game, call your own people out on it.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“It’s a joke from Mac Allister and it’s got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they can and red cards are being given for it.

“Whether it’s [ProRef supremo] Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers getting together, this has got to stop.”

Ex-Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge, 37, also hit out at Mac Allister’s shock theatrics.

He said: “He doesn’t headbutt him with any force. It’s a coming together and they’re both into it.

“He’s trying to bait him and that is league wide – that’s not just Mac Allister. Every player in world football – that’s the game.



“He knew exactly what he was doing and ultimately it didn’t work out for him. You tried to bait a man into something and he didn’t bite.”

Ian Wright, who joined Carragher and Sturridge on Sky Sports punditry duties, called for changes to be made in an attempt to stop stars trying to get opponents sent off.

The iconic Arsenal marksman, 62, added: “The first thing with Mac Allister is the way he goes over. He’s actually slapped Odegaard on the back of the head.

“The laws have to do something about this because that [Mac Allister going down] is trying to get someone sent off.”

Sports.title: Labuschagne facing Australia axe after poor South Africa series?
Sports.content:
Marnus Labuschagne is facing the axe from the Australia Test team after their 2-1 series defeat in South Africa, with head coach Andrew McDonald saying "he hasn't taken his opportunity on this tour".

Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting had branded Labuschagne's spot as "untenable" after a lean return at home to Bangladesh left him without a Test century in 43 innings, stretching back to the 2023 Ashes in England.

That has now extended to 49 innings after he signed off the South Africa series, in which he averaged 21.83, with scores of 0 and 4 as Australia lost the series-deciding Test in Cape Town.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day five of the series-deciding third Test between South Africa and Australia as the Proteas won by 176 runs to go top of the rankings.

"We believed in Marnus for this tour, we'll have to reassess that as we move forward," McDonald said.

"There's still a very good cricketer ‌there. Every time he drops back to state level, he outperforms the others. But he hasn't taken his opportunity on this tour."

Australia have faced some fierce criticism for the way they lost the series in South Africa, with an innings defeat in the second Test followed by a 176-run drubbing in the third - the Proteas knocking them off the No 1 spot in the Test rankings as a result.

Image: Australia collapsed to a heavy defeat on the final day in Cape Town to lose the series and their No 1 Test ranking to South Africa

Set 288 on the final day in Cape Town, Pat Cummins' side were 60-7 by lunch as they were ultimately bowled out for 111 in a timid display, which former opener David Warner branded "disgraceful" and "un-Australian".

McDonald, though, backed his players, telling reporters: "It's still a very good cricket ​team with a lot of very good players in there.

"Some are legends of the game, or down the path they will be acknowledged as legends of the game. So we've got to ​balance that out with who comes in, what the next decisions are."

He added: "In the emotion of the current situation, my answer would be we've underachieved here.

"I think people put a lot of sort of premium on the key series, and that's ultimately where you are judged. ​We understand that, we realise that."

Australia much-changed for England white-ball series

Australia's defeat at Newlands was their third in five Tests, jeopardising their campaign to reach a third-straight World Test ⁠Championship final next year.

They next host a four-Test series against ⁠New Zealand in December and January, which is followed by a trip to India to play a five-match series. They visit England next summer for the 2027 Ashes.

Before any of that, they host England for three one-day internationals and five T20Is in November and December, with Australia naming a much-changed squad.

Image: Matt Renshaw impressed for Australia in South Africa, averaging 61.50 and hitting 190 in the first-Test win in Durban

Travis Head, Matt Renshaw, Cameron Green, Alex Carey, Josh Inglis ​and Cooper Connolly are the only players from the South Africa Test series that feature in the ODI squad. ‌None will play in the T20s.

Front-line pace bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Test captain Cummins are being rested. Mitch Marsh will captain both white-ball squads.

The ODI series begins in Perth on ⁠November 13, with further matches in Adelaide and ​Hobart. There will be five T20 clashes in Melbourne, ​Gold Coast, Brisbane, Sydney and Canberra in late November and ​early December.

Australia ODI squad vs England: Mitchell Marsh (captain), Xavier Bartlett, Mahli Beardman, Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Jack Edwards, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Spencer ⁠Johnson, Ollie Peake, Matthew Renshaw, Liam Scott, ​Adam Zampa

Australia T20I squad vs England: Mitchell Marsh (captain), Xavier Bartlett, Mahli Beardman, ​Nikhil Chaudhary, Tim David, Joel Davies, Jack Edwards, Nathan Ellis, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Sam Harper, Spencer Johnson, Mitchell Owen, ‌Lachlan Shaw, Adam Zampa

Sports.title: Haskell backs Borthwick, Pollock as England prepare for Nations Championship
Sports.content:
James Haskell has backed Steve Borthwick as "the right man for the job" as England prepare for the conclusion of the inaugural Nations Championship in November.

Borthwick oversaw England's worst-ever Six Nations campaign earlier this year, with four losses from their five matches, but despite growing pressure the RFU have publicly expressed their support for Borthwick through to the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

This month, England will face Australia, Japan and New Zealand ahead of Finals Weekend, which takes place November 27-28 at Twickenham.

Former England international Haskell, who earned 77 Test caps between 2007 and 2019, insists it is not the time to change the head coach.

"The RFU have got behind Steve Borthwick, and rightly so," Haskell told Sky Sports.

"I think he's the right man for the job."

Image: Former England back-row James Haskell spoke to Sky Sports about head coach Borthwick and back-row Pollock

Borthwick oversaw a 12-game unbeaten streak ahead of the 2026 Six Nations, and Haskell insists the change in performance is not as stark as the critics might suggest.

"It's never as bad as you think it is and it's never as good as you think it is," he said.

"I think there's a lot of talent, and without being a super nerd - which rugby pundits often can be - if you look at the stats, we create lots of opportunities.

"When we were on our unbeaten run of 12 games, 83 per cent of the time we got into the 22-metre line, we took away points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' James Cole speaks with Borthwick ahead of England's Nations Championship Tests, starting with Australia

"When we were losing games, we were making the same opportunities but coming away with points less than 33 per cent of the time.

"And that's the fine margins."

Pollock has that 'X-factor'

Haskell also praised the ego and style of rising star Henry Pollock.

The Northampton Saints back-row who made headlines by becoming the first rugby union player to sign for Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency back in March, could be given more international chances in the coming weeks.

"He's definitely got that X-factor, in terms of the way he plays," said Haskell.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Borthwick reacts to the scuffle between Northampton Saints and Leicester Tigers players which featured England players Henry Pollock and Ollie Chessum

"He's probably the most talked about rugby player at the moment. He creates opinion and challenges opinion - and that's what makes the world go round now.

"But when he gets opportunities on the field, he delivers… I'm very excited that he will hopefully get more of a chance to play for England.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Borthwick believes he is close to deciding which players will secure a place in his eventual squad for the World Cup which takes place in Australia in 2027

"It will challenge some of the stuffier, more stoic sides of the upper echelons, and of the fanbase, who like their sports stars manageable and with a bit of ego, but not too much.

"If someone could bring that cohesion together, keep raising awareness and building superstars like Henry Pollock, you're going to be in a great place."

Sports.title: From crisis to champion: Antonelli's historic turnaround
Sports.content:
This is how it was meant to be.

When Mercedes announced in August 2024 that they were fast-tracking Kimi Antonelli - who had turned 18 just days earlier - into one of Formula 1's most desirable seats, expectations could not have been set much higher.

Fast-forward a little more than two years, and the Italian has delivered on his billing as a generational talent by becoming the sport's youngest world champion at the age of 20.

Even with expectations set so high, winning a title in just his second season in F1 has seen Antonelli surely exceed even the wildest dreams of Mercedes chief Toto Wolff.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli watches back a montage of videos from his journey from go-karting, to F1's youngest champion.

But the most remarkable thing about Antonelli's triumph is the fact that this sporting fairy tale didn't initially go to plan, starting from the day before his signing was announced.

After Antonelli was crowned at the chequered flag of Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, Sky Sports F1 look back at his remarkable journey to this moment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli wore a GoPro during his celebrations at the Mexico Grand Prix.

Shock Hamilton exit leads to Wolff gamble

Mercedes were left stunned in February 2024 when Lewis Hamilton announced that he had decided to leave the team he had won six of his seven championships with to join Ferrari the following year.

Once the dust had settled on the biggest driver transfer in the sport's history, Wolff's attention shifted to finding a new team-mate for George Russell, whose strong first two campaigns with the team had suggested he was a world champion in waiting.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Those who've known Antonelli from a young age reflect on what's got him to the top of Formula 1.

The Austrian's top target appeared to be Red Bull's Max Verstappen, while the likes of Fernando Alonso and Carlos Sainz, who was making way for Hamilton at Ferrari, provided very solid and experienced options.

The wildcard for Wolff was Antonelli, who had been scouted by Mercedes as he dominated the European karting scene and signed by the team in 2019 as a 12-year-old.

Antonelli starred as he worked his way through the junior categories, so much so that Mercedes had him skip Formula 3 to go straight up to Formula 2 in 2024.

It's unclear whether Wolff had planned to loan Antonelli out to another team, as was the case when Russell, also a product of Mercedes' junior programme, spent his first three seasons in F1 at Williams, but the opening created by Hamilton's departure changed everything.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sebastian Vettel congratulated Kimi Antonelli on breaking his record as the youngest ever Formula One world champion.

An unprecedented testing programme was arranged that allowed Antonelli big chunks of track time in Mercedes' cars from recent seasons. It was surely in those sessions, rather than a slightly underwhelming F2 campaign in which he finished sixth, that Wolff saw enough to convince him to roll the dice.

Some speculated that a factor in Wolff's decision was his regret at missing out on signing Verstappen as a teenager a decade earlier and wanting to ensure there was no way the sport's next generational talent would somehow end up in the clutches of a rival team.

Crisis point? Tears and 'underwhelming' Wolff

Antonelli was not only replacing the most successful driver in the sport's history in Hamilton, but the only real example of someone of his age being given a chance at a top team was when Red Bull promoted Verstappen from their junior squad during the 2017 season.

Even in that case, the Dutchman had 23 Grands Prix under his belt.

While it had become clear in the paddock that Antonelli had been chosen to partner Russell in 2025, Mercedes arranged a grand announcement around the 2024 Italian Grand Prix in Monza.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli loses control of his Mercedes and has a huge crash on his practice debut at the Italian Grand Prix in 2024.

The plan was for him to make his first appearance in F1 practice on the Friday, before his signing was officially announced on Saturday. That is what happened, but only after Antonelli had destroyed the car by spinning into a barrier at high speed just 10 minutes into the session.

Six months later, Antonelli's first F1 qualifying session didn't go to plan either as he was knocked out of Q1 in Melbourne. But he would drive a mature race to fight back to fourth in the wet, and make a generally solid start to the season, with a Sprint pole position in Miami offering the first real glimpse of the speed that had been promised.

A first Grand Prix podium followed in Canada in June, but instead of pushing on from there, the Antonelli story reached its darkest moments.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli caused a collision with Max Verstappen at the 2025 Austrian Grand Prix.

There was the difficult sight of the teenage boy dabbing at his tearful eyes with a tissue as he attempted to conduct his media responsibilities in Belgium after an early qualifying exit, before Monza once more failed to provide any home comforts.

Having scored just one point across the five preceding races, Antonelli endured a torrid weekend at the Temple of Speed, which saw a crash in practice throw off his preparations before he finished ninth in the race. The Mercedes W16 car was far from best-in-field, but Russell had got it in the top five at five of those six races.

Wolff had been steadfast in his backing of Antonelli throughout the year, which meant it felt extremely significant when the Austrian was publicly critical of his young star for the first time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli was involved in another collision with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc at the 2025 Dutch Grand Prix.

"Underwhelming this weekend, underwhelming," Wolff said. "You can't put the car in the gravel bed and expect to be there. All of the race was underwhelming."

Wolff caveated his criticism by insisting he retained belief in his driver, but the comments raised doubts over whether Mercedes would persist with Antonelli if there wasn't an upturn in performance.

The tough love from Wolff appeared to work as Antonelli found some form to deliver a stronger final third of the year, with a memorable drive, once more in the wet, in Brazil providing a season's-best second-placed finish.

Antonelli arrives with five in a row

There was a major shift in the sport's landscape over the winter as the introduction of new chassis and power unit regulations effectively reset the playing field.

Having failed to contend for titles during the previous generation of rules from 2022 to 2025, Mercedes were installed as pre-season favourites, with paddock murmurings establishing a widespread belief that the Silver Arrows had aced their new engine - as they did in 2014 - and would start strongly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli is left almost speechless after securing his first Grand Prix win in China, while Lewis Hamilton congratulates the him after finishing third.

While the change in competitive order of teams was anticipated, there was less of an expectation that alterations in driver performance could be similarly dramatic. For that reason, Russell was considered the clear favourite to claim the drivers' title.

While Russell lived up to expectations by taking pole position and winning the opening race of the season in Australia, perhaps more important in the long run was the second place Antonelli salvaged after an unnecessary crash in final practice threatened to leave him starting from the back of the grid.

Having avoided calamity, Antonelli took advantage of a little bit of luck as Russell suffered technical issues in Chinese Grand Prix qualifying to take pole, and backed that up by claiming the first race victory of his career a day later.

The result was the start of a streak that will live long in F1's history books, with Antonelli going on to reel off the first five victories of his career in successive races as wins followed in Japan, Miami, Canada and Monaco.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli jumps in Monaco harbour, celebrating his fifth consecutive win of the 2026 Formula 1 season.

Russell was left dumbfounded. The title chance he had waited patiently for was suddenly being snatched away.

The Brit appeared in denial to begin with as he attributed the results to various external factors, but by the time Antonelli dominated and Russell finished 12th on a Monaco weekend where few expected Mercedes to win, it had become clear to all that the generational talent had well and truly arrived.

Wolff recently reflected: "It's been 30 or more years that I've tried to understand racing drivers' brains, and I still don't know what has happened (to Antonelli) over the winter. His ability to process and deliver something that's outstanding, which we didn't see coming."

Monza magic and Austin excellence close the show

However, winning a title rarely comes without adversity, and it struck during the European summer as an engine failure took Antonelli out of a podium finish in Barcelona, before a wheel-guard failure denied him a potential victory at the British Grand Prix a few weeks later.

Russell was back within 25 points, while Hamilton was also in striking distance a further seven points adrift, and Mercedes were no longer as dominant as they had been in the early stages of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli has impressed his rivals during the 2026 F1 season.

With the pressure on, Antonelli responded by winning the next race in Belgium and then delivering podiums either side of the summer break to rebuild his lead, but the best was still to come.

Unlike a year earlier when Oscar Piastri had appeared on course for his maiden title before suffering a dramatic loss of form and finishing third in the standings, Antonelli seemed to get better.

Given what had happened to Antonelli on his previous two appearances at Monza, it seemed there was a psychological element to a decision being made for him to take an engine penalty at the race, which would drop him to 19th on the grid, perhaps relieving the pressure that had hindered him at home in the past.

It turned out to be a masterstroke, as Antonelli scythed his way through the field to win with ease, producing a performance that belongs with legendary displays of the past: Verstappen in Brazil in 2024, Hamilton in Germany in 2018, Michael Schumacher in Belgium in 1995.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch how Antonelli converted 19th to 1st to take a sensational victory at the Italian Grand Prix.

The drive alone was enough to make it the standout moment of this season, but there were two further elements that made it even more significant.

The result demoralised Russell, who had started from second on the grid, and made it a question of when, not if, Antonelli was going to close out his triumph.

And then there was the turning of the tifosi, Ferrari's fiercely loyal legion of fans in red, many of whom found themselves cheering for Antonelli and proudly singing the Italian national anthem as the boy wonder stood on the top step of the podium.

While it was less eye-catching than the Monza display, Antonelli would also produce a different type of brilliant victory at the United States Grand Prix as he overcame Mercedes' struggles with their new upgrade package to deny an in-form Verstappen pole, before producing an unexpectedly dominant race to win comfortably.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli produced a superb drive to win the United States Grand Prix.

Antonelli could hardly be more popular within his Mercedes team, but the result was a massive moment for the Silver Arrows as it confirmed there is potential in the development path they've been pursuing ahead of a 2027 season where Red Bull and Verstappen look primed to return to title contention.

Wolff described it as Antonelli's "best race" in F1, before being reminded of what had happened in Monza seven weeks earlier. The Austrian admitted he may have been slightly forgetful, but insisted the performances belonged in the same bracket.

A megastar in waiting?

The mathematical equation after the Austin victory turned the Mexico City Grand Prix into something of a title parade for Antonelli, but he still overcame illness and nerves to produce a strong performance that earned him a podium finish in third.

While there was no crowning victory, the fairy-tale scene on the podium was near perfect as race winner Verstappen and second-placed Hamilton - the two most successful drivers on the current grid - hoisted Antonelli onto their shoulders, creating an iconic image that will live long in the memory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former world champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton lift Antonelli onto their shoulders in Mexico.

The problem for the rest of the grid, and his team-mate Russell in particular, is that Antonelli should theoretically get better and better.

As Wolff explained in Austin, "the work of nine years" and more than £10m has gone into developing Antonelli. There is little doubt that both the team and driver himself will continue to leave no stone unturned in maximising his extraordinary talent.

Perhaps crucial to that process has been Mercedes allowing Antonelli to act his age in some ways, with videos of him pranking his engineers and vice versa shared on the team's social media channels throughout the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was ecstatic after Antonelli sealed the title.

While Mercedes have created a familial environment for Antonelli to thrive in, credit must also go to his own parents, who have raised a young man who has achieved the remarkable feat, at least to this point of his career, of being almost universally popular.

His father Marco, a former racing driver himself, has been an ever-present in the paddock, but has also taken enough of a step back to allow an extremely close father-son relationship to flourish without creating too many challenges for the team.

You'd be hard pushed to find anyone in the paddock - driver, team boss or journalist - who would have a bad word to say about Antonelli, who does just about everything with a smile on his face.

Even McLaren team principal Andrea Stella, whose squad were constructors' champions in 2024 and 2025, spoke of his pride and excitement as an Italian at seeing what Antonelli is doing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli was in buoyant mood after becoming the youngest ever Formula world champion.

Away from the paddock, Antonelli's age and charm have made him extremely popular with younger fans of the sport, and he will surely continue to bring new followers in Italy and beyond.

With Italy's passionate fans desperate for a new hero amid their men's football team's continued slump and tennis star Jannik Sinner struggling with injuries, Antonelli is quite possibly about to become the nation's most popular sporting figure.

If F1 bosses had any fears over the sport lacking some star power when Hamilton eventually retires, the emergence of Antonelli will have them sleeping easier, with global superstardom an inevitably if he continues on this path.

The other question that probably won't go away until it happens, whether that's in five, 10 or 15 years, is whether Antonelli will follow in Hamilton's footsteps by moving from Mercedes to Ferrari.

Enjoy the ride.

Formula 1 next heads to Brazil for the final leg of the triple header with the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from November 6-8, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW.

Sports.title: Hamilton hits out at Leclerc after Mexico clash
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton criticised Charles Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix, suggesting his team-mate's driving came down to "a mentality thing".

Hamilton and Leclerc battled for the lead during the first four corners of Sunday's race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in a duel that saw the latter cut across the second chicane to take over first place from the pole-sitting Briton.

Having also run slightly wide himself in defence of the position, Hamilton was overtaken on the exit of Turn Five by Max Verstappen.

That proved significant as when Leclerc was handed a five-second penalty by stewards for running off track and gaining an advantage in the Turn Four incident, Verstappen took over the lead of the race when the lead Ferrari served the sanction at his pit stop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton criticised Charles Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari a likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Verstappen went on to win, with Hamilton eventually finishing a close second after passing Leclerc at the second race start following a red-flag period for Valtteri Bottas' high-speed crash.

Hamilton, who had expressed unhappiness over the radio on several occasions with the fact Leclerc had only been handed a five-second sanction by the stewards, said after the team's eventual two-four finish that they required "serious talks behind the scenes" in a season that has contained other flashpoints between the team-mates, including the opening lap at Monza two months ago.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.

Speaking in the post-race press conference, Hamilton was asked about Leclerc and whether a different approach was required against a team-mate when it came to fighting for race wins.

"Before I joined this team, when I was in Mercedes, I watched and witnessed the back and forth between Charles and Carlos [Sainz] for several races where they were battling so much that the person ahead just pulled away, and they had the pace to actually win the race," said Hamilton, who is in his second season at Ferrari alongside Leclerc.

"But it's one thing when that's happening for fourth and fifth, as opposed to first and second, and you lose the win. That's significant.

"The guy's 28 years old, so I don't think it's an age thing. I think it's a mentality thing. It's like 'do or die. Like either I win or none of us do', and it shouldn't be that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive a dramatic opening lap as Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was given a five-second penalty after overtaking Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the Mexico City Grand Prix.

"It should be us getting that one-two because it's still a good feeling.

"Silverstone, I could have gone all kamikaze on him and taken him off and lost us the win but instead it was first and third.

"For me, I'm happy for the team to have experienced that. But I'm hopeful we'll work towards a better working place in the future."

Stewards' verdict on Hamilton-Leclerc battle "The Stewards have determined that both cars entered turn 4 with excessive speed and therefore neither would have been able to make the corner on track, as demonstrated by the fact that car 44 [Hamilton] which was on the inside, had to go off track to make the corner.



"Car 16 [Leclerc] was therefore not entitled to claim the corner due to the excessive entry speed. The driver then completed an overtake whilst off track and accordingly this warrants a penalty.



"The baseline penalty guideline is 10 seconds however in mitigation is the fact that car 44 was also off track on the inside of car 16 and this occurred early in the first lap."

'Today we lost the win for the team'

Speaking to Sky Sports F1, Hamilton said Ferrari's wider interests on the first lap had not been put first.

"In the race, I gave it everything," he said after finishing within one second of Verstappen.

"Unfortunately the race was lost in the first few corners and it's a shame because we could have easily finished first and second in this race if we worked together as a team."

Asked if there had been any pre-race discussions about how they would approach the opening lap, which features the longest run of the season to the first corner, from first and third on the grid, Hamilton said: "We didn't sit down and talk before.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc reflect on their Mexico City GP, which saw them tussle at the start of the race.

"Again, it's something I mentioned in the past, but it's all fair and well racing against your team-mate as long as it's not to the detriment of the team's points and the team's opportunity of getting the result.

"At the end of the day the team has to come first and today we lost the win for the team, today we lost points, I lost second in the championship and that's a real shame.

"It affects so many people back at the factory. Luckily, we still got points so we can hold onto second in the constructors' but it impacts the people that put in all the hard work, and the Tifosi. So it wasn't good."

Hamilton added: "It definitely needs some discussions for sure but we'll take it offline and figure out what we can do."

What did Leclerc say about the first lap battle?

Leclerc, who eventually finished fourth, defended his approach to the opening corners of the race, although suggested his first thought after running off track at Turn Four had been to give Hamilton the lead back.

By then, however, Verstappen was between them on the road.

Leclerc told Sky Sports F1: "Turns One, Two there was a gap and when you're fighting for a win, I will always go for it.

"Turns Four, Five I broke as late as I possibly could and I guess Lewis did the same and we didn't both make the corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok analyses Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc's battle at the start of the Mexico City GP.

"Then in my head it was about giving the position back but then Lewis got overtaken by Max and I thought it was worth it to kind of try and see what happened because it was a very confusing situation.

"I asked on the radio but I kept my position."

Asked about what will happen next, Leclerc added: "I'm sure Lewis definitely hated those first few laps and we'll discuss."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen was full of praise for Kimi Antonelli after he became Formula One's youngest ever world champion.

'Today it cost them the win' - Verstappen cashes in on Ferrari squabble

After claiming his third win in four races to move ahead of Hamilton and Mercedes' George Russell to second in the Drivers' Championship, Verstappen offered his assessment of what had unfolded ahead of him on the opening lap.

"I think today we also capitalised on Ferrari's battles with each other," Verstappen told Sky Sports F1.

"They are two No 1 drivers so they always go for it, but I think today it cost them the win."

Sports.title: Novak cruises to Mexico Open title for maiden individual PGA Tour triumph
Sports.content:
Andrew Novak bounced back from seeing his six-shot lead halved with three straight birdies to card a two-under 69 and win the Mexico Open by five shots, claiming his first individual PGA Tour title.

Novak staked himself to a big lead with rounds of 61-62 the previous two days, and it was going to take something special to track him down. But with a soft bogey on the 10th hole, his lead was down to three over Steven Fisk and Mexico-born Norwegian Kristoffer Ventura.

And then it was effectively over. Novak hit a greenside bunker shot to four feet on the par-5 12th at Vidanta Vallarta, drove the 13th green to 15 feet for a two-putt birdie, and he ended his decisive run with a 45-foot birdie putt on the 14th.

"That kind of really settled everything," Novak said. "Just happy with how I played today. I thought I grinded it out pretty well."

Mackenzie Hughes of Canada shot 66 and wound up in a tie for fourth when Doug Ghim, playing in the final group, made double bogey on the 18th hole. Hughes moved up to No. 101, a manageable spot with three tournaments remaining.

"Gives me a bit of momentum for the last three," Hughes said. "Obviously, I still know I need more points and I need to keep climbing, but today was a big step in the right direction."

Hughes tied for fourth with Ben Griffin, who was Novak's partner when they won the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year. Griffin (67) was waiting on the 18th green when Novak finished.

"I loved Zurich and everything about that tournament. That's so fun," Novak said. "But it is nice to have one by myself, too. This is one I've been working for for a while. Obviously not a great season for how I wanted it to go, but this is a nice way to kind of finish."

On the third hole, the easiest of the par 5s, Novak's second shot plugged into the lip and he could only nudge back into the bunker, leading to par. He missed two other birdie chances from just inside 10 feet on the front nine.

"I played really well on the front and didn't get much out of it," he said.

Novak waited his turn, and three straight birdies was more than enough to send him on his way. He moved from No 89 to No 53 in the FedEx Cup, making him practically a lock to at least be in a pair of $20m (£14m) signature events next year at Pebble Beach and Riviera.

The victory also assures Novak will start the 2028 on the upper Championship Series.

Sports.title: America's next great heavyweight? 'Stop looking. I'm already here!'
Sports.content:
American boxing needs a great heavyweight champion, and Da’Mazion Vanhouter is here to audition for the role.

Vanhouter is in the early stage of his professional career but the prospect has been blasting through his recent opposition.

An explosive puncher, he's on a run of seven consecutive inside-the-distance victories. Overall nine of his 10 stoppage wins have come in the first round.

His last fight caught the eye especially. Against the six foot eight inches tall Raphael Akpejiori in Las Vegas, it looked like Vanhouter's left shoulder was badly wrenched out of position. He responded immediately - viciously knocing Akpejiori out with his other hand.

"I'm just here to fight and showcase my skills."

Vanhouter is still only 21 years old and 13 fights into a professional career that began when he was just 17. As a teenager remarkably he boxed down at super-welterweight. He's put on nearly 80lbs since then as he's developed into a heavyweight.
