"I've grown into my frame but I still fight the same, the same movement, the same speed, I think I've gotten faster and obviously I hit harder now than I did before," Vanhouter said.

America was once the home of heavyweight boxing. Over the last decade, with the exception of Deontay Wilder, European fighters have dominated the heavyweight division. It's prompted a search to find America's next great heavyweight.

Vanhouter is ready to answer the call.

"They already stopped looking. Because I'm already here," he said with a beaming smile. "I'm here for it. That's the role I've taken, it's normal.

"I wouldn't be boxing if I didn't want to be the best. That means I want to be the best heavyweight."

High expectation can lead to a harsh fall. Moses Itauma, only 21 years old too, was, and is, the next great hope in British heavyweight boxing.

But even Itauma came unstuck in his first world title fight, losing surprisingly to Filip Hrgovic.

It's the American's fourth fight with Dana White's high-profile Zuffa Boxing promotion.

White believes that in Vanhouter they have a star for the future. "It would be great to have an unbelievable American heavyweight," White told Sky Sports.

"What America definitely needs is some heavyweights. Obviously we're high on him, we believe in him and that's exactly what we need for boxing in America."

Sports.title: Wolff: Russell 'distraught' after watching Antonelli seal title
Sports.content:
Toto Wolff has revealed that Mercedes excused George Russell from carrying out his post-Mexico City Grand Prix media duties because the British driver was "distraught" after seeing his team-mate Kimi Antonelli clinch the Drivers' Championship.

Russell began the season as the clear title favourite but has been comprehensively outperformed by Antonelli, who finished third in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest ever world champion at the age of 20, with four rounds still remaining.

Russell started second on the grid, but a poor getaway - caused by a technical issue out of his control - saw him drop back to sixth on the opening lap, during which he was adjudged to have caused a collision with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar that would earn him a 10-second time penalty.

Before avoiding his obligatory media duties and leaving the circuit, Russell was one of the first to congratulate Antonelli in person as he embraced the Italian, after eventually finishing sixth himself.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.

Mercedes initially announced Russell wouldn't be doing any post-race interviews without providing a reason, but Wolff later explained the situation.

"I saw George after the race on the FIA scales, and obviously he's distraught about the situation," Wolff said.

"It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was ecstatic after Kimi Antonelli became the youngest ever champion in Formula One history.

"I have known George for such a long time. So, I saw him and thought, for a racing driver, this is a catastrophic moment.

"And maybe today the race was a little bit a picture of his season. This was a race for him to win. We had the pace in the car. And we let him down on the first straight. The energy delivery is not what we thought it should be.

"And so I'm very much with him at the moment. I've been in situations where it's very, very difficult to cope.

"So, him not doing the media work, or leaving the track, is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at some of F1's newly-crowed champion Kimi Antonelli's best moments of the season.

Mercedes were fined €5,000 (£4,173) by the FIA for Russell's absence from his media duties.

The result also saw Russell drop from second to fourth in the drivers' standings, with race winner Max Verstappen climbing two places and second-placed finisher Lewis Hamilton moving ahead of Russell but remaining third.

Russell is scheduled to speak to the media on Thursday in Brazil ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.content:
1 Arsenal show maturity and quality

Good defending is the mark of champions. At Anfield, where Arsenal had not won in the past 13 visits, Mikel Arteta followed the orthodoxy of locking down once his team took the lead. This time around, it proved successful. Arsenal did not allow the occasion or the stadium to get to them as they have on previous occasions. In April 2023, Granit Xhaka entangling with Trent Alexander-Arnold energised home fans previously despondent that Arsenal were 2-0 up. It finished 2-2. On Sunday, Liverpool zipped around zestfully, as Andoni Iraola requests, though the final-ball quality was lacking. That owed a great deal to the organisation of the Arsenal defence. Ahead of the last international break, Brighton set a blueprint for getting the better of Arsenal in winning 3-0. Liverpool’s squad profile might have made a similar strategy possible though Iraola’s outfit is struggling to create chances in the same volume as Brighton or his Bournemouth team. John Brewin

View image in fullscreen Kai Havertz scores the only goal at Anfield. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

2 Reds’ attacking flurries not enough

No shots on target for Liverpool, leaving them with zero margin for the errors that preceded Kai Havertz’s decisive goal. Nine points behind Arsenal with a quarter of the season gone, Liverpool’s season risks becoming a developmental one, a time to regroup and rethink rather than challenging for the title. The squad Iraola inherited still bears the weight of the failed rebuild of the summer of 2025. Florian Wirtz was both unlucky when rattling the crossbar and too ponderous when a second-half chance dropped his way. Alexander Isak is nothing like the busy-bee striker his manager asks to press from the front. Milos Kerkez continues to be chaotic. Bradley Barcola, 2026’s headline signing, played his part in the flurry that followed Arsenal’s goal but faded, as did his fellow forwards. There are shards of light. Jérémy Jacquet and Trey Nyoni (aggressive – perhaps too aggressive – and involved in his hour on the field) are young players who can go places. Though it may take some time for Liverpool to get there as a team. JB

3 Emery can keep Villa in the sun

The small matter of a glamorous trip to Barcelona comes first for Aston Villa but it is a quirk of timing that Unai Emery’s next Premier League assignment should come at Old Trafford. It is the historical stature of Manchester United that triggered all the controversy over Jamie Carragher’s claim that Emery should be looking to climb the football chain and consider succeeding Michael Carrick should he be sacked. But even if Emery perceived United as a step up (as Youri Tielemans did when trading clubs in the summer, and look where that’s led him), would he prosper there? At Villa Park, he has an increasingly strong hold on how all team affairs are run, as signalled by his nominal upgrade from head coach to manager when he last signed a new contract, and he will visit the Camp Nou looking to extend Villa’s 100% start to their Champions League campaign. Having suffered dips at Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal, there is no certainty Emery’s methods would work in the febrile cauldron that is Old Trafford. After all, Manchester United will never be Aston Villa. Peter Lansley

4 Rose helping Bournemouth bloom

Bournemouth are in full flow, winning each of their past six matches, scoring 16 goals. All while Alex Scott is absent with the muscle injury sustained with England. Those goals have come unanswered. Marco Rose has added a defensive solidity not always present during Iraola’s era. Last season’s goal difference was +4. Djordje Petrovic has not conceded a goal since the 5-1 defeat at Chelsea on 10 October. “The Chelsea game was the moment we changed all momentum,” said Petrovic after beating Leeds. Rose has admitted testing opening weeks in the Premier League had altered perceptions to force a rethink. “Everyone in the team, starting from the attackers, is doing their job offensively and defensively,” he said. Since Stamford Bridge, commitment to the collective has paid impressive dividends. “If you have that intensity with the attackers, it gets easier,” said Petrovic. “We have a good group of players with quality and huge rotations in each position.” JB

5 Lavia’s potential on show at last

Roméo Lavia completed his first 90 minutes as a Chelsea player during their Carabao Cup defeat by Liverpool last Wednesday. It was a major milestone for a player who has struggled to stay fit since joining from Southampton three years ago. Lavia’s injury record invites caution but the midfielder is making progress. He followed up his performance against Liverpool with his second consecutive 90-minute display when Chelsea beat Manchester United 2-0 on Saturday. “As long as I feel good, I’ll do everything possible to help the team to get this type of result and I’m feeling good, so I’m very happy with my performance,” Lavia said after starring against United and creating the opening goal for Morgan Rogers. “All I can say is that the work that we’re doing with all the people at the club is going well. It’s just about keeping it going. Hopefully it can continue this way.” Jacob Steinberg

6 Rising star Williams-Barnett gets chance

With Tottenham cruising towards a third successive Premier League victory, against 10-man Crystal Palace, Roberto De Zerbi decided the time had come in the 88th minute. Luca Williams-Barnett is rated as one of the best prospects to emerge from the Spurs academy in many years but the attacking midfielder has had to be patient for his first league appearance as De Zerbi’s side struggled at the start of the season. The 18-year-old made an instant impression with a sensational first touch and pass after replacing Mathys Tel before setting up Mohammed Kudus for a great chance, to make it 3-0, that was spurned. We can expect to see more of him if De Zerbi gets his way. “My career is clear: when I have young, talented players, nothing changes,” he said. “I thought it was the right moment for him in the Premier League – but as a quality, he’s a big, big talent.” Ed Aarons

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

7 Hürzeler’s ‘connections’ keep Seagulls flying

After Fabian Hürzeler masterminded Brighton’s fine 1-0 win at Manchester City that lifted the Seagulls to 19 points, only two behind their hosts, the manager pointed to the culture he is building. “For me, I think it’s a lot about connection. We work in the people business. And we speak a lot about players. But for me, it’s more important to understand the person behind the player. And therefore, we try to build a lot on connection. We try to build a lot on culture. Because I think having the right values, having the right connection, the right relationship between the players helps you massively on the pitch. On the pitch, they need to rely on each other, trust each other. And you can only build this on and off the pitch. And therefore, we try to emphasise this a lot.” Jamie Jackson

8 Igor Thiago shows signs of best form

The oddity about Brentford this season is that they’re playing well, have a very good chance of qualifying for Europe for the first time in their history, and yet there’s been a feeling that they’ve been leaving points behind. Inexplicably, victory over Nottingham Forest was their first win in five and their first clean sheet since the 3-0 demolition of Chelsea six weeks ago. Perhaps the biggest issue in terms of improving on last season’s ninth-placed finish was whether Igor Thiago could match his tally of 22 goals. He’s started this campaign slowly, but got his second of the season with Brentford’s second against Forest. The finish, which looped in off Nikola Milenkovic, was fortuitous and not entirely convincing, but more significant perhaps was the way he stepped back away from the defenders, creating space for Jaidon Anthony to pick him out. That instinct will always generate chances, and the finishing will surely return. Jonathan Wilson

9 Enciso can be key in fight to survive

The word at Ipswich is that Julio Enciso has come back to the club with an increased level of maturity after a year in Ligue 1. He occasionally sparkled at Portman Road on loan from Brighton in the second half of the doomed 2024-25 season but lacked consistency. This season he already has two goals, a pair of assists and has become Ipswich’s chief creator. Enciso is comfortably top of the club’s chances-created chart, the Paraguayan’s tally of 14 is nearly double the next names on the list – Sasa Lukic, Emersonn and Abdul Fatawu, who have eight apiece. After the Tractor Boys had managed to turn a 1-0 lead into a 2-1 deficit at Hull, Enciso’s thwack from the edge of the box earned his side a vital point. He will be required to keep producing these kinds of moments if Gary O’Neil’s side are to do what they couldn’t last time around and stay in the top flight for consecutive seasons. Tom Bassam

10 Coventry take big step at Sunderland’s expense

Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s head coach, said post-match: “First year in Europe, you will have on average 10 less points. It’s our reality.” The reality is Sunderland have 12 points fewer than they did after nine games last season and if you extrapolate their current form over 38 games it amounts to relegation. Only Crystal Palace have conceded more goals and only Nottingham Forest have scored fewer. It would stun no one to learn that those three clubs make up the bottom three, but what is a surprise is that three promoted sides are all looking capable of avoiding the drop. A word for Coventry, who have responded to a chastening start to the season by winning three of their past five. Beating the teams around you is important in the fight for survival and this was a big tick in that box. TB

Sports.title: Liverpool’s work in progress fizzles out in the face of streetwise champions | Andy Hunter
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola had swatted aside any question that veered in the direction of Liverpool’s title credentials during his press conference on Friday with two simple words. “Too early,” he would respond. The Liverpool head coach was dismissive in terms of the stage of the season but, as Arsenal doggedly demonstrated, too early also applies to the development of his team.

Arsenal cavorted to the sound of fury at Anfield. At the final whistle Mikel Arteta leapt into the arms of the first-team coach Gabriel Heinze as he celebrated the release of his first win at Liverpool as Arsenal manager, his club’s first league victory at Anfield in 14 years and the champions moving three points clear at the top of the table. His players, tireless in the protection of Kai Havertz’s early winner, lined up to accept the acclaim from a jubilant away section. Anger filled the space around them.

From Virgil van Dijk collecting a post-match booking for sarcastically applauding the referee, Andy Madley, to the jeers of the home crowd, enraged by the match officials and most of all by Arsenal’s streetwise tactics/shithousery (delete as appropriate), this was an infuriating evening for a team that had arrived with momentum and amid talk of a potential title challenge. There was only applause for Liverpool’s players as they left the pitch in recognition of their effort and misfortune.

The hosts should have had a penalty for Jurriën Timber tugging Alexander Isak’s shirt and preventing him from connecting with a Bradley Barcola cross. Florian Wirtz struck the crossbar during Liverpool’s brightest spell and Alexis Mac Allister squandered a free header from 10 yards out. But as the second half ticked by and Arsenal absorbed the pressure, with Gabriel Magalhães and Declan Rice to the fore, belief in Liverpool’s powers of recovery faded.

There was no clearer sign of an expensively assembled team running out of ideas than Van Dijk operating as a makeshift centre‑forward in the final exchanges. He had Isak, Barcola and the substitutes Lewis Koumas, Victor Muñoz and Rio Ngumoha in support. Ngumoha had an impact but, ultimately, Liverpool’s varied forward line did not. For the first time in 16 years Liverpool failed to register a shot on target in a Premier League game.

Iraola’s complaint about Liverpool’s two defeats this season both turning on contentious refereeing decisions was valid. But he ended that particular discussion with a telling point. “I think it’s a penalty but we need to think about what we can improve to be on the right side of these big games,” Iraola admitted.

View image in fullscreen Trey Nyoni impressed after Andoni Iraola handed him a first Premier League start. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

Another slow start cost Liverpool but they also lacked the penetration and the defensive might that underpinned Arsenal’s win. That will come in time under Iraola. In the meantime, there will be harsh lessons to occasionally absorb.

The Liverpool head coach again showed he is prepared to trust and reward young talent by handing a first start in the Premier League to Trey Nyoni. It was a bold call from Iraola, with Ryan Gravenberch dropped to the bench alongside the fit-again Dominik Szoboszlai to accommodate the 19-year-old, but one based on merit. Nyoni impressed Iraola from the moment he walked into the club this summer and stepped up a level on Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US. The debut had been coming, and there was added weight to the vote of confidence that it should come against such formidable opposition.

Nyoni made his presence felt immediately. One reservation over the midfielder’s inclusion against a midfield of Rice, Bruno Guimarães and Martin Ødegaard was whether he had the physicality to compete. After merely 49 seconds he left Ødegaard in a heap to concede the game’s first free-kick. In the 10th minute he caught Havertz’s ankle with a late challenge and was perhaps fortunate to avoid the game’s first booking.

Nyoni’s timing was more accurate, his speed and strength clear, when beating Ødegaard convincingly in a 50‑50 challenge as they closed in on a David Raya throw. Arsenal rightly survived a video assistant referee’s check for a penalty against Christos Tzolis in the spell of pressure that followed Nyoni’s intervention.

The youngster’s composure on the ball and intelligent reading of the game were the most encouraging aspects of his full league debut. What worked against Nyoni, however, was Liverpool’s need to chase the game from as early as the 16th minute. Iraola needed attacking aggression and chaos in the final third more than the teenager’s defensive protection and patient buildup play. It was a reflection of the circumstances, not Nyoni’s own contribution, when he was replaced by Szoboszlai in the 59th minute.

There was chaos but no clarity to Liverpool’s performance in the final third, however. Despite the anguish over the antics of Gabriel, Havertz and the performance of Madley, there was a gap between the champions and potential contenders. Too early, as Iraola would say. But give it time.

Sports.title: Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts?  | Andrew Beasley
Sports.content:
No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change.

The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.

Michael Carrick remains the favourite to be the next manager to leave his post. He is unsurprisingly followed by the managers of the clubs who occupy the relegation zone: Pierre Sage of Crystal Palace, Sunderland’s Régis Le Bris and Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest. It seems almost inevitable that Carrick will leave soon so the more interesting analysis lies among the bottom three.

Sunderland sit 20th and are predicted by Opta to finish there. However, they have had a testing start to the season. Le Bris’s side have faced five of the current top seven clubs, the joint-most along with Liverpool. The manager also has enormous reserves of goodwill after taking the club back to the Premier League and then into Europe.

Despite their tough schedule, Sunderland came into the weekend within one expected point of Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham before losing 3-1 at Coventry with the xG count 1.8 to 0.7 in their favour. It was a familiar outcome for a side that has scored 6.2 goals fewer than expected this season.

With Sunderland’s next five league opponents being Chelsea, Aston Villa, Tottenham, Liverpool and Newcastle, the challenge of staying up will not immediately get easier. At least their chance‑converting woes are not as bad as those of Nottingham Forest.

Their shots have been worth 14.7 expected goals, the fourth most in the division after the matches on Saturday. But not once in a game this season have the goals they scored at least equalled their xG, let alone surpassed it. It is a finishing issue, not a question of opposition goalkeepers having super-human performances against them.

The analytical step above standard expected goals is xG on target (xGOT). It measures the likelihood of an on-target shot becoming a goal based on chance quality and shot placement. Forest’s xGOT this season is 7.4, little more than half of their expected goal tally.

This inability to test goalkeepers severely enough explains why Glasner’s men have scored just six times. They are squandering almost one goal per game on average according to their expected goals, a significant shortfall. None of the 96 teams in Europe’s big five leagues were worse than 0.5 goals per match below xG last season, which suggests Forest’s luck should turn for the better.

Is Evangelos Marinakis patient enough for that to happen? Forest’s expected goal data is much stronger for Glasner than it was under any of the four managers their owner fired last season. Whether he pays attention to such numbers is a different issue.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Glasner hinted at a physical deficiency in the squad after defeat at Brentford. “We are outrun by the opposition in every single game. We have to change it,” he said. Distance covered data from Fotmob suggests that is not quite the case, albeit Forest have been outrun in their past five league games. Both the underlying xG data and physical statistics are worse at Glasner’s former club Crystal Palace though.

As expected goals have a far greater bearing on future performance or results than running stats, those numbers are the greater concern. Equally, Palace’s average of 96.9 sprints per match is the fewest in the Premier League (after Saturday’s matches).

The club have been through similar teething troubles with new managers before. Palace’s previous two appointments that occurred between seasons were Frank de Boer and Patrick Vieira. The former was sacked after only five matches in all competitions in 2017, the latter won just one of his first nine league games four years later before recovering to finish 12th.

While Palace are a little wasteful in attack, they have not been as bad as Forest or Sunderland. Their defence is a much bigger problem, which is unusual as Sage’s Lens conceded the fourth fewest expected goals in Ligue 1 last season. Palace are second worst for that metric in the Premier League in 2026‑27, rock bottom if penalties are excluded. Some of that may be down to starting seven combinations of players in the back three because of injuries and Axel Disasi’s three‑match ban, but it is imperative that a manager overcomes such inevitable difficulties.

Palace host Liverpool next weekend. They return after the international break with potentially winnable games against Coventry and Hull. Will those fixtures represent a good opportunity for Sage to kickstart his reign or an excellent chance for his replacement to hit the ground running? Only the chair, Steve Parish, will know the answer but Palace are the strugglers who look most in need of managerial change.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick to stay in charge of Manchester United for Roma game
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is poised to remain in charge of Manchester United for the Champions League game against Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday.

United have not won in nine games and have made their poorest start to a season since 1988, but Carrick’s position is expected to be reviewed again during the international break after the next round of Premier League matches, in which United host Aston Villa next Sunday.

The 45-year-old head coach came close to losing his job last Monday when Jason Wilcox and Omar ­Berrada met at the training ground to discuss his future. The director of football and the chief executive decided ­Carrick should be given a chance to turn form and results around.

Manchester United fans on Michael Carrick and the club after the defeat at Chelsea.

Carrick’s side are in 17th with seven points, above the relegation zone only on goal difference.

There remains a view within the hierarchy that Carrick can still transform fortunes, with United’s travelling support still backing him at the end of the defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. After the game the head coach indicated that he expected to still be in position for the Roma match. He said: “We’ve got to move forward and win matches, it’s as simple as that.”

Eddie Howe is Wilcox’s preferred candidate should Carrick be sacked, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle manager is open to taking up the position, subject to negotiations. He would cost about £3m in compensation to Newcastle.

Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.

Sports.title: Boy hands himself into police after Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland match
Sports.content:
A 14-year-old boy has “handed himself in” to West Midlands police after a video posted on social media appeared to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland with a photo of Bradley Lowery during the Premier League match on Saturday.

Sunderland fan Bradley captured the hearts of the football world when he was diagnosed with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer. He died aged six in 2017.

Coventry said on Sunday that they were investigating the video footage and Bradley’s mother, Gemma, issued an emotional statement through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children.

West Midlands police said: “We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City’s Premier League match with Sunderland [on Saturday] afternoon.

“A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course. We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim’s family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.”

Coventry said in their earlier statement: “Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.”

Gemma Lowery said her “beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate” in her statement. She posted on Instagram: “Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

“I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between.

“So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?”

Lowery added: “I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t, just for him to learn from this.

“Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.”

Sports.title: European football: Mbappé penalty helps Real Madrid stroll to sixth straight win
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.

The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.

Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomandé were also on target to keep third-placed Madrid within three points of the La Liga leaders, Barcelona, who thrashed Alavés 6-1 on Saturday.

José Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind Atlético Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.

Real Sociedad’s four-match winning run came to an end after they lost 2-1 to Athletic Bilbao thanks to first-half goals from Inaki Williams and Alex Berenguer, who scored a penalty.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points.

Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M’Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win.

Como moved back into the top four as they eked out a 1-0 victory at home over bottom side Venezia on Sunday for a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions.

The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. The Como captain, Lucas Da Cunha, converted in the 43rd minute for the French international’s first goal of the season. “This is the type of match we found hard to win last season,” Da Cunha told DAZN.

Second-half goals from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga ensured Juventus returned to winning ways with a 2-0 victory over 10-man Napoli, who had Luca Marianucci sent off in the second half as they slipped to their fourth defeat of the campaign.

Lyon and Paris FC both won to close in on the defending Ligue 1 champions, Paris Saint-Germain, with the capital team defeating Monaco 3-1.

View image in fullscreen Lyon’s Corentin Tolisso embraces coach Paulo Fonseca after scoring the second goal against Angers. Photograph: Manon Cruz/Reuters

Lyon won 2-0 at home to Angers with goals in each half from Ernest Nuamah and Corentin Tolisso, as they bounced back from a 2-0 defeat away to PSG last time out.

The seven-time French title winners are third in the table, three points behind PSG and one behind second-placed Lille. Lyon’s win came amid reports that their coach, Paulo Fonseca, is close to leaving the club to return to his native Portugal.

“I know that I will be with the players tomorrow morning but beyond that it is hard to say,” Fonseca, who was in tears as he embraced his backroom staff at the end of the game, told reporters. Fonseca is reportedly a target for Sporting, whose coach Rui Borges is under pressure.

Paris FC are fourth after getting the better of Monaco at the Stade Jean-Bouin. Lassine Sinayoko, the Malian international forward, scored twice late in the first half for Paris FC before Folarin Balogun pulled one back on 65 minutes.

Sports.title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller
Sports.content:
Goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City to escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter with London City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to before kick-off.

The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been impressive.

Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City manager, praised the ability of his team to win in different ways as needed, after three games in eight days. “We said afterwards, the players should be so proud of what they put into this game,” he said.

“We’ve learned we’re a great team who can keep the ball for 75% of the game and win that way, or we can win like this. That quality to win in different ways is good to have, but the players also have to adapt to that and feel it’s OK to not have the ball all the time, take pride in defending and only having three or four chances but finishing off those chances.”

Before kick-off, cameras showed London City’s superstar summer signing Alexia Putellas opening the boot of her car and taking out a heavy leather-clad square item, her third Ballon d’Or safely encased inside. The Spain midfielder did not present her trophy to fans in the stands before kick-off, instead choosing to put it on display so supporters could queue to have their photo taken with it.

The only nod to the player’s stunning individual year, in which she won the quadruple with Barcelona before joining London City, was on her feet, the geometric gold on her custom Ballon d’Or-themed boots glinting on their first outing.

There have been jokes aplenty about the unlikelihood of the world’s premier individual award heading to its new Bromley home. To reach the stadium from Hayes Lane, you pass a field of horses on your left. London City Lionesses are not Barcelona, and they have become the home of the Ballon d’Or winner by default rather than being the key component of that individual success.

Except, based on the season London City are having and the ruthless ambitions of the owner, Michelle Kang, the idea that the club could produce a season that delivers them collective success and individual success off the back of it feels less distant than it did just a few short months ago.

Against the champions, London City more than held their own, the opportunity to move level on points with their opponents and league leaders Chelsea an inviting incentive. Their threat was evident within 30 seconds, when the Manchester City defender Rebecca Knaak was forced to turn Lucía Corrales’s cross wide of the far post just ahead of a waiting Isobel Goodwin.

Neither team has impressed defensively this season, each only managing to keep one clean sheet in the Women’s Super League, and it made for a thrilling encounter, the high lines and aggressiveness of both attacks delivering a showstopper.

Making her first WSL start for the home team, with Elene Lete hitherto preferred, Mary Earps made a huge statement with an impressive double save from a Knaak header to keep the game goalless going into the break.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Mary Earps dives at the feet of Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

City broke the deadlock despite London City dominating and it was their most influential player who delivered. Hemp flicked the ball into the run of Shaw and with her first touch, she took it past Earps before she switched the ball on to her right foot and fired in to become just the third player to score in eight consecutive WSL starts.

A deserved equaliser arrived in the 72nd minute, when Fernández was at the near post to meet a corner and her assured header sent the ball looping in at the back post.

The celebrations were emphatic but they were short-lived. This is a new, more resilient Manchester City, one that survived various scares last term to secure a second WSL title, and they re-established their lead two minutes later, when Hemp stretched out a leg to poke in Mary Fowler’s cross from the right to secure the win.

That London City could feel aggrieved at having not taken something from the game was a testament to their performance and how quickly progress is being made. The home team had 23 shots to City’s seven and 52 touches in the opposition box to City’s 13, but critically the visiting team were clinical when it mattered. Converting two of their three efforts on target and showing the edge needed to battle at the top.

Sports.title: WSL roundup: Arsenal stall despite Russo strike; Chelsea’s James suffers injury
Sports.content:
One shot, on target and in the back of the net, was all it took for Aston Villa to reopen the wound that Arsenal had been carefully trying to stitch back up.

Despite almost 65% possession, 28 shots to one, and 56 touches in the opposition box to four, Alessia Russo’s 85th-minute goal meant Arsenal were only able to salvage a point against Villa after back-to-back wins in the league and Champions League had appeared to have kickstarted their season.

The worst possible scenario for a team that has struggled against low blocks arrived in the 25th minute, when Lynn Wilms found Chasity Grant, who fired low into the bottom corner. It was a hammer blow to the home team, with Villa knowing exactly what to do next: stick 11 players behind the ball and frustrate the Gunners.

Russo’s late goal spared Arsenal’s blushes a little, the forward flicking a header in at the far post from a Stina Blackstenius cross, but the reprieve delivered by Arsenal’s victories over Tottenham and Benfica has been rolled back.

The Gunners have an incredibly tricky run of fixtures coming up, with Liverpool away followed by Barcelona, London City and then Lyonnes. And, despite the back-to-back wins, they haven’t been able to resolve the problems in the final third that have plagued every performance.

The pressure will be back on head coach Renée Slegers and there are questions to be asked about some decision making. However, with similar problems present under Joe Montemurro and Jonas Eidevall before her, maybe it’s time to look beyond the head coach.

Elsewhere Lauren James was forced off with an injury in the first half of Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton. The England forward was replaced by Erin Cuthbert in the 35th minute with the away team 4-0 up. There were five different goalscorers with Melvine Malard getting two. The coach, Sonia Bompastor, said: “It is too soon [to know] about Lauren’s injury. I spoke to her at half-time and it seems to be her hamstring so we will have to have a proper assessment tomorrow.”

Tottenham climbed to fourth in the table after a comprehensive 4-1 win at Birmingham City. The Spurs midfielder Drew Spence set a new all-time WSL appearance record with 217 to move one above the former Chelsea defender Millie Bright. West Ham were also 4-1 winners, over Liverpool, in their third league win of the season, leapfrogging their opponents in the table to move up to 10th.

Annabel Blanchard gave Crystal Palace the lead at Brighton with a glorious long-range effort but the visitors could not hold on and strikes from Caitlin Hayes and Sophie Peskett completed the turnaround 2-1 win for Arturo Ruiz’s side. “I think that these three wins in a row will be key for the rest of the season and we are in a very good moment,” Ruiz told the club website. “And I think that we are showing what we want to do in terms of our energy. The first half was very good even though we conceded a goal.”

Sports.title: George Russell's 's***show' snub to title-winning team-mate: 'Distraught' Brit walks out on Kimi Antonelli's F1 celebrations - and takes a £4,000 fine
Sports.content:
A 'distraught' George Russell skipped Kimi Antonelli's immediate Formula One title celebrations after being let down by Mercedes during the Formula One Grand Prix.

And team principal Toto Wolff apologised to driver Russell for the 's***show' after he suffered yet another technical fault on a day of rejoicing for his junior team-mate.

Antonelli, aged 20 years and 68 days, became the youngest Formula One title-winner in history after finishing third at the Mexican GP, wrapping up the crown with four races to spare in his second full season.

Russell had the respect to congratulate Antonelli but did not hang around on the track or for his media duties, taking a £4,173 fine as a result.

The Englishman, who at 28 is still seeking a Drivers' Championship, started the day in second but an engine battery deployment failure saw him drop back to sixth. He also served a ten-second penalty for a collision with Isaac Hadjar. It felt like the story of his season in miniature.

'I saw George after the race on the FIA scales, and obviously he's distraught about the situation,' Wolff said.

George Russell was 'distraught' after Kimi Antonelli's title win after a season where everything has gone wrong for him, says Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff

Russell did congratulate Antonelli but did not hang around on track or for his interviews

'It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi.

'I have known George for such a long time. So, I saw him and thought, for a racing driver, this is a catastrophic moment.

'And maybe today the race was a little bit a picture of his season. This was a race for him to win. We had the pace in the car. And we let him down on the first straight. The energy delivery is not what we thought it should be.

'And so I'm very much with him at the moment. I've been in situations where it's very, very difficult to cope.

'So, him not doing the media work, or leaving the track, is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me.'

Russell entered the season as Mercedes' number one driver but it has not gone to plan and he is fourth in the drivers' standings, the joint-highest he has ever finished.

On a race-by-race basis, Russell has been bemoaning his car's performance.

He has suffered three Did Not Finishes this season – in Canada, Belgium, and Singapore – leading to a loss of 43 points based off where he was at the time of his retirement.

Antonelli became the youngest Formula One champion in history aged 20 years and 68 days

Russell was also the victim of a water leak and anti-stall in Hungary, another power unit issue in Malaysia, and further complications in China, Japan, and the United States.

In July Russell claimed he was feeling optimistic, feeling that the team had fixed his persistent engine issue, but he has been unable to achieve consistency since then.

'It's unfortunately happened too many times this season, and, yeah, this is just where we are,' he said after retiring from the Singapore GP while he was driving in third.

Further bad luck beset him in Monaco where, after being handed a five-second time penalty for pitlane speeding, a team miscommunication caused him to serve it incorrectly and he ended up with a ten-second dock, causing him to finish 12th.

Russell's bad fortune should not take away from the joy felt for Antonelli, whose father claims he was 'born in a garage' and has been practising simulators since the age of three.

'We did it! And without them, I wouldn't be here, without Mercedes, without my family,' he said.

'So, I'm very grateful for this moment, and it's one that will live forever. I'm speechless. I'm trying to process what just happened.

'This weekend I did feel a bit more tense, but I'm just so happy and happy that we got it done, and then we can now we can enjoy the rest of the season.'

Lewis Hamilton finished second on Sunday and said: 'A huge congratulations to Kimi and the Mercedes team. It's great to see them all up here celebrating their success. Youngest world champion ever. It's pretty phenomenal, and I'm so grateful to be in the race to witness it.'

Max Verstappen, who finished third, added: 'What a season he had, and you know, to do that also at such an age, I think it's just really, really impressive

'It's amazing to see the whole team, of course, celebrating with him, his family is here as well. So, I'm sure this is a very emotional day for him, and I'm very proud of him.'

Sports.title: Fuming Lewis Hamilton questions Charles Leclerc's mentality and demands 'serious talks' with Ferrari after Mexican Grand Prix clash
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has declared Ferrari need 'serious talks' behind the scenes after claiming the team had 'big problems' following a first lap incident with team-mate Charles Leclerc at the Mexican Grand Prix.

Hamilton had sat on pole in Mexico but battled with Leclerc on the first four corners of Sunday's Grand Prix.

Leclerc would ultimately seize the lead from Hamilton by running across the grass at turn four, while Hamilton was also passed by Red Bull's Max Verstappen following his team-mate's attack.

Leclerc was then hit with a five second penalty for his actions, enabling Verstappen to seize the lead in the Grand Prix.

A furious Hamilton was heard saying 'We've got big problems, big, big problems' over his team radio during a red-flag period in the race caused by a crash for Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac.

Hamilton passed Leclerc to claim second following the restart of the race, but ultimately was forced to settle for second place behind Verstappen.

A furious Lewis Hamilton insisted Ferrari needed to have 'serious talks' after the Mexican Grand Prix

Hamilton was angered by a move from Charles Leclerc on the fourth corner of the race, which he believes cost Ferrari the race

The British star claimed following the race that 'serious talks' were needed as he insisted Leclerc's actions had cost Ferrari victory in Mexico.

'We have to have some serious talks behind the scenes for sure,' Hamilton said, who had complained on team radio that Leclerc had only received a five-second penalty.

'I think the core thing to remember, which maybe comes with age, is that every decision you make in the car impacts all the people that work in the background for the whole team.

'Working as a team is a part of our job and a part of our contract. We could have easily done that today.

'This will just continue unless action is taken, unless a real deep, serious conversation is had. So, it shouldn't happen moving forward.

'Of course, the frustrations… today I'm happy because this guy [Kimi Antonelli] just won the championship and on the other side, I'm really p***ed.'

The seven-time world champion renewed his call for 'rules of engagement' with his Ferrari team-mate, having previously come together with Leclerc at the Italian Grand Prix.

Hamilton questioned Leclerc's move as being a 'mentality thing' and insisted that 'something needs to change'.

'When your team-mate works against you and then you lose positions like that, it's definitely tough,' Hamilton said.

Hamilton questioned the mentality of his Ferrari team-mate following the first lap incident

Leclerc claimed he considred giving position back to Hamilton, but the British star had already been passed by Max Verstappen

'We don't have rules of engagement, and whether or not that will change anything from Charles' side, I don't know. Something needs to change for sure.

'Before I joined this team, when I was at Mercedes, I watched the back and forth between Charles and Carlos (Sainz), where they were battling so much that the person ahead just pulled away.

'But it is one thing when that's happening in fourth and fifth, as opposed to first and second, and you lose the win. That's significant.

'The guy (Leclerc) is 28 years old, so I don't think it's an age thing. I think it's a mentality thing. It's like, "Do or die. Either I win or none of us do", and it shouldn't be that.

'It should be us getting that one-two. You know, Silverstone, I could have gone all kamikaze on him and taken him off and lost us the win.'

When asked about Hamilton's comments, Leclerc insisted he had considered giving the position back to his team-mate, but the British driver had already been passed by Verstappen.

'I'm sure Lewis definitely hated those first few laps and we'll discuss,' Leclerc said.

Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur admitted his frustration at how the race had played out for the team, adding he would need to speak to both of his drivers following their comments.

Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur admitted he would need to speak to both of his drivers following their comments

'I think it's just a matter of respect,' Vasseur told Sky Sports.

'The respect for the brand, for the sponsors, for the team, for the 2,000 people working at home like hell. Honestly, it's difficult to digest for me to give up a win like this.

'The comments of Lewis I will discuss with Lewis and the comments of Charles I will discuss with Charles.'

Verstappen's victory in Mexico saw him move above Hamilton into second place in the drivers' championship.

Mercedes star Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion on Sunday after finishing third.

Sports.title: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Who put in the 'complete' performance? Who disappointed once again in a big game? And who barely put a foot wrong in Anfield bearpit?
Sports.content:
Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Who put in the 'complete' performance? Who disappointed once again in a big game? And who barely put a foot wrong in Anfield bearpit?

Arsenal's miserly defence thwarted Liverpool at Anfield to send the Premier League champions three points clear at the top.

Kai Havertz tapped in the winner from a fine Arsenal move 16 minutes in, with Alexis Mac Allister spurning Liverpool's best chance to equalise before the break.

Wave after wave of attack from the home side came and went in the second period, although Andoni Iraola's men were unable to conjure many clear-cut chances, and they failed to have a single shot on target.

The Gunners took advantage of Man City's defeat by Brighton on Saturday and now have clear water between themselves and the chasing pack.

So who shone the most on an attritional and potentially pivotal afternoon in the title race?

Daily Mail Sport's LEWIS STEELE and ISAAN KHAN were in position at Anfield to run the rule over both sides...

Ezri Konsa (left) and Gabriel Magalhaes (right) were at the heart of Arsenal's resilient win

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1):

Alisson - 6/10

A loose pass cost Liverpool and led directly to Arsenal’s goal but he made a phenomenal save on 73 minutes to deny Christos Tzolis.

Ronald Araujo - 5

Could he have done better to keep track of Kai Havertz for the winning goal? The German ghosted in at Araujo’s back post.

Jeremy Jacquet - 6

A few heavy touches early doors but the youngster settled in and made some important tackles.

Virgil van Dijk - 6

Made a last-ditch intervention on 71 minutes to prevent what looked certain to be Arsenal's second goal.

Milos Kerkez - 6 (Booked)

Threatened more than usual going forward and nearly had an assist, but a bad Alexis Mac Allister header flew over when he should have done far better.

Trey Nyoni - 6

Two fouls were lucky to go unpunished in the opening stages but Nyoni, on his first league start, soon settled and started to dictate from deep.

Trey Nyoni made a shaky start for the Reds but quickly found his composure

Alexis Mac Allister - 7 (Booked)

Had Liverpool’s best chance when unmarked in the box and the Argentine usually gobbles up those chances. Was Liverpool’s sharpest player.

Cody Gakpo - 5

Did an important defensive shift up against wildcard left-back Riccardo Calafiori, who is everywhere, but Gakpo did not offer enough threat the other way.

Florian Wirtz - 5

Another big game where fans would have wanted more. Some nice moments but he made the wrong decision too often.

Bradley Barcola - 7 (Booked)

Had a big opening just after Arsenal’s goal to make it 1-1 but a heavy touch let him down. Was Liverpool’s most dangerous asset in the first half, then looked tired late on.

Bradley Barcola was the most dangerous Liverpool attacker but fatigue set in

Alexander Isak - 5

His honesty came back to bite him when he did not throw himself to ground in a first-half penalty shout. Did not impact proceedings enough otherwise.

Lewis Koumas (for Wirtz, 81min)

Manager:

His attackers got into dangerous positions but could not finish their dinner.

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1):

David Raya: 7

Accurate, fast distribution when under pressure from the Liverpool frontline. Consistently set Arsenal away on counter-attacks.

Jurrien Timber: 6

Looked overwhelmed at times and didn’t get forward as much as he’d have liked. Still, played his part in keeping the cleansheet.

Ezri Konsa: 8

Bailed out by Declan Rice for his errant pass on 18 minutes. After that, he barely put a foot wrong. Found himself in the right place at the right time defensively.

Konsa defended brilliantly, seen here shielding the ball from Alexander Isak

Gabriel: 7

Up for the fight in the bearpit atmosphere that is Anfield. Strong aerially and stayed switched on for darting runs of Isak.

Riccardo Calafiori: 8

A handful both in attack and defence. Made menacing runs into final third which the opposition found tricky to track.

Declan Rice: 9 (Man of the Match)

A complete, domineering display typified by a desire to break into attacking areas and clean up in midfield. Excellent cross to assist Havertz.

Declan Rice celebrates the first Arsenal win at Anfield in 14 years after full time

Bruno Guimaraes: 6

Aggressive in tackles and pressing. His wild scream towards the Anfield crowd after tackling Barcola set the tone. Yet the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly brought more control.

Noni Madueke: 7

Has now strung together a few promising displays after facing scrutiny. Direct and kept looking to take on Kerkez.

Led the press, which led to Havertz's goal. Tireless and his will didn’t peter, even when Liverpool enjoyed much possession.

Christos Tzolis: 6

Good effort by the Greek to accelerate his return to Arsenal’s squad after his injury woes. Curling effort on 73 minutes required a fantastic save.

Christos Tzolis looked on in disbelief after Alisson saved brilliantly from his effort

Kai Havertz: 7

Simple finish from Rice’s excellent cross. Did his best to hold play up when in possession. Put in a vigorous shift off the ball.

Arsenal win at Anfield for the first time in 14 years, and they kept a clean sheet. An excellent day’s work.

Sports.title: Liverpool's anonymous attackers cost them the chance of beating Arsenal despite dominant display... the gap to the champions is narrowing - but the Reds still aren't close enough, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
As disheartened fans spilled out of Anfield, nearly all conversations were about the referee and questions over why he did not point to the penalty spot in the first half when Jurrien Timber pulled back Alexander Isak.

They had a point and this game would have been completely different had Andy Madley – or VAR Stuart Attwell – seen what everyone else saw when Isak was an inch short of connecting with a header and possible goal because he was pulled back by his marker.

It was a similar situation to Liverpool’s only other defeat under new boss Andoni Iraola, where supporters were left aggrieved at the incorrect call to send off Ryan Gravenberch against Manchester City.

In both cases they were unlucky to be on the wrong side of refereeing mistakes and would have cursed the fine margins. But in both cases Reds fans will also realise their team just did not do enough to win too.

Just like against City, Liverpool dominated Arsenal for large parts of this match. It felt as though they were one magic moment or opposition mistake away from scoring and lfiting off the Anfield roof.

But in both cases, that moment never materialised. It felt like the Liverpool attackers were looking around waiting for somebody else to step up and be the man to start the pendulum swinging in Liverpool’s favour.

Alexander Isak and Liverpool's attackers struggled against Arsenal's defence

They had zero shots on target, according to Opta, and that is the only statistic that Iraola will be mulling over in the coming days.

Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have all been frighteningly good in recent weeks but in this game, especially the second half, Liverpool’s big-money forwards looked like they had run out of ideas.

Arsenal defended like their lives depended on it and their away fans, who barely saw the ball down their end of the pitch after half-time, celebrated every Gabriel header or David Raya catch like a goal.

The home team, meanwhile, were left throwing long balls forward to Virgil van Dijk – the only player who could aerially compete with Arsenal’s team of giants. It felt like several Hail Mary passes but no one could answer Iraola’s prayers.

Liverpool’s two defeats to City and now Arsenal both demonstrate the gap between Iraola’s outfit and a genuine title contender. There is definitely a small level between Liverpool and Arsenal – but Reds fans can take solace in knowing it is not a chasm like last season.

A referee decision here, a better final ball there and Liverpool may be still unbeaten under Iraola and the whole country would consider them a title contender.

Iraola has closed the gap on the top teams but knows several tweaks are still needed to take that next step. Can they do it this season? It is far from impossible but seems a tall order.

The upcoming fixture list is kinder to them, at least. Of the current top eight, Liverpool have played all of them – two in the Carabao Cup – and won each test apart from City and Arsenal. The next two league games are against teams in 18th and 17th.

Florian Wirtz has improved recently but was unable to provide cutting edge on Sunday

But right now, Liverpool are a team with too many ‘ifs’, ‘buts’ and ‘maybes’. If Alexis Mac Allister did not get under a first-half header that looked like a certain goal… if the referee had given a clear foul on Isak… if the forwards packed their shooting boots.

As it was, for all of the nail-biting moments for Mikel Arteta on the touchline as Liverpool had lots of the ball in the final third, his goalkeeper David Raya could have had a cigar in and read the papers for most of the second half.

That is what will bother Iraola the most.

As for being a complete team able to compete for the league title again, Liverpool seem so close yet so far.

Trey bien

Trey Nyoni made his first Premier League start and it will not be his last after he put in a solid shift.

Though he misplaced some passes and was probably lucky to escape an early yellow card after two late challenges, the 19-year-old presents Iraola with an interesting tactical quirk.

The Englishman always wants the ball and drops into the back line to start attacks, with a maturity beyond his years.

He sits deep which allows Alexis Mac Allister to play as more of a box-to-box midfielder, undoubtedly his best position.

So where does this leave Ryan Gravenberch, who spent the afternoon on the bench? Given the amount of games Liverpool have across competitions, the Dutchman will still play many minutes — but he is currently at risk of falling down the pecking order thanks to the exciting talent of Nyoni.

There is also a conversation to be had about how Liverpool’s balance and control was lost when Nyoni was replaced by Dominik Szoboszlai.

Trey Nyoni excelled for the Reds and helped the home side control the tempo

Another Wirtz no-show

Casual football fans who maybe only tune in for the big games have never seen Wirtz play well.

They must wonder what all the fuss is about.

The German has been on fine form in recent weeks but has been like a ghost — no Halloween pun intended — in the two biggest matches against City and Arsenal.

It is all well and good performing against teams like LASK in the Champions League but Wirtz, at £116million, was signed to make a difference in these blockbuster clashes.

Instead, his national team colleague Kai Havertz continued his record of impacting the games that really matter come May. How Wirtz could do with some of that killer instinct.

Sports.title: 'I have something unresolved': Ole Gunnar Solskjaer piles more pressure on old pal Michael Carrick as he says he WOULD manage Man United again - despite trying to back him to succeed
Sports.content:
Ole Gunnar Solskjaer has admitted that he would be interested in returning as Manchester United manager in the future as he has 'something unresolved'. Pressure is mounting on current head coach Michael Carrick as the Red Devils' dismal season continues to go from bad to worse. After losing 2-0 at Chelsea on Saturday afternoon, United sit 17th in the Premier League - only above 18th-placed Crystal Palace on goal difference and just two points ahead of bottom side Sunderland. Solskjaer has been in the Old Trafford hotseat before with his own path mirroring Carrick's from being an interim manager initially to becoming a permanent appointment. The Norwegian had Carrick among his backroom staff before he was sacked as United boss in November 2021. When Ruben Amorim was sacked in January, both were interviewed as interim successors before Carrick was chosen. And speaking about taking the reins at United in the future, Solskjaer revealed he would accept it. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (left) has revealed he would like to manage Manchester United in the future but backs current head coach Michael Carrick (right) to overturn the club's fortunes Pressure is growing on Carrick which increased following Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Chelsea Solskjaer was sacked as United manager in November 2021 after nearly three years in charge 'Going back to what has been is not always as good,' he told Norwegian outfit TV2. 'Yes, I had lined up [as Manchester United's interim manager last season], but I didn't think it would last longer than the summer. It was probably time for someone else to try. 'I also feel like I have something unresolved. Of course it would have been nice to have the opportunity again.' Elaborating further, Solskjaer was keen to stress that he is not looking to oust his former United team-mate and friend Carrick. 'If Michael does well for 10 years and decides to quit, and they ask me if I can take them for two months, of course I wouldn't say no. I've been at that club for 18-19 years, so it's part of the family. But it's not something I'm thinking about.' Despite growing scrutiny on Carrick, Solskjaer is adamant that the under-fire head coach can turn around the club's fortunes. 'Michael has what it takes to take that club forward. I think he's the right man. He understands the club, understands the fans and knows what's needed.' Proof will be in the pudding with Carrick preparing his side for Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma and then Sunday's Premier League encounter versus Aston Villa, both at Old Trafford, before the international break. Sports.title: Invincibles beware! Mikel Arteta might just be assembling Arsenal's greatest EVER defence, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Within seconds of the full-time whistle, Gabriel Heinze had lifted an elated Mikel Arteta off the turf. The Argentine knew why this result brought his colleague a certain catharsis, which had eluded him for over a decade. Arteta had previously opened up about the psychological difficulties of playing at Anfield, describing the experience akin to a cyclist suddenly running out of energy. A mental paralysis of sorts. The game in question was in February 2014, having experienced a 5-1 defeat as a Gunners player. Arsenal’s previous victory against Liverpool away dated back to September 2012, a 14-year wait to banish these demons which he was duly reminded of in Friday’s press conference and in the minutes before kick-off. Instead, it’s now getting scary for Arsenal’s Premier League title rivals. The prospect of Arteta's side opening up a gap from the chasing pack by Christmas is becoming a real possibility — and it’s all because of their defence. A William Saliba-less backline reducing the Reds to zero shots on target at Anfield is a moment worth digesting. Mikel Arteta and Gabriel Heinze jubilantly embrace as the final whistle blows at Anfield Arsenal ended their 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at Anfield with a superb display Winning on opposition territory after an abysmal record lasting over a decade is an achievement in itself. But to ensure a frontline featuring Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola aren't given so much as a sniff in front of goal is a further statement. For all the focus around the fragilities of their frontline — the weaknesses are still very much in the open, as seen by the shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town — it’s Arsenal’s defence which underpins everything. Since the start of last season, Arsenal have not lost a league game when leading the scoreline at half-time. Just like how Arsenal’s (previously) woeful record at Anfield would be used as a reminder, this statistic is a menacing one for future opponents. It raises the question: how does this backline compare to the best Premier League defences who came before them? If the team carry on in this vein towards a consecutive league title, the Arsenal Invincibles set-up from the historic 2003-04 season of Sol Campbell, Kolo Toure, Ashley Cole and Lauren, with Jens Lehmann in goal, could soon be superseded. The current collection of defenders, backed up by David Raya, create a defensive structure which is proving so hard to break down, even with the lack of a sole regular scorer in the side. Gabriel, despite his embarrassing attempt at pretending Isak struck him in the face yesterday, stayed strong in physical duels and didn’t relent in periods when Liverpool piled the pressure on. By the 42nd minute, the Reds had whipped in 17 crosses, many of which were cleared by Gabriel or Konsa. Riccardo Calafiori is a wonderfully-gifted footballer who finds himself in some unorthodox positions which are difficult to track. The Italian’s menacing runs inverting from the left flank caused Liverpool many a problem. Kai Havertz tapped home from a low cross early on to give Arsenal a crucial lead to defend Even Jurrien Timber, who didn’t have his best game in the final third, helped ensure solidity at right back up against Cody Gakpo. It’s Ezri Konsa, though, who reflects a shrewdness typifying Arsenal and Arteta. As soon as it emerged that Saliba would be sidelined for months with a back injury, a right-sided centre back became the priority. The 29-year-old has slotted in seamlessly and again shone against the Reds, mirroring the ‘blessed’ tattoo he has inscribed on his left hand. The versatile defender won 100 per cent of his ground duels, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances. He ranked No1 in all these categories yesterday. An Arteta team starts from a rock-solid base with multiple, versatile defenders, often at the cost of fewer frontline options (Arsenal struck just two more league goals than third-placed Manchester United last season, for example). It ultimately worked in the previous campaign, their defence propelling Arsenal to a first Premier League title in 22 years. Another title appears to be well on track. And: watch out Campbell and Co. The moniker for Arsenal’s best defence in modern history is at risk. GUNNERS GAINING FROM MIKEL'S RUTHLESS STREAK Arteta’s ruthlessness is well-documented. Just ask Aaron Ramsdale or Jakub Kiwior, who were eased out after being surplus to requirements in recent years. Or the cold treatment of Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Mesut Ozil earlier in the Spaniard’s reign over their behaviours. Arteta's ruthlessness with team selection is continuing to pay dividends for the Gunners The current squad is brimming with talent — and spades of uncertainty. Eberechi Eze performed well off the bench against Bayern Munich after Bukayo Saka’s thigh injury on 10 minutes, followed up by a start against Everton — and didn’t get a minute against Liverpool. While Viktor Gyokeres was given his first league start of the season against Everton, where he played well — only to be dropped for this match. As seen by Christos Tzolis’ dash to make yesterday’s squad ahead of schedule, influenced by Max Dowman’s three-match suspension, no one’s place is really secure. That makes for a truly competitive environment. HEINZE IS RAISING THE BAR The final word must rest with Heinze. The fiery serial-winner, drafted in by Arteta in July 2025, was always going to demand high standards and bring a ferocity which can turn some the wrong way. At Argentine side Newell’s Old Boys, for example, he would weigh the players twice a day. Heinze's arrival in July 2025 has added a steeliness to the defence and paid off in spades So the appointment was attached with risks, even if Arteta had grown close to his ex-team-mate from his Paris Saint-Germain. It’s turned out to be a clever addition, which has added a steeliness to the defence and paid off in spades. Sources say that Heinze, who has managed five teams, is well-respected by the players, but is also seen as someone who does not mince his words. They know he’s not here to mess around.
