Sports.title: Piastri loses points finish after 10-second penalty for Lindblad collision | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oscar Piastri has lost his points finish in the Mexican Grand Prix after the stewards penalised him for a collision.

The McLaren driver tangled with Arvid Lindblad while trying to overtake the Racing Bulls driver. The stewards issued the McLaren driver a 10-second time penalty which drops him from seventh place to 15th.

The stewards ruled Piastri was not entitled to be given racing room when he tried to pass Lindblad on the outside of the corner and could have avoided the collision.

“On the approach to turn one the driver of car 81 [Piastri] attempted an overtake on the outside of car 41 [Lindblad],” the stewards explained. “Car 81 was never fully alongside car 41 so was not able to claim the right to the corner.

“Through turn one, the driver of car 41 defended his position by releasing the brakes however [did] not force car 81 off the track, allowing racing room on the outside – which he is not required to do.

“The stewards determined that the collision could have been avoided if the driver of car 81 had moved further to the left after turn one, even if this involved leaving the track prior to turn two.”

Speaking before the stewards issued their decision Piastri said there was little he could have done to avoid the contact.

“I obviously need to look back at it more,” he said, “but from in the car, I went to go up the inside of turn one Arvid moved very late and so I kind of ended up on the outside because I was avoiding him. And then from that point onwards, I tried to go around the outside.

“He pushed me pretty wide and I was trying to back out and you where we made contact was well before the corner actually happened. So from my side of things I really didn’t have anywhere else to go.”

Sports.title: Social Media: Vettel congratulates Antonelli for breaking his record as youngest F1 champion | Brief
Sports.content:
Sebastian Vettel, who became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in 2010, sent his congratulation to Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who has taken the record from him.

“Only very few of us manage to achieve that, and nobody has done it as young as you. You are curious, you listen, you learn fast, you are fearless, your driving has been very clean and controlled, yet on the limit when it needed to be. You understood that you can only control what you can control. You have a unique drive, and we enjoy watching you.”

Vettel won his first world championship title in the final race of 2010. He went into the title-decider behind Fernando Alonso and Mark Webber in the standings, and came out on top in a stunning conclusion to the championship.

“When I won my first title, it all seemed to happen the moment I crossed the finish line,” said Vettel. “I was overwhelmed. I got out of the car and the world around me was racing at full speed. It was like a rush. It was impossible to reflect. I didn’t sleep properly for days, so be prepared.

“But I remember the feeling once it sank in, holding the world championship trophy in my hands and reading all the other champions’ names. I felt proud and satisfied.

“I realised the best part wasn’t crossing the line that decided the title. It was all the races that led up to it. It is never the one race that matters. It is all the races we do. Every race shapes us. And with all that’s about to happen in the coming weeks, I’m sure you will soon feel the drive to race again. As in the bigger picture, there’s still a race to win.

“Lastly, a piece of advice. Great achievements might change the way people look at you, but you don’t have to change the way you look at people. Now go on and enjoy it. Un abbraccio forte [a big hug], Sebastian. Ciao.”

Sports.title: Joshua Buatsi Chases Paper Crown Against Willy Hutchinson
Sports.content:
Joshua Buatsi claims he made the right call walking away from Dmitry Bivol. Picking up a vacant strap against Willy Hutchinson will not convince anyone he belongs with the division elite. Taking the long road to a world championship by beating an opponent you already handled proves very little.

Buatsi meets Hutchinson for the vacant WBC light heavyweight belt at Manchester AO Arena on November 7. David Benavidez moved up to cruiserweight, opening up the position. That handed Buatsi a lifeline after Callum Smith battered him. That defeat derailed his standing as a serious threat at 175 pounds.

The brutal three-fight stretch since 2024 has taken plenty out of Buatsi, and walking straight into a rematch with a spiteful puncher like Hutchinson right now is playing with fire.

At 33, Buatsi is not the fresh prospect who could rely on physical superiority to bail him out. The wear and tear is showing.

Buatsi told BoxingScene that the financial terms to face Bivol were unacceptable. He insisted he has zero regrets about passing up the Russian champion.

Boxers can argue over purse splits all day. The reality is that picking up a belt against Hutchinson will never replace the test Bivol presented. It will not recover the years Buatsi wasted playing it safe.

The British bronze medalist is running out of road. Securing a belt gives him leverage at the bargaining table, yet beating Hutchinson does not turn him into an elite light heavyweight.

Hutchinson knows Buatsi looks vulnerable. Buatsi dropped him twice in their first clash, but Smith exposed him soon after. Buatsi also looked ordinary squeaking past Zach Parker in a controversial verdict many observers scored the other way.

Hutchinson has a clear path to victory. He must keep the pressure on. He must stay active every minute of every round. He must stay off the floor.

Buatsi can defend his business decisions. Inside the ring this weekend, he needs a dominant display if he expects fans to take his championship status seriously.

Sports.title: Floyd Mayweather Says He’ll Fight Ryan Garcia After Tune-Up
Sports.content:
Floyd Mayweather talks like a clash with Ryan Garcia is already locked in, but booking an exhibition changes nothing about the massive financial hurdle standing in the way. Astronomical purse demands alone could easily sink the proposed meeting long before either man steps into training camp.

Mayweather revealed a December 19 exhibition in Bangkok against Matty “The Jedi” Floyd, labeling it direct preparation for Garcia. “This is a tune-up before me and Ryan Garcia lock up,” he posted on social media. That sounds remarkably assured for an event lacking confirmed financing, network backing, or official sanctioning.

Calling something a tune-up assumes the main event actually happens. To reach that point, a promoter or broadcast platform must risk immense guarantees to satisfy both camps. Mayweather always commands record paydays, while Garcia brings huge modern star power, meaning neither fighter will agree to participate on the cheap.

Finding someone willing to swallow that financial gamble is the ultimate test. Mayweather’s brand recognition does not automatically produce enough pay-per-view buyers to cover two staggering paydays. At 49, he is pitching pure nostalgia against an active champion, banking on younger viewers paying premium rates for an icon whose prime occurred a generation ago.

Ryan certainly draws attention by threatening Mayweather’s pristine 50-0 record, yet heavy online talk rarely guarantees profitable buys. Expensive novelty attractions frequently produce widespread discussion without translating into verified purchases at the box office.

The WBC welterweight belt introduces another complication. Even if Ryan holds the title, the sanctioning body still must officially approve Mayweather as a credible challenger. Handing a world title opportunity to an aging retiree whose recent outings have been soft exhibitions would invite intense public criticism. Mayweather’s name would be doing all the heavy lifting instead of genuine sporting merit.

Garcia wants a firm commitment for February 6, but that timeline remains just a vision without signed contracts, bank guarantees, and full sanctioning approval. Mayweather’s confidence alone cannot substitute for the actual business required to make it reality.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Owes Bektemir Melikuziev His Title Shot
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia owes Bektemir Melikuziev his next title defense, and his narrow escape against Nikita Zon gives the mandatory challenger plenty of confidence. Munguia already received permission to delay that obligation once. Looking elsewhere simply because the required fight feels risky should not be on the table.

Munguia retained his WBA super middleweight belt by unanimous decision against Zon in Riyadh, but a routine showcase quickly turned into survival mode. An uppercut staggered him in the sixth round, leaving an unheralded opponent inches away from wrecking the champion’s plans on the Canelo Alvarez card.

The Ring reports that a deal is set for Munguia to face Melikuziev in early 2027. That ought to settle any debate over what comes next. The WBA granted Munguia an exemption to squeeze in Zon; the man waiting patiently in line deserves his shot.

Diego Pacheco and Jermall Charlo have surfaced as potential backup plans if that agreement hits a snag. Both carry name recognition, but floating them ignores the central issue: the champion already used his free pass.

If talks collapse, context is important. A legitimate injury or an insurmountable contract dispute would need a close look. Sidestepping Melikuziev because the stylistic matchup feels uncomfortable, on the other hand, would look terrible. Sanctioning another detour would demand some serious answers from the sanctioning body.

Zon revealed exactly why the champion’s team might hesitate. Munguia landed heavy blows throughout the night, yet he left wide defensive lanes that nearly cost him everything. His appetite for firefights always delivers excitement, but it invites danger that a veteran titlist should know how to avoid.

Melikuziev brings an even trickier puzzle as a southpaw with serious power in his left hand. Munguia cannot afford to linger in the pocket after unloading combinations, where incoming fire arrives from sharper, unfamiliar angles. Getting caught in the transitions could easily recreate the sixth-round crisis he just barely survived.

A dedicated body attack could prove decisive for the challenger. If Munguia relies on movement to limit the exchanges, steady work to the ribs can take the air out of his legs. If he sits down on his punches, he enters a shootout with a heavy hitter built to exploit porous defense.

Munguia earned respect for weathering that sixth round storm and pulling away once Zon ran out of steam. That resilience won the night, but surviving a scare does not guarantee another puncher will run dry before closing the show.

Melikuziev has every reason to believe he walks away with the title. Munguia brings volume and championship seasoning, but his latest outing makes backing the underdog a very reasonable call. The champion got his delay; the next ring walk must fulfill the order.

Sports.title: Beating 40-Year-Old Usyk Won’t Buy David Benavidez Immortality
Sports.content:
David Benavidez might think beating Oleksandr Usyk punches his ticket to the Hall of Fame, but boxing fans will see right through it. Dragging a 40-year-old heavyweight down to 200 pounds gives him a famous scalp on his resume, not an automatic pass to greatness.

“I’m going to get [my respect] one way or another. Once I beat [Usyk], there’s no denying me my spot in the history books,” Benavidez claimed via Fight Hub TV.

That chip on his shoulder is blinding him to reality. Benavidez acts like everyone owes him adulation, but demanding respect while targeting a 40-year-old on a brutal weight drain is the exact definition of taking a shortcut.

Beating Usyk under these conditions proves nothing. Draining an older fighter down 20-plus pounds leaves him vulnerable, sluggish, and dry. When an elite volume puncher swarms a drained legend whose legs are gone by the fifth round, educated fans do not applaud. They write it off as an obvious cash-out mismatch.

History books remember who you conquered at their absolute peak. If Benavidez wants undisputed recognition, he has to run that exact fire line:

– Turn back Jai Opetaia at 200 pounds to settle who actually rules cruiserweight.

– Step into Daniel Dubois’ range and take flush heavyweight heat without blinking.

– Grind out Filip Hrgovic through grueling, foul-filled trench warfare.

– Risk getting sparked out by a vicious young phenom like Moses Itauma.

– Solve the tricky Cuban ring craft of Frank Sanchez without losing discipline.

That five-man run creates an untouchable resume. Beating an aged, depleted Usyk simply adds a famous name with an asterisk next to it. Until Benavidez trades the easy scalps for real danger, that chip on his shoulder is going to stay right where it is.

Before any of that happens, Benavidez has to get past WBC belt-holder Michal Cieslak on December 5 in Glendale with his WBA and WBO straps on the line.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Says Mbilli Blew Golden Chance Against Canelo
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley believes Christian Mbilli let the threat of Canelo Alvarez’s counters strip away his aggression Saturday night. His harshest criticism was that the pressure fighter stopped fighting like himself once he got in front of the Mexican star.

Rather than setting a grueling pace, Mbilli grew tentative. Bradley noticed a fighter second-guessing his offense out of dread for the incoming counters.

“He was scared to get countered. They came in with an entirely different game plan. He lost his identity last night,” Bradley said on his channel about Mbilli. “He lost his identity last night because Nelo was on a whole another level.”

Bradley praised Canelo’s defense for creating that doubt. He highlighted subtle head movement and shoulder rolls that defused punches, robbing Mbilli of the momentum he needed to let his hands go.

“That slowed down the pace. That discouraged that man even more,” Bradley said. “Mbilli didn’t look ferocious like he usually looks ferocious.”

Bradley even noticed shades of Terence Crawford in Canelo’s tactics. He pointed out the snappy combinations and strategic clinches, suggesting Canelo learned a few practical tricks from their meeting.

“You take something from each fight,” Bradley said. “Crawford tied his ass up when he had to, and Nelo finally tied somebody up. I could not believe it. Turned that pitbull into a poodle,” Bradley said.

Whether Mbilli chose to box off the back foot as a deliberate tactic remains an open question. Nothing from his corner confirmed it after the final bell, but the approach looked calculated rather than fearful.

Mbilli did not look terrified of getting hit. Instead, he looked like a fighter saddled with a flawed strategy, trying to outthink a master counterpuncher at his own game. The decision to abandon his trademark swarm left him stranded in no man’s land.

By the time Mbilli finally realized the mistake and started pressing inside, the fight had already slipped away. Giving up the early and middle rounds in a passive posture dug a hole far too deep to climb out of against someone of Canelo’s caliber.

Mbilli left his mark, connecting with shots whenever he actually let his hands go. The official scorecards did not reflect how competitive those exchanges really were.

More importantly, Mbilli exposed Canelo’s current physical limitations. The Mexican star simply cannot fire sustained combinations or maintain an intense pace anymore. Canelo was fighting in brief spurts, resting frequently, and relying on single power shots.

The real tragedy of the night was Mbilli’s failure to exploit those vulnerabilities. With Canelo showing his age and accumulated ring wear, the blueprint was right there: step on the gas, make him work every second of every round, and drown him in volume. Instead, Mbilli gave an aging veteran the exact thing he needed to survive, which was time to breathe.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Risks World Title Ambitions On Pointless Clarke Revenge Tour
Sports.content:
Even with a world title on his resume, Chris Billam-Smith cannot completely shake his two amateur losses to Cheavon Clarke. On Saturday, November 7, he gets his shot at redemption, though he risks far more than the man who twice got the better of him in the unpaid ranks.

Their 10-round cruiserweight clash tops Zuffa Boxing 12 at London’s Copper Box Arena, broadcast live on Sky Sports and Paramount+. This marks their first meeting as pros, and Billam-Smith admits those past defeats fuel his fire.

“I’ve got a lot of bitterness inside me which I need to unleash on November 7!” Billam-Smith told Sky Sports in October. Clarke’s wins include the 2016 national amateur championship final, which crushed Billam-Smith’s long-standing tournament dream.

That backstory brings real heat to this matchup, but Billam-Smith must keep his emotions in check. A victory maintains his momentum toward another major title run. Chasing payback for a decade-old loss could easily backfire against a dangerous puncher.

Clarke showcased his resilience along with his defensive flaws against Jack Massey in June. He hit the canvas twice before rallying to halt Massey. Billam-Smith competed on that same Bournemouth card, dispatching Ryan Rozicki in seven rounds. Both enter the ring coming off stoppage wins, yet Clarke’s grit under fire stands out as a crucial factor.

Those knockdowns offer Billam-Smith an incentive to test Clarke’s chin early. Still, they serve as a clear warning to remain composed if Clarke gets hurt. Clarke proved that dropping him does not guarantee the win. Rushing in recklessly could leave Billam-Smith wide open to counterpunches.

As a former WBO champion, Billam-Smith owns the far more accomplished professional resume. That pedigree ought to carry more weight than short-format amateur bouts from years ago. Billam-Smith excels in grueling pro championship rounds where physical strength, inside fighting, and pace control reign supreme.

Clarke is 35, entered the pro ranks late, and his absolute ceiling so far has been British and European contention. If Billam-Smith goes out and dominates him over ten rounds, the immediate reaction will simply be that an experienced former world champion beat a novice pro who started his career late. Nobody is awarding Billam-Smith points in the world cruiserweight rankings for beating a domestic contender.

If things go wrong, the fallout is devastating. Clarke can crack, as Jack Massey found out, and Billam-Smith gets hit cleanly in almost every fight he enters. Getting clipped or outpointed by someone who has not even fought for a world title instantly kills Billam-Smith’s chances of getting back in line for the division leaders or securing another massive payday.

Letting amateur grudges dictate matchmaking at this stage of a pro career is purely emotional thinking. It satisfies a personal itch, but in business terms, it is a massive detour that risks throwing away years of hard-earned status over a couple of short-format bouts from 2016.

Sports.title: Team Haney Overlooking Liam Paro To Chase Ryan Garcia Circus
Sports.content:
Mickey Bey has already mapped out next year, treating Liam Paro like an afterthought. Even with Paro holding the IBF belt, Haney’s trainer cannot stop eyeing a massive repeat encounter with Ryan Garcia.

Bey expects Haney to claim his second 147-pound title in December, hoping Garcia grabs the remaining pair to set up a mega-unification down the line.

“I want Ryan to get the belt from Teofimo and we fighting for the undisputed next year,” Bey said to MillCity Boxing. “That’s the biggest fight in boxing.”

The Ring’s Mike Coppinger reports that Haney and Paro are penciled in for December 19 at Chase Center in San Francisco for unified WBO and IBF honors. The date serves as Haney’s first outing under his fresh DAZN contract, ending a layoff that stretches back to his points win over Brian Norman Jr. last November.

Paro arrives hungry to spoil the party, yet Bey refuses to look at the man right in front of him. Team Haney is banking on Devin doing the business in the Bay Area, then counting on Garcia to snatch the WBA strap away from Teofimo Lopez. It reads like a promoter dream on paper, but counting on two separate fighters to deliver flawless results is asking for trouble.

“But hey, let’s settle the score. Hey, we going to win our fight. We going to have our two on our end. If he get his two, we got it for undisputed,” Bey said.

Collecting four belts looks great on paper, but hardware is not the real motivator here. Avenging the beating against Ryan is about erasing humiliation that titles cannot fix. Garcia planted Haney on the canvas three separate times in April 2024, and while a positive ostarine test officially wiped the defeat into a no-contest, commission paperwork cannot delete the footage. Fans remember Haney wobbling around the ring, and no collection of straps washes that stain away.

Bey keeps harping on Garcia missing weight as the deciding factor in that first beatdown. Complaining about the scale might sell tickets for a rematch, but excuses do not erase a one-sided shellacking. Haney has to get in the ring and physically prove he can handle the smoke himself.

Before any future rematch happens, Liam Paro is standing in the doorway. The Australian won his IBF belt by scraping past Lewis Crocker on tight 115-113 cards in June. That razor-thin margin might make Haney’s team think Paro is ripe for the picking, but the champion is not showing up just to roll over and surrender his hardware.

Between the ropes, Haney brings a frustrating, defensive style built around an active jab and constant retreat. Paro cannot fall into the trap of following him like a tourist. The Australian southpaw has to cut the ring in half, pin Haney against the ropes, and batter the ribs the second Haney dives in to initiate a clinch. If Paro allows Haney to jab, circle away, and reset without taking damage, he will spend the entire night chasing shadows on the scorecards.

Bey talks like December is just a tune-up stop on the road to a mega payday with Garcia. Treating a unified title bout like an afterthought provides Paro with perfect ammunition to derail Team Haney’s master plan before it ever gets off the ground.

An undisputed fight offers both men all four titles to parade around, but everyone knows the hardware is secondary. The actual hook for the public is seeing whether Haney can avoid getting planted on the canvas again, or if Garcia repeats the destruction.

Sports.title: Sheeraz Expects Canelo Payday After Limping Past Zachenhuber
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz is openly campaigning for an unearned lottery ticket against Canelo Alvarez, and boxing fans are expected to pretend this makes sense.

Fans online already assume Turki Alalshikh will force this matchup. That speaks volumes about the current matchmaking environment. People expect what they think the money wants instead of the fights worth watching. Canelo has genuine options available. A rematch with Terence Crawford makes sense, while Jaron Ennis, Dmitry Bivol, Lester Martinez, or Osleys Iglesias would each offer far more entertainment.

Sheeraz, in contrast, is the ideal safe business fight. He gives the Riyadh Season brass an easy UK marketing angle, brings a recognizable name to British television, and holds zero real threat of upsetting the apple cart. As Simon Zachenhuber showed, Sheeraz is upright, gets uncomfortable when pressed, lacks defensive subtlety, and struggles to impose his height when someone refuses to fold early.

Against Canelo, Sheeraz would stand right in range, get timed coming in, and walk straight into counters without the ringcraft to survive it. Picking him is about protecting the brand and cashing a check, not testing greatness.

“Why not, bro? Why not test myself against the best,” said Sheeraz to DAZN Boxing when asked yesterday why he wants to fight Canelo. “I’m in this game to be the best, and put myself in there with someone with the likes of Canelo. It’s stuff you can dream of. Every day, I wake up, training harder and harder. It’s starting to become more of a reality. So, now it’s like, let me get in there and let me do my thing.”

Sheeraz did himself no favors during his recent majority decision win against Simon Zachenhuber. The German walked through his shots, pressed him constantly, and exposed his discomfort under fire. Nothing in that performance signaled that Sheeraz belongs in the ring with the face of boxing.

His brief title run did not validate him either. Picking up a vacant WBO belt by blowing out Alem Begic in two rounds proved very little. Begic was 39 with a paper record built on obscure opposition. Sheeraz then vacated rather than face Janibek Alimkhanuly, citing low money and an opponent returning from a failed test. He had every right to walk away, but walking away did not prove he is elite.

The refusal to fight Iglesias makes Sheeraz even harder to sell. Canelo openly suggested Hamzah face the dangerous Cuban to earn the shot. Sheeraz rejected the idea, pointing out that Edgar Berlanga and Jaime Munguia never had to pass such an audition. Canelo might have double standards, but whining about Berlanga does not elevate Hamzah’s resume.

Testing yourself against the best is what you do after you run through actual contenders, not after edging Simon Zachenhuber on a majority decision or blasting out Alem Begic.

If Sheeraz genuinely wanted to “test himself against the best” to prepare for Canelo, Osleys Iglesias was standing right there. Canelo offered him the exact blueprint: beat the Cuban southpaw, prove you belong at the elite tier, and bring real credibility to the table.

Saying “It’s stuff you can dream of” gives the game away. It is a dream because it represents the ultimate lottery ticket: a massive purse, global visibility, and zero downside if he loses to an all-time great. Every fringe contender wakes up training hard with that exact dream.

Wanting the biggest purse in the sport is understandable from a business perspective. Pretending that ambition alone makes you a worthy challenger is the part fans are tired of seeing. If everyone who “wakes up dreaming of Canelo” got the call, the sport would be nothing but exhibition paydays. Until Sheeraz takes on a legitimate threat who can punch back, talking about testing himself just sounds like someone angling for a retirement check.

My sources tell me chances are uncomfortably high, easily hovering around 65% to 75% that Canelo fights Hamzah next. Everything coming out of Riyadh points to Hamzah Sheeraz being the preferred target for that spot: Sheeraz sat ringside in Riyadh, gave pre-fight interviews to DAZN building up the matchup, and openly positioned himself as next in line.

That is standard operating procedure when organizers are preparing the public for an announcement. From the promotional side, Sheeraz checks the exact commercial boxes Turki Alalshikh looks for. He provides a British draw to anchor UK pay-per-view buys, brings a Middle Eastern connection based out of Dubai, and comes without the brutal negotiating headaches that accompany figures like Dmitry Bivol or Terence Crawford.

For Canelo, the risk calculus makes Sheeraz almost irresistible. After working through twelve rounds with Christian Mbilli, taking on an upright target who does not use angles or elite lateral footwork is a safe day at the office. Canelo avoids the nightmare styles of Osleys Iglesias or Jaron Ennis while pocketing another massive purse.

The only real hurdles that could derail it are: Crawford agreeing to unretire for the massive bag that a rematch would command. If Crawford says yes, every other fight gets pushed aside immediately. A sudden pivot to a mandatory unification, such as Osleys Iglesias holding the IBF belt or the winner of Janibek Alimkhanuly against Jacob Bank for the vacant WBO strap, if organizers decide they want all the belts consolidated again. Lester Martinez, who holds the WBC interim belt and was also sitting ringside, is being enforced as a mandatory obligation.

As such, unless Crawford signs on the dotted line or public ridicule forces a change in direction, all arrows point toward Sheeraz getting the nod. It is safe matchmaking dressed up as an international event.

Ghana News.title: WPL 2026/27: Police Ladies continues impressive start; FC Savannah record first win
Ghana News.content:
Police Ladies continued their strong start to the 2026/27 GoldFields Women's Premier League following their victory over Immigration Ladies.

In an all-security affair, Police Ladies sealed a thumping 4-0 victory over Immigration Ladies at the Alajo Astro Turf to move to the top of the league table in the Southern Zone.

Fidous Yakubu scored a brace in the fixture, while Sophia Agyakwa and Beatrice Tsifokor scored the other two to give Abu Kassim Tabasu's side all three points.

In Takoradi, Cecilia Acquah scored in the 38th minute for Hasaacas Ladies, who recorded their first league victory over Jonina Ladies in three games.

Barbara Marfo was the star of the day for Oak Ladies who defeated FC Samartex Ladies for their first league win over the season at the Hearts Complex.

Epiphany Warriors fought from a goal sown to salvage a point in their home game against Army Ladies. Both teams are now without a win in their first two games.

LadyStrikers also made it two wins from their opening two games of the season after Betsheba Nyarko scored the only goal of the game in their victory over Roots Sistaz.

In the Northern Zone, Ampem Darkoa Ladies were exempted from action due to their participation in the CAF Women's Champions League, leaving their game against Supreme Ladies postponed.

Ashanti Ladies recovered from their defeat last weekend to claim a 1-0 win over Northern Ladies in the latter's first outing of the season.

Dreamz Ladies continue their search for a first win of the season as they were held again to a goalless draw by Tamale Super Ladies at home.

Prisons Ladies sealed a 1-0 victory over Fosu Royal Ladies on the second match week while FC Savannah defeated Dormaa Candy Soccer Ladies 2-0.

Ghana News.title: Court users stranded as Kumasi High Court and other lower courts shut down over JUSAG strike
Ghana News.content:
Court users seeking various services have been left stranded at court premises in Kumasi as critical staff of the judiciary lay down their tools over their 2026 salary review and outstanding arrears.

The Kumasi High Court and other lower courts in the Ashanti region, like in many parts of the country, have been shut down as the ongoing industrial action by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) brings the judiciary to its knees.

A tour of the Kumasi High Court, the Court of Appeal, the Asokwa Circuit Court and the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) Court confirmed that the facilities were closed with no judiciary staff around but a handful of persons seeking legal services.

Some clients who had cases scheduled for hearing today, Monday, November 2, arrived at the court premises only to find the gates locked and adorned with red cloth announcing the strike.

One of the affected persons, Joyce Konama, whose case was scheduled for judgment at the High Court on Monday, expressed her frustration.

Madam Konama noted that she was unaware of the strike and had travelled a considerable distance to attend the proceedings only to meet empty courtrooms.

“I didn’t know they were on strike today, and I am very worried after travelling all the way from my town to find the court closed. The government should fast-track negotiations on their conditions of service,” she said.

Speaking to Joy News, some of the affected court users appealed to the government to prioritise the welfare and conditions of service of judicial service staff to ensure the smooth administration of justice.

“If this strike continues for days, things will escalate in this country,” some of the clients warned.

Ghana News.title: GPL 2026/27: Kotoko fine assistant coach Diogo Peral over slap incident
Ghana News.content:
Diogo Peral

Asante Kotoko have fined assistant coach Diogo Peral following his sending-off for slapping a Medeama SC player during their Ghana Premier League clash at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium.

The club confirmed the disciplinary action in a statement, describing the coach’s conduct as inconsistent with its values.

"The Club wishes to state that such conduct does not reflect the standards and values we uphold at Asante Kotoko.

“Consequently, the Club has imposed a fine on Coach Diogo Peral as part of its internal disciplinary measures. This decision reinforces the Club’s commitment to maintaining the highest standards of discipline, professionalism, and accountability."

"We firmly believe that emotions must never compromise the professionalism, discipline, and respect expected of everyone representing this great institution."

Peral was shown a red card after allegedly assaulting Medeama player Ebenezer Adade during the 1-1 draw between the two sides.

The Ghana Football Association (GFA) has also charged the Portuguese coach over the incident.

Peral has until Wednesday, November 4, to respond to the charge.

Meanwhile, the result leaves Kotoko ninth in the league standings with 13 points.

The Porcupine Warriors will now shift their focus to their next league fixture against Berekum Chelsea.

Ghana News.title: JUSAG strike begins to bite as courts shut down in Accra
Ghana News.content:
The entrance to the Accra High Court was locked to prevent people from entering.

The nationwide industrial action declared by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) has affected court operations across the country, forcing the closure of several court premises, including the Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, Accra High Court, Circuit Court and some District Courts.

Access to the affected facilities has been restricted, with security officers reportedly directed to keep the gates closed following the commencement of the strike.

In a show of protest, red pieces of cloth have been placed at the entrances of some court premises to highlight the workers’ grievances.

At the Accra High Court, JoyNews' Legal Correspondent, Fatawu Bayaga, reported that several persons were outside the Court as they were denied entry.

The association is demanding the payment of outstanding salary arrears arising from the revised salary structure, which dates back to January 2026.

Amid the disruption, Judicial Secretary Musah Ahmed has urged JUSAG to reconsider its decision and suspend the strike to allow negotiations to continue.

He explained that management had engaged relevant government stakeholders in high-level discussions conducted in good faith to find a lasting solution to the concerns raised by the association.

Mr Ahmed also acknowledged the frustration among judicial staff over the delay in implementing the 2026 salary review, assuring them that management was attentive to their concerns.

Ghana News.title: Muntaka calls for stronger law enforcement cooperation to tackle transnational crimes
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, has called for stronger cooperation and information sharing among law enforcement agencies to tackle the growing threat of transnational crimes and strengthen national and regional security.

He said the increasing cross-border nature of criminal activities required security institutions to work together and improve the exchange of information to support investigations and prevent criminals from exploiting weaknesses in the security system.

The minister made the call at a meeting of the West African Police Information System (WAPIS) Ghana National Committee (WANACO) at the Police Headquarters in Accra, where stakeholders discussed the progress, challenges and sustainability of the programme.

He identified human trafficking, drug trafficking, cybercrime, financial crime and other organised criminal activities as some of the crimes requiring closer cooperation among law enforcement agencies, given their increasingly transnational nature.

The Minister observed that criminals continued to take advantage of communication gaps and weaknesses in information exchange among security institutions, making effective collaboration essential in tackling such activities.

He said law enforcement agencies must therefore strengthen their capacity to collect, manage, analyse and share criminal information in a timely, secure and lawful manner.

He further explained that the effectiveness of WAPIS depended not only on modern technology and infrastructure but also on accurate criminal data, adequate resources, strong inter-agency collaboration and the retention of trained personnel.

To ensure that the system achieved its intended objectives, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak urged WANACO to strengthen its oversight and coordination role by translating its deliberations into clear decisions, defined responsibilities and measurable outcomes.

He also emphasised that the sustainability of the programme required the collective commitment of all stakeholder institutions, rather than leaving its implementation solely to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) or the WAPIS Centre.

The Minister said every institution involved must take ownership of the programme and actively contribute to its effective implementation and long-term sustainability.

The meeting was attended by representatives of the European Union, the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the International Criminal Police Organisation (INTERPOL), and various security and law enforcement institutions.

Ghana News.title: Marvin Senaya returns to action after 120-day injury absence
Ghana News.content:
Ghana defender Marvin Senaya has returned to competitive football after 120 days on the sidelines with a hamstring injury.

The 25-year-old made his first appearance of the 2026/27 season for AJ Auxerre on Sunday, coming off the bench in their 5-1 defeat to Strasbourg in Ligue 1.

Senaya was introduced in the 63rd minute, playing 27 minutes as he began his return to action.

The defender had been out since sustaining the injury during Ghana’s Round of 32 match against Colombia at the 2026 FIFA World Cup on July 3.

He was forced off after just 13 minutes, bringing his tournament to an early end after featuring in all four of Ghana’s matches.

Senaya subsequently underwent hamstring surgery in Paris before beginning his rehabilitation with Auxerre.

His return will be welcome news for both the French club and the Black Stars as he works towards regaining full fitness.

Ghana will face Somalia in a doubleheader in mid-November in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

Ghana News.title: Finding Love In Accra Episode 3: Typing…
Ghana News.content:
Read Also: Finding Love in Accra Episode 2: Like a Brother

By the time Kojo left the restaurant, I had remembered why I used to enjoy having him around.

Unfortunately, I had also noticed several new reasons.

“Your brother is leaving,” Emefa said.

“Will you stop calling him that?”

“You introduced him.”

I ignored her and opened WhatsApp.

His number was still saved.

Kojo Campus.

Four years, and I had not even promoted him out of university.

His profile picture was a photograph of him standing beside the sea. Linen shirt. Dark glasses. Smiling at whoever was behind the camera.

Who took the picture?

I enlarged it.

“Are you listening to me?” Emefa asked.

“Yes.”

“What did I say?”

“You said… something about work.”

“I asked whether you wanted the last chicken wing.”

“Then why are you still holding it?”

She looked at my phone.

“Oh, Lovia.”

I locked the screen.

“What?”

“Nothing. Greet your brother for me.”

That evening, I opened his chat before I removed my makeup.

Our last conversation was still there.

Can I take you to dinner on Saturday? Just the two of us.

Four years old.

No reply.

Seeing it now, I felt a small, uncomfortable twist in my stomach. I had somehow remembered his kindness more clearly than my own silence.

I typed:

It was lovely seeing you tonight.

I read it twice.

Too formal. We had met in Osu, not at a shareholders’ meeting.

Deleted.

So you were just going to leave without asking how I’ve really been? 😂

No. Accusations already? The man had returned a bracelet.

Deleted.

Hey, stranger.

I stared at that one.

I was the reason we were strangers.

Deleted.

At midnight, I was in bed, on his profile again.

He came online.

I immediately left WhatsApp.

Please don’t ask me why. Apparently, he could see me through the phone.

On Monday, I decided I would message him after work.

By evening, I felt Tuesday would be more appropriate.

Tuesday, he posted a picture of coffee and his laptop.

I nearly replied, Working hard or hardly working?

Even loneliness has limits. I deleted it.

Wednesday was worse.

He posted a woman.

I sat upright so quickly my charging cable came out.

Proud of you, sis ❤️

I studied her face for family resemblance.

There was some around the nose.

Possibly.

I called Emefa.

“Do men call their girlfriends ‘sis’?”

“Good afternoon to you too.”

“I’m asking generally.”

“Then generally, leave me alone. I’m at work.”

By Thursday, I was annoyed with him.

He had my number. He knew where to find me. Why hadn’t he said anything?

Then I scrolled up to his unanswered invitation.

Fair enough.

That night, I finally typed what I had been avoiding.

They say it takes twenty-one days to break a habit. It’s been four years, and I still can’t get you off my mind.

I paused.

Had I thought about him every day for four years?

No.

But I had missed him in little moments. When something funny happened, and I knew he would understand. When I had good news. When I needed to talk without first making myself sound cheerful.

I kept typing.

I know I did you wrong by not responding to your message about the date. But you know I adore you. It hurt not having you in my life.

I read it.

Then I imagined him opening it beside the woman from the beach photograph.

Deleted everything.

On Friday, Emefa took my phone.

“Just say hello.”

“It’s more complicated than that.”

“It is five letters.”

She handed it back.

At 9:43 p.m., after a week of composing messages that nobody had commissioned, I sent:

Hey, Kojo. It was good seeing you the other day.

Delivered.

I put the phone down.

Picked it up.

Two blue ticks.

Then:

Typing…

I held my breath.

I was wondering whether you’d reply this time.

Before I could recover, another message arrived.

What did you delete last night?

I looked at the empty space where my confession had been.

I had deleted the words.

I had forgotten WhatsApp could announce that I was typing them.

To be continued.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod generates $1.011bn in forex from gold trade in October
Ghana News.content:
Sammy Gyamfi, GoldBod CEO

The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) says it generated US$1.011 billion in foreign exchange from its artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold trading operations in October 2026.

In an announcement issued on Monday, November 2, the Board said the entire amount was sold to authorised commercial banks through its GoldBod GoFX platform to support stability in the foreign exchange market.

GoldBod is projecting to generate US$1.2 billion in foreign exchange from its ASM gold trade operations in November.

Of this amount, US$800 million is expected to be made available to commercial banks to support foreign exchange market stability.

The Board said the sales would be conducted through the GoldBod GoFX platform in accordance with its approved FX Sales and Intermediation Framework to ensure transparency, fairness and regulatory compliance.

It added that it remains committed to its statutory mandate of generating foreign exchange for the country and supporting the accumulation of Ghana’s foreign reserves by the Bank of Ghana under the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Policy (GANRAP).

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts a missile as fighting rages in Yemen’s al-Jawf
World.content:
Houthi-affiliated media report that seven people were wounded in strikes on the city of Hodeidah.

Share Saudi-led coalition intercepts a missile as fighting rages in Yemen’s al-Jawf on social media

The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen says air defences intercepted a Houthi missile, while fighting continues to rage along key fronts between the armed group and forces loyal to the internationally recognised Yemeni government.

Defences “intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile” targeting Saudi Arabia’s southern region, said coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki in a statement on Monday.

Earlier, he said defences destroyed a drone launched toward the southern region on Sunday evening.

Also on Monday, the Saudi Civil Defence authority issued and then lifted alerts warning of “potential danger” in the city of Abha, as well as the provinces of Khamis Mushait, Taif and Najran.

The authority warned residents against “filming, publishing or sharing information” related to missile and drone attacks.

In Yemen, a media outlet affiliated with the Houthi armed group, also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), reported that seven people were wounded in Saudi-led coalition air strikes on Hodeidah on the Red Sea coast.

Four people were wounded in the attacks on Ras Isa port dock, while three others suffered injuries in a strike on an oil company site in the governorate’s Bajil district, Houthi media reported.

There was no comment on the reports from the Saudi-led coalition.

Humanitarian crisis

The latest clashes come as Yemeni government forces keep up their campaign to regain positions from the Iran-aligned Houthis in the strategic northern governorate of al-Jawf.



Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said on Sunday evening that government forces conducted 1,272 “targeting operations” against Houthi fighters, fortifications and weapons supplies over 24 hours.

Operations are ongoing in al-Jawf, neighbouring Marib and al-Bayda to the south, added al-Nazili. Government forces killed roughly 500 Houthi fighters and destroyed or disabled nearly 170 vehicles, equipment or heavy weaponry.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the claims.

In southwest Yemen, the Houthis continue to besiege the city of Taiz, blocking the entry of food, fuel and medical supplies, in what authorities warn is a mounting humanitarian crisis.

Taiz Governor Nabil Shamsan has called for urgent help for the city’s deteriorating health facilities. He said 120 health centres have stopped operating and another 66 are close to shutting down since the Houthis cut off supply routes to the city in early October.

Nour al-Din al-Mansouri, a member of the committee facilitating the work of the Taiz Siege Affairs Office, told Al Jazeera that at least 23 trucks were damaged or overturned in the past two weeks while seeking alternative routes to Taiz.

The city is Yemen’s third-largest and home to about one million of the country’s roughly 43 million people.

Full-scale fighting reignited in Yemen in September, when the Houthis made crucial gains that tightened their grip on the Red Sea coast.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government launched a campaign called Operation Dawn of Yemen last month to regain Houthi-held sites and restore government control over other territories held by the group, which seized the capital Sanaa in 2014.

World.title: Nuclear radiation in Russia, Ukraine? No, just hacked warning alerts
World.content:
Warnings startle people in Ukraine, but authorities say they cleared up the confusion in under an hour.

Ukraine and Russia have accused each other of hacking into systems used to send out emergency alerts to citizens, raising fears of a new escalation of digital and psychological warfare tactics.

The systems’ apps sent out radiation alerts on Sunday and Monday to civilians before officials issued public clarifications.

The fake threats began on the same day as a localised ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Kherson region came to an end on Sunday. The truce, which the United States said was brokered by first lady Melania Trump, is the longest so far in Russia’s more than four-year war on Ukraine. The ceasefire lasted for six days, during which humanitarian aid and evacuations were allowed in the Russian-occupied town of Olekshy.

Al Jazeera’s Audrey Macalpine, reporting from Kyiv, said many people in Ukraine now expect renewed fighting along the front lines.

Here’s what we know about the fake notifications:

What happened?

Ukraine’s Air Force said late on Sunday that users of its Air Alert app, which warns people of incoming air attacks, received fake warnings of nuclear and chemical threats to areas in and around Kyiv.

Users were also warned of potential street combat and told that Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile had been deployed.

“The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence,” the Ukrainian Air Force said on Telegram.



“There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel.”

Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications blamed Russia. In a post on X, the agency pointed to the use of the Russian language in one of the fake messages. The Ukrainian government said a separate app created for the capital city was working normally.

The fake alerts came just after 10pm (20:00 GMT), startling a lot of people, Macalpine reported.

“Even the speakers here in the centre of the city rang out warnings of these attacks,” she said. “But most people here understood within at least half an hour that this was some kind of hacking attack.”

Hours later on Monday morning, similar announcements came from Russia’s Ministry of Civil Defence, Emergencies and Disaster Relief, which said its warnings app came under a “massive cyberattack” and wrongly warned users of imminent drone attacks. The ministry did not name any suspects but said the alerts spread “false information”.

Media reports said the hackers warned Russians that “nuclear warheads mounted on P1-Suns [Ukrainian drones] had been launched on all regions” of the country. The alerts also instructed people to “urgently” stock up on food for three weeks and to hide.

Has this happened before?

This appears to be the first time either Ukraine’s or Russia’s official alert apps have been hacked.

However, cyberwarfare has long been a major part of the countries’ previous confrontations.

Russian hackers have attacked Ukraine’s election systems in the past and in January 2022 attacked Ukrainian government and banking sites. Cyberwarfare tactics have only intensified since February 2022 when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In late 2023, the Russian hacker group Sandworm took the private telecommunications network Kyivstar offline, disrupting notifications for days.

Ukrainian groups have also launched multiple cyberattacks on Russia.

The country’s volunteer-based IT Army of Ukraine was founded in the wake of Russia’s invasion specifically to engage in cyberwarfare against Russia and has reportedly targeted the Moscow Stock Exchange, Russia’s power grids and several government websites. In 2022, the Reuters news agency reported Ukrainian attackers used facial recognition software to scan the faces of dead Russian combatants and notified their families of their deaths.

Why is the threat of nuclear radiation in Ukraine significant?

Ukraine is particularly vulnerable because it has already suffered one nuclear disaster and it remains at risk due to fighting around another major nuclear plant.



In April 1986, the Chornobyl nuclear power plant, located in the then-Ukrainian Soviet Republic, exploded, releasing radioactive material. Scores of people died from the explosion itself, but thousands later developed severe health issues as a result, including thyroid cancer. Radiation was detected as far away as Sweden. It’s regarded as one of the two worst nuclear accidents in history along with the 2011 Fukushima disaster in Japan. Chornobyl remains a ghost town after its inhabitants were evacuated.

Ongoing fighting in the Ukrainian region of Zaporizhia has raised fears that the tragic story could repeat itself. Russia partly controls the region, including Enerhodar, where the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Europe’s largest nuclear energy facility, is located.

Both sides have repeatedly launched attacks on each other’s positions with Russia targeting the Ukrainian-held provincial capital, Zaporizhzhia, and Ukraine targeting Russian-held areas, including Enerhodar.

Last week, the International Atomic Energy Agency, the United Nations nuclear watchdog, said a welder working at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant was killed in a drone attack. The head of the agency, Rafael Grossi, called for “maximum military restraint” from both sides.

World.title: US midterms: 1 day to go – Democrats rally around El-Sayed amid attacks
World.content:
Democrats slam Haley Stevens over her endorsement of a Republican candidate a day before the polls.

Share US midterms: 1 day to go – Democrats rally around El-Sayed amid attacks on social media

With one day to go before the United States midterm elections, campaigning has reached a fever pitch with Democratic and Republican leaders pulling out all the stops to mobilise voters.

Democrats are hoping to flip control of both chambers of Congress, which is currently controlled by US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party.

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the Senate’s 100 seats are up for grabs on Tuesday. Voting will also be held to elect governors in 36 of the 50 US states.

With the cost-of-living crisis, exacerbated by the US-Israel war on Iran, becoming one of the key talking points of these elections, here’s where things stand as of Monday:

What’s happened on the campaign trail in the past 24 hours?

In a dramatic political development on Sunday, Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens threw her support behind Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers over her own party’s nominee, Abdul El-Sayed, in Michigan – one of the most closely watched races of the US midterm elections. Stevens had lost Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary in August to El-Sayed.

Her announcement followed weeks of tension with El-Sayed over US support to Israel, which has been accused of committing genocide in Gaza. El-Sayed has opposed military support to Israel, arguing that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pushed the US into the Iran war. Stevens has accused El-Sayed of anti-Semitism for his criticism of Israeli actions in Gaza.

El-Sayed said a vote for his rival Rogers “is going to be a vote for Donald Trump” as his campaign reportedly saw a fundraising surge after Stevens crossed party lines.



Democratic leaders have rallied behind El-Sayed, who has faced Islamophobic attacks during the campaign.

The chairman of the Democratic Party in Michigan criticised Stevens. “She does not speak for that larger community,” Curtis Hertel said in an interview with CNN.

The leader of the Democrats in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, slammed Stevens over her endorsement of the Republican candidate.

“This is a despicable betrayal from Representative Stevens,” he posted on X.

“Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors.”

Meanwhile, the advocacy group Michigan Jews for Democracy has backed El-Sayed.

“Haley Stevens does not speak for Michigan’s Jewish community,” it said in a statement, which rejected her “attempt to divide our community” two days before the election.

While Democrats have been angered by Stevens’s action, Trump celebrated her decision.

During a rally in Iowa later on Sunday, the US president said he would “love” it if Stevens joined the Republican Party. “Haley said what few people are willing to say,” Trump added. “It’s a thing called bravery.”

The question now is whether Stevens’s endorsement could persuade some of her supporters to back Rogers or discourage them from voting altogether.

Polling suggested El-Sayed has largely consolidated Democratic support, according to the Reuters news agency.

Judge dismisses Trump’s Alaska election lawsuit

Meanwhile, a ⁠federal ⁠judge has thrown out a Trump administration ⁠lawsuit seeking to block Alaska from ⁠certifying a loss by Republican Senator Dan Sullivan. The administration has argued that a rival on the ballot with the same name could change the outcome.

Sullivan pledged to accept the election outcome, days after the US Department of Justice filed a lawsuit seeking to decertify the results of the Senate race if he loses.

“I’m going to accept the election results,” Sullivan, an ally of Trump, told CNN on Sunday.

Alaska’s Senate race is one of seven key toss-up races that will likely decide whether Republicans keep their majority in the upper chamber of the US Congress.

How many Americans have already voted?

This year, out of about 210 million registered voters, 54.5 million had voted early as of 10am US East Coast time (15:00 GMT) on Sunday, according to a University of Florida analysis. This includes 30 million in-person votes and 24 million mail-in ballots.



In the 2022 midterm elections, 46 million people voted early.

Early voting enthusiasm has been higher among Democrats this year with more than 11 million registered Democrats having voted early, compared with about 8 million registered Republicans, according to the university’s analysis.

Early voting has particularly surged in the state of Texas, a key battleground, where more than 7.7 million people have voted early.

According to an Associated Press polling analysis, in South Carolina, where Trump won by nearly 18 percentage points in 2024, early voting has surged 83 percent compared with the same point in 2022. The state has open races for governor and US Senate this year.

Kansas, Michigan and Maine have also seen a surge in early voting.

Early turnout figures, however, don’t show which candidates voters have chosen or what the final results will be.

World.title: MLB ‘spot-fixing’ trial set to begin in US court
World.content:
MLB pitchers charged with conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery go on trial in New York.

Former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz go on trial on Monday on charges of accepting bribes after colluding with gamblers who made hundreds of thousands of dollars by betting correctly on individual pitches in Major League Baseball (MLB) in the United States.

Their careers and possibly their freedom are at stake in the jury trial expected to unfold over the next month in New York’s Brooklyn federal court. Several professional baseball players, including catchers and baseball executives, are among witnesses expected to testify.

Clase, the Guardians’ former closer, and Ortiz, a starter, have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges and are on non-disciplinary leave from the club without pay while their fate is determined.

According to an indictment, the pitchers accepted thousands of dollars in payoffs to help two gamblers from their native Dominican Republic win at least $460,000 on in-game prop bets on the speed and outcome of certain pitches.

Prosecutors allege that Clase began providing the betters with information about his pitches in 2023 and recruited Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Ortiz’s lawyers unsuccessfully sought to have him tried separately from Clase.

Judge Kiyo A Matsumoto said at a conference last Friday that she hopes to complete jury selection quickly enough that lawyers can deliver relatively short opening statements in the afternoon.



Clase, 28, is a three-time All-Star and two-time American League Reliever of the Year who had completed his fourth season of a $20m, five-year contract when charges against the pitchers were revealed in November 2025.

Ortiz, 27, had earned $782,600 as a starting pitcher for the Guardians during the 2025 season.

The pitchers have been charged with wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy and conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery.

Defence lawyers are expected to argue that the pitchers did not collude with gamblers and instead were varying the placement of pitches strategically to fool batters.

On Friday, the judge ruled that prosecutors cannot show the jury proof that Clase owed $500,000 in US taxes because they had only provided the evidence to defence lawyers several days earlier and long after a deadline had passed to turn over evidence to their adversaries.

A prosecutor had argued that the government wanted to put the evidence in the trial to offset any claim by Clase’s lawyers that he had no incentive to collude with gamblers because he had several million dollars in financial accounts in the Dominican Republic.

MLB and the Guardians have said they have fully cooperated with authorities. MLB said it contacted federal law enforcement when it began investigating unusual betting activity.
