“This is for our honour. This is for reciprocity. This is for the enduring stability and peaceful coexistence of our great nation. That is exactly what the re-election of Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a second term stands for. That is the future we build today,” it added.

Also speaking, Governor Yusuf corroborated Abdulmajid’s position, saying the unity of Nigeria could only be guaranteed by fair play and inclusivity.

The Governor who was represented by his Director-General of Media and Publicity, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, argued that reversing the existing rotational arrangement would paint the North in ignoble light, even as he urged the region to maintain the status quo by re-electing President Tinubu for a second term.

In his remarks, former Governor of Jigawa State and immediate past Minister of Defence, Mohammad Abubakar Badaru, said the Renewed Hope Administration of President Tinubu has benefited the North more than any other part of Nigeria.

Badaru listed major completed road projects to include the 88km Zuba-Jere section and the 81km Abuja-Kaduna section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano Highway commissioned in October 2026, the 77km Kaduna-Pambeguwa road, Yakasai-Badume-Damargu-Marken Zalli roads in Kano, and the Jimeta Bridge in Yola.

On social infrastructure, Badaru cited completed health facilities such as Gadon Kaya PHC in Kano, three Polio Emergency Centers in Katsina, Kano and Sokoto, pharmacy lab at ABUTH Zaria, 50-bed mental health center at UNIMAID, and infertility center at ATBUTH Bauchi, plus ongoing upgrades at Bichi General Hospital and deployment of 79 CNG ambulances.

Igbo Torn Between Emotion and Reason in 2027 Elections, Declares Soludo

Soludo has summarised the disposition of the Ndigbo ahead of the 2027 elections, saying they were torn between emotions and reason in the forthcoming presidential election, but advised that it was better to embrace reason than work on emotion.

Soludo was referring to the support being given by most Igbo people to Obi, who is from the region.

Speaking at a stakeholders’ meeting of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party, which he convened in Awka as the Anambra State Coordinator of the Presidential Campaign Committee of APC, Soludo insisted that those who couldn’t win Tinubu when he was not in power should not expect to win him now that he was in charge.

Speaking at the well-attended meeting which had members of the four political parties in attendance, Soludo insisted that there would be consequences for not supporting Tinubu if he won reelection next year.

He said: “This is a grand coalition for the progress, prosperity, security, and welfare of Nigeria and of course, Anambra. This is a battle for the soul of Ndigbo and Anambra, a battle between emotion and reason. Emotion will always dominate, but reason will eventually triumph.

“We have clamoured for the presidency since 1978, we have held many positions in Nigeria except president. So, how do we get there? We need partnerships. Politics is about interest, we are not doing Tinubu any favour by supporting him, rather we are doing ourselves a favour. We did not vote for him in 2023, yet he won, and some people want us to repeat the same mistake?”

Soludo said he was sure of Tinubu’s victory next year, saying, “A warrior who you couldn’t beat when he was sleeping in 2023, is it now that he is fully awake that you think you can defeat him? It can’t happen. Show me anywhere in the world that anyone has taken power from a powerful incumbent president?

“Ndigbo have been playing politics of protest and it is not in our own favour. Our brother who is running for president (Peter Obi) is my friend. We are close, our families are close and we will remain close. The only place where we disagree with each other is in politics. We cannot keep deceiving our people.

“In politics, there is not prize for second position, that is why I say we should not throw away our votes. We must remember there is consequence for running and failing. So, for Ndigbo, this is a battle between temporary emotion and reason.

“If we back Tinubu for a second term, after his tenure, power will move to the north, and when it comes to the South again, we will be able to negotiate with other regions in the South to support us because we supported them when they needed us.”

The Governor insisted that he was not supporting Tinubu’s reelection for any percuniary gains, adding that after winning a second term as governor, he was done with election contest.

He said: “I grew up in the era when we used to say – speak the truth and shame the devil. In 2023 I even wrote it down that he (Obi) will fail. I wrote that at best he would come third, and what later happened? This time, I’m saying it again that he will fail. Once you go to election with fragmented opposition, the incumbent will carry the day.

“I’m saying this truth because I care for Igbo. I’m no longer contesting any election after my second term, so I can retire to my village and be enjoying fresh palm wine, but it is the future of Ndigbo that we are fighting for. That is why I’m shouting because I know that contesting and failing has serious consequences.”

Soludo charged all parties in the coalition to go out and scout for votes to ensure a resounding victory for Tinubu on January 16, 2026.

He said parties must adopt a door-to-door campaign strategy to be able to reach undecided voters, insisting that securing victory for Tinubu in Anambra will give the state the right to negotiate for favours in his second term. He also scored the president high on projects being done in the state, saying only victory will give him the courage to complete the projects when he returns.

“Tinubu is doing many projects in Anambra State. We want to support him to ensure that he returns to complete them. There are numerous other projects that we would want him to do, but you can only ask for them if you are a member of the inner chamber.

“We need to partner the federal government for some projects. Our roads need to be motorable, there is the gas pipeline project, rail project, erosion menace. Some of these are not things a state can take on with just FAAC, and the only way the federal government can come to our aid is if we are partners,” Soludo said.

Akpabio: Akwa Ibom’ll Deliver South-South’s Highest Votes for Tinubu in 2027

The President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, has assured President Bola Tinubu and the leadership of the APC that Akwa Ibom State would deliver the highest number of votes for the ruling party’s presidential candidate in the South-South geopolitical zone in the January 16, 2027 general election.

Akpabio, according to a statement from his Media Office, gave the assurance yesterday, at a special religious service organised to dedicate the APC’s 2027 election campaigns to God at the International Christian Worship Centre, Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital.

The service, which had the theme, ‘We Are Well Able,’ brought together party leaders, government officials, political stakeholders and supporters to seek divine guidance for the party ahead of the forthcoming general election.

The Senate President, who called on APC members in the state to close ranks and present a united front, said the party could only translate its electoral ambitions into reality if internal divisions and disagreements were set aside.

He attributed his emergence as President of the Senate to the support of Tinubu, describing the development as an opportunity for Akwa Ibom State to demonstrate its appreciation through massive electoral support for the President.

He said, “An Akwa Ibom son, through the support of Mr. President, is today the President of the Senate and the number three citizen of Nigeria. Whether you like him or not, he is there today.

“The only way to thank Mr. President for that support is to give him all our votes. From what I have seen here today, Akwa Ibom State will give Mr. President the highest number of votes in the South-South region.”

In an address titled ‘One Family, One Destiny, One Akwa Ibom Under God,’ the statement explained that Akpabio emphasised the importance of unity, inclusiveness and peaceful coexistence among members of the APC, warning against divisions based on the length of membership or political affiliation.

He maintained that the party should operate as one family in which old and new members enjoy equal opportunities to contribute to its growth and electoral success.

He said, “In the APC family, there should be no aborigines and no newcomers; no landlords and no tenants; no first-class members and no second-class members. There should be only one big family, united by a common purpose and a shared responsibility.

“Those who were here yesterday have a history to honour, and those who arrived today have contributions to make. Neither history nor arrival should become an instrument of exclusion.”

Using a biblical illustration from John 14:2, the Senate President said there was sufficient political space for every member of the party, irrespective of when they joined.

He said, “Our Lord Jesus Christ declared in John 14:2: ‘In my Father’s house are many mansions.’ Let me borrow that beautiful imagery today. In this house, there are many mansions, enough for everyone!

“There is room for the pioneer and room for the newcomer; room for the elder and room for the youth; room for those who laid the foundation and room for those who will raise the roof.

“Nobody needs to demolish another person’s mansion to find accommodation, and nobody needs to extinguish another person’s candle for his own light to shine. We may have arrived through different doors, but we must learn to live under one roof,” he added.

Akpabio further urged political leaders and party members to ensure that their political ambitions did not override the welfare and aspirations of the people.

He said political activities should reflect the moral values of the faith professed by the people, stressing that electoral campaigns must respect human dignity and promote peaceful coexistence.

“Therefore, our politics must reflect our faith, our campaigns must honour human dignity, and our ambitions must never become greater than the welfare of our people,” he stated.

The Senate President also described Akwa Ibom as a developing success story, attributing the state’s progress to purposeful leadership, peace and sustained development.

According to him, the state’s achievements should not be measured solely by physical infrastructure but also by its ability to strengthen relationships among its people and restore public confidence in governance.

He said, “Akwa Ibom has become a Nigerian wonder story, a testimony to the possibilities of purposeful leadership, peace and development.

“Our state is demonstrating that progress is not merely about the roads we construct or the buildings we erect, but also about the bridges we build between people and the hope we restore in human hearts.

“We must preserve this progress and ensure that the chapters yet to be written are greater than those already written,” he said.

He also linked the state’s development to the broader national interest, insisting that Akwa Ibom could not achieve sustainable prosperity in isolation from the challenges confronting other parts of the country.

Akpabio said, “Akwa Ibom’s greatness is inseparable from Nigeria’s greatness. We cannot desire peace in Uyo and be indifferent to insecurity elsewhere in our federation, nor celebrate prosperity in our communities while ignoring hardship in other parts of our country.

“Nigeria is not merely the nation to which Akwa Ibom belongs; it is the larger destiny to which Akwa Ibom contributes,” he said.

He urged political stakeholders to demonstrate national solidarity through their actions and strengthen the foundations of democracy.

Earlier, Governor Umo Eno thanked the people of Akwa Ibom for their support during the last election and appealed for even greater backing for Tinubu, Akpabio, himself and other APC candidates in the 2027 general election.

The governor also reaffirmed his commitment to serving the people with the fear of God, expressing the hope that they would give him another mandate to continue his administration’s development agenda.

He urged residents to sustain their support for the APC, describing the forthcoming election as an opportunity to consolidate the party’s political fortunes and development efforts in the state.

World.title: Atiku Accuses APC Presidential Campaign of Obscuring President’s Unfulfilled Promises
World.content:
· ADC council says ruling party’s sustained assault on democracy will fail

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

President candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC) and former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has accused the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council of seeking to obscure President Bola Tinubu’s unfulfilled electricity promise with a long recital of laws, committees, bonds, and projects.

Atiku made the accusation in a statement by Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC), Phrank Shaibu.

Separately, ADC-PCC condemned what it called sustained, coordinated, and state-sponsored assault on democracy, freedom of association, and the constitutional right of Nigerians to political participation under the Tinubu administration. It, however, declared that the assaults would fail and democracy was bound to survive and outlive APC.

Atiku said, in the statement by ADC-PCC, “The APC should spare Nigerians the spectacle of celebrating paperwork while homes and businesses remain in darkness.

“After three and a half years, families still struggle to keep their homes lit. Traders and small business owners spend scarce resources on alternative power, yet struggle to keep their businesses alive.”

ADC campaign council said, “Nigerians are billed for electricity they cannot rely on. President Tinubu promised steady power and an end to estimated billing. That promise has not been kept.

“Across Nigeria, consumers are placed in Bands A, B, C, D and E and charged different rates. In many areas, Band A customers pay about N209.50 per unit before VAT. Rates for the other bands vary by state and electricity provider.

”Yet across every band, the same hardship endures: the power fails, but the bill arrives. No family should have to weigh the cost of electricity against the cost of food. No business should be left to pay more while receiving less.”

ADC added, “The government now says it plans to end electricity subsidies from 2027, even as it insists there will be no immediate tariff increase. Nigerians are entitled to a clear answer: what will happen to their bills when the subsidy ends?”

The ADC presidential candidate promised that if elected, “I will work with state governments and regulators, within the law, to abolish the present band system and replace it with a fair, transparent and affordable framework that protects households and holds power companies accountable for the electricity they deliver.

“Steady power that Nigerians can afford will be a national priority.”

Insisting that Tinubu had no justification for seeking another term, the ADC campaign council stated, “When President Tinubu campaigned in 2022, he made an unmistakable commitment. He said: ‘If I don’t give you constant electricity for four years, when I come back for a second term, don’t vote for me.’

“Nigerians have lived through those four years. They do not need his campaign council to interpret his words for them. They need him to answer for them.

“His administration has not built a single new generation infrastructure of its own to increase Nigeria’s power capacity. Yet it has floated a multitrillion naira bond programme to settle legacy debts owed to generation companies, without showing Nigerians how this financial intervention has produced the steady electricity they were promised.

”Paying old debts is not the same as building new power infrastructure. Bonds cannot be presented as a substitute for power in people’s homes.”

ADC also accused the Tinubu government of worsening the power woes with unjustifiable energy taxes.

It stated, “Meanwhile, Nigerians face VAT on electricity, and the Nigeria Tax Act provides for a five per cent surcharge on certain fossil fuels, including petrol and diesel.

“The government says the surcharge has not been activated and would require a ministerial order. At a time when families already struggle to meet the cost of energy, Nigerians deserve to know why another potential charge has been placed before them.

“Dele Alake’s statement cannot light a home. Signing a law is not electricity. Raising a bond is not electricity. Approving a project is not power delivered. Nigerians cannot cook, study, work or sustain a business on announcements.

”President Tinubu invited Nigerians to judge him by his performance. They have done so. What they seek is simple: reliable electricity they can afford, and a government that keeps its word.”

APC’s Sustained Assault On Democracy Will Fail, Says ADC Presidential Campaign

ADC-PCC condemned what it described as organised assault on democracy and freedom of association and political participation under the administration of Tinubu, declaring that the assaults will fail, as democracy will outlive APC.

The council said the unfolding incidents across the country went beyond ordinary political rivalry. It alleged that the incidents represented a disturbing pattern of intimidation, harassment, and suppression of opposition voices.

The council said the Tinubu government had engaged in calculated atrocious actions skewed to scare Nigerians ahead of the general election.

In a statement signed by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, ADC-PCC recalled a series of incidents, including attacks on its leaders and members in Kaduna, the reported assault on its Sokoto State governorship candidate, Alhaji Munir Dan Iya, by operatives of the Sokoto Marshals along Airport Road, Sokoto, and alleged attacks on other opposition figures.

It also cited the reported demolition of its governorship campaign office in Kebbi State and the alleged denial of a campaign venue in Enugu State to Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi.

The council further referenced the reported attacks on the presidential candidate of African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, and other opposition voices, describing the incidents as part of an emerging pattern of political intolerance.

According to ADC-PCC, the attacks, denial of campaign venues, arrests, harassment, and intimidation of opposition figures raised serious concerns about the state of democratic freedoms and political pluralism in Nigeria.

The council maintained that no government, regardless of its political or institutional strength, could successfully suppress the democratic aspirations of Nigerians, recalling that popular resistance contributed to the collapse of former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s third-term agenda.

It also stated that Tinubu and APC enjoyed the benefits of political participation and opposition politics when they were outside government, insisting that those same democratic freedoms must be guaranteed to all political parties and their members.

Sharing Atiku’s thoughts, ADC-PCC also described as an afterthought the attempt by Alake and APC-PCC to rewrite Tinubu’s categorical 2023 electricity pledge through selective quotations and elaborate explanations.

Reacting to comments by Alake, Ologbondiyan maintained that Tinubu was unequivocal when he told Nigerians not to vote for him for a second term if he failed to deliver electricity during his first tenure.

According to ADC-PCC, Nigerians have not forgotten the president’s words. His commitment was clear and unambiguous: “Don’t vote for me for second term if I fail to deliver electricity.”

The council said no amount of selective editing, additional paragraphs, or grammatical gymnastics could erase that commitment from the consciousness of Nigerians.

It said rather than end estimated billing, the Tinubu administration had presided over increased electricity bills, leaving many households struggling to afford power supply.

ADC-PCC further observed that businesses, including hospitality facilities, had been forced to ration electricity by switching off power for guests during daytime hours to contain operating costs.

It also criticised the introduction of discriminatory tariff classifications under Bands A, B, C and others, stating that consumers continue to pay more without receiving reliable electricity supply.

World.title: Tinubu to Nigerian Delegation to Makkah: Our Diversity, A Recipe for Prosperity
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu prayed Almighty Allah to transform Nigeria’s rich diversity into a source of prosperity, unity, peace and sustainable development for the benefit of all Nigerians.

Tinubu offered the prayer on Sunday in the holy city of Makkah, Saudi Arabia, while hosting members of his delegation for dinner.

The president expressed the hope that Nigeria’s ethnic, religious, and cultural diversity would continue to serve as a source of strength and national advancement rather than division. He stressed the need for citizens to embrace mutual understanding, peaceful coexistence, and a shared commitment to the country’s progress.

He prayed that Almighty Allah would bless Nigeria with enduring peace, harmony, and prosperity, and grant the nation’s leaders the wisdom, courage, and foresight to steer the country towards greater development and improved living conditions for its people.

“May Almighty Allah bless Nigeria, convert our diversity into prosperity as a country,” the president said.

Tinubu also prayed for divine guidance and protection for Nigerians at home and abroad, asking Allah to strengthen the bonds of brotherhood among citizens and inspire a renewed spirit of patriotism, compassion and service to the nation.

The president stated that Nigeria’s abundant human and natural resources, coupled with the talents, creativity and enterprise of its diverse population, provided a strong foundation for building a prosperous and inclusive nation.

The dinner with members of his delegation in Makkah provided an opportunity for fellowship and reflection on Nigerians’ shared aspirations for a peaceful, united and prosperous country.

Tinubu urged Nigerians of all faiths and backgrounds to keep working together in the national interest, expressing confidence that, with faith in Almighty Allah, unity of purpose, and collective determination, Nigeria would overcome its challenges and realise its full potential.

Chairman of BUA, Alhaji Abdulsamad Rabiu, reaffirmed Tinubu’s commitment to peace, unity and prosperity of Nigeria.

Rabiu said, “Today is actually the third dinner we’re having with His Excellency, Mr President, since we came to Makkah on Thursday night or Friday morning when Mr President arrived.

“So, we discussed, and the discussion was, you know, to always continue to pray for Nigeria, for peace, for unity and for Nigeria’s prosperity. To again, you know, thank His Excellency for his passion, for what he’s doing for Nigeria.

“And also for us, it’s quite important because, as I said, it has given us the opportunity to come and pray not only for ourselves and our families, but also for Nigeria.

“We will continue to support His Excellency in whatever capacity we can and, definitely, as you all know, Mr President is very passionate about the country. He’s working very hard, and we’ll continue to support him.”

Kwara State Governor and Chairman of Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF), Abdulrahman AbdulRazaq, said the forum was overwhelmed by the president’s passion and commitment to achieving a united and prosperous nation.

AbdulRazaq stated, “Only Allah can reward you; we will continue to pray for you daily and pray for Nigeria that you lead. May Allah continue to strengthen you in making the right decisions, strengthen your wisdom, your boldness, your audacity, your courage. May Allah lead you to the right path.”

Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Mr Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), also prayed for Almighty Allah to continue to strengthen the president in his determination to deliver governance and justice to all Nigerians, irrespective of their religion or ethnic backgrounds.

The dinner was attended by Yobe State Governor Mai Mala Buni; Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani; Jigawa State Governor Mohammed Namadi; Sokoto State Governor Ahmed Aliyu; Borno State Governor Babagana Umara Zulum; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate; and National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu.

Others were Chief Executive Officer of Oando Plc, Mr Wale Tinubu; Special Adviser to the President on Political Matters, Ibrahim Kabiru Masari; and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, among others.

World.title: N70,000 Transport Allowance: Public Service Unions Back NLC as Labour Rift Deepens
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The disagreement between the two main labour centres, Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and Trade Union Congress (TUC), over the federal government’s N70,000 transportation allowance approved for public servants seemed to be deepening as Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council (JNPSNC) backed NLC against TUC, which rejected the allowance.

National Secretary of JNPSNC, Comrade Gbenga Olowoyo, said, in circular to affiliate unions and state councils, that the agreement leading to approval of the allowance was the product of constructive engagement and exhaustive negotiation.

Olowoyo said the meeting was presided by Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Mohamed Maigari Dingyadi, and attended by a labour team led by NLC President Comrade Joe Ajaero, with the participation of the leadership of JNPSNC and Joint Health Sector Union (JOHESU).

According to the circular, the meeting was tough and lasted more than six hours before both sides reached the terms.

Olowoyo said the N70,000 monthly transportation allowance to be paid for the next six months to public servants, starting November 2026, and it was meant to subsidise unbearable transportation costs being experienced by workers.

He expressed hope that states and local governments, with their current humongous allocations, will be patriotic enough to concur with the agreement to complement the federal government’s effort to ameliorate the hardship of workers and their dependants.

He said the agreement also cemented implementation of long overdue 40 per cent peculiar allowance, reflecting N70,000 minimum wage, which ought to have started since July 2024, when the new minimum wage commenced.

The allowance will be domesticated at sub-national levels from November 2026 while arrears from May 1, 2026 will be paid in three tranches.

Olowoyo stated that the federal government agreed to set up a tripartite negotiation committee comprising government, labour, and Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA) representatives with immediate effect, which formed the focal request from JNPSNC under Comrade Benjamin Anto Uyanto that necessitated the three-day warning strike called on October 2, 2026.

Olowoyo tried to correct what he termed a notion that NLC was a union of junior workers, saying all unions affiliated to NLC have members across Ministries, Departments and Agencies up to Directorate level.

He said the clarification became necessary because of the position taken by TUC, which rejected the allowance, though it was never part of the discussion.

“TUC has explicit right to express opinion on any matter it is directly involved, but not on what it was not part of at any stage of engagement or negotiation with the federal government,” he said.

He, however, said it would be commendable if TUC could secure higher amounts, above the N70,000 already agreed by NLC, JNPSNC and JOHESU.

The circular added that the meeting also resolved other long-standing issues, including CONHESS adjustment demand since the past 13 years. It said National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) was given three weeks to finish work on the adjustment and forward to Presidential Committee on Salaries headed by Minister of Finance, for approval.

It approved payment of 19-month arrears of health workers allowances in three instalments from December 2026, and resolved the issuance of circular for hazard allowance to agricultural professional officers within three weeks.

On tax relief, it was agreed that the matter will be presented to National Economic Council as it involved the federal and state governments.

The meeting gave a window of one month to reconvene to evaluate implementation level.

Olowoyo said rejection of any item by any trade union was inconsequential to implementation because a wider spectrum of workers had applauded the decision as a step in the right direction.

World.title: Hyron Andrews: Funeral details confirmed
World.content:
Last month, much-loved South African rugby player Hyron Andrews passed away in tragic circumstances while on tour with the Lions, and on the eve of the team’s Champions Cup opener.

In an official statement, the cause of death was confirmed to be “a tear in the aorta (due to natural causes)”.

Following the medical examination and his body’s return to South Africa, the service arrangements for the late Hyron Andrews have been shared on behalf of his family.



Although there will be a public memorial service and celebration of life, the funeral service is private and some event details remain to be confirmed.

CONFIRMATION OF EVENTS CELEBRATING THE LIFE OF HYRON ANDREWS

Public Memorial Service

Date: Friday, 6 November 2026

Venue: VGK Hugeunot Church (Paarl)

Time: 18:00

Private Funeral Service (Paarl)



Date: Saturday, 7 November 2026

Celebration of Life

Date: Wednesday, 11 November 2026

Venue: Kings Park Stadium

The Andrews family has shared the following message:

“We would like to sincerely thank everyone for the messages of support and condolences following Hyron’s passing.



“As a family, we are deeply grateful for every message, call and gesture of kindness as we navigate this difficult time.

“Your love and support have carried us, and it means more than words can express.”

death found to be caused by an aortic dissection

According to the statement following Andrews’ autopsy, this “dissection most likely occurred on an aortic aneurysm”.



“The French authorities, who conducted the autopsy and, in whose care Hyron’s body currently remains, described the cause of death as ‘a tear in the aorta (due to natural causes), which led to a significant accumulation of blood within the sac surrounding the heart’,” the statement continued.

“The Andrews family asks for respect, privacy and patience during this difficult time as the repatriation process begins.

“A timeline for the return of Hyron’s body to South Africa has not yet been determined. Further information will be communicated when it becomes available and under the guidance of the family.”

World.title: Mamelodi Sundowns tipped for January clear-out after shock Champions League exit
World.content:
Former Mamelodi Sundowns defender Hilton Jordaan has predicted a major squad overhaul at Chloorkop, with several players potentially leaving the club on loan during the January transfer window.

The Brazilians were dealt a disappointing blow after crashing out of the CAF Champions League, meaning they will have fewer matches to compete in during the second half of the season.

Their attention now shifts to domestic competitions, with the Carling Knockout Cup, Betway Premiership and Nedbank Cup still on their agenda.



Jordaan believes Sundowns could allow some fringe players to leave on loan in January but insists the club is unlikely to dismantle its squad completely.

“I think they may know what to do. I think there might be some players going out on loan in January, but I think they will keep the nucleus of that squad. They still got the Carling Knockout, there’s a league, and there is Nedbank Cup also,” Jordaan told KickOff.

Jordaan reacts to Mamelodi Sundowns’ Champions League exit

The former defender also expressed his surprise at Sundowns’ early elimination from Africa’s premier club competition.

Having won the Champions League last season, the Tshwane giants entered the campaign among the favourites to retain their continental crown.

However, their failure to overcome Angolan opposition proved a major setback, forcing them to shift their attention back to domestic football.

Mamelodi Sundowns wont defend the CAF CL

“It was a shock that they didn’t beat a side from Angola, and now they have to focus on the Carling Knockout. It is a blow for Sundowns because they won the Champions League last season, which made them the tournament’s favourites. So for them to go out in the first round wasn’t part of the plan.”



With fewer continental commitments, Mamelodi Sundowns could use the January transfer window to reassess their squad and give some players opportunities elsewhere through loan moves.

Who should be released?

World.title: MK Party’s Andile Mngxitama on Donovan Marx attack: ‘No land, no peace’
World.content:
MKParty MP Andile Mngxitama has courted controversy over a tweet about North West farmer, Donovan Marx. Images via X

MK Party MP Andile Mngxitama is unfazed by the backlash to his tweet condoning the attack on North West farmer, Donovan Marx.

The outspoken politician, a former member of the EFF who later started his own party,

Black First Land First (BLF), has a has a long history of controversial social media statements, particularly about race, land ownership, white South Africans, and farm attacks.



MK PARTY’S ANDILE MNGIXITAMA’S TWEET ABOUT DONOVAN MAR ATTACK GOES VIRAL

On his X account, Andile Mngxitama tweeted over the weekend: “Ventersdorp white farmer Donovan Marx had his ears cut off during a Plaas moord aanval [farm murder attack]. Attacking the ears is symbolic to denote the refusal of land thieves to listen. No land, no peace.

He added, “Farm life is overdetermined by systematic violence! Blacks got killed and fed to pigs!”

Andile, an MK Party MP, later deleted the tweet but did not deny having posted it.

He responded to his critics: “Job done”, “Point made” and “I said what I said”.

He added: “Cry some more” and “Give the land back first”

Cry some more  November 2, 2026

Plaas moord is the thing — ANDILE MNGXITAMA (MP) (@Mngxitama2) November 1, 2026

BACKLASH AND CALL FOR ACTION

Andile Mngxitama’s tweet about Donovan Marx’s gruesome farm attack has elicited widespread backlash on social media.

FFP MP Renaldo Gouws responded to the tweet, urging the public to report the comments to the South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC). He also called on Mngxitama to be formally removed from parliament.

Sunette Bridges, the daughter of Bles Bridges, claimed that Mngxitama was “revelling” in Marx’s injuries.

“This cannot be allowed to continue”, she appealed to the government.

Former Olympic swimmer Roland Schoeman tweeted from his X account: “These statements deserve international scrutiny and a formal response. How much more explicit does the rhetoric need to become before it is taken seriously?”

CHARGES BY AFRIFORUM

Meanwhile, AfriForum has vowed to take legal action against Andile Mngxitama over his racially charged tweet.

The Afrikaner activism organisation added that it would “deploy all necessary resources to ensure that he is held accountable”.

World.title: New medical school puts this North West city in the property spotlight
World.content:
Potchefstroom’s property market is attracting younger buyers, with a new medical school expected to add further demand. Image: wikimedia common

A new medical school could further boost the residential property market in the North West’s city of Potchefstroom, attracting more students, academics, healthcare professionals, and businesses.

North-West University’s (NWU) new Desmond Tutu School of Medicine is being developed at its Potchefstroom campus, with construction having started in 2025.

The school will become South Africa’s 11th medical school, with its first students expected to enrol in 2028.



According to Pam Golding Properties area principal Ferdi Coetzee, the development could have a significant long-term impact on the city.

“Together with continued investment in the university and surrounding infrastructure, it has the potential to attract additional professionals, students and businesses,” he says.

Younger buyers enter the PROPERTY market

The medical school comes as the city’s property market is already attracting a broader range of buyers.

Approximately 28% of buyers are now younger purchasers, including young professionals, couples and families looking for secure, modern and low-maintenance homes.

The market continues to benefit from its established student, investor and retirement segments, as well as the surrounding agricultural economy.

Affordability remains important, with a shortage of well-maintained family homes below R1.5 million. Properties in this price range can sell relatively quickly.



SO, what can you buy IN POTCHEFSTROOM?

The market offers a wide range of options depending on budget.

Budget What you can get R500,000 Sectional-title units at estates such as Waterberry, while vacant stands at Ailanto Country Estate start at around R440 000 R1 million Smaller sectional-title properties, including a one-bedroom Die Bult apartment priced at about R1.025 million R2 million Family homes in areas such as Potchefstroom South and Miederpark, as well as sectional-title properties at Tuscany Ridge R4 million Larger freehold homes, including properties in Hillside Estate and higher-end homes in Van der Hoff Park and Tuscany Ridge

At the student-property end of the market, Die Bult remains a major investment hotspot because of its proximity to NWU.

Approximately 82.5% of properties in Die Bult are sectional title, with a median sales price of R625 000 in 2026 to date. One- and two-bedroom units are particularly popular among investors and parents buying accommodation for students.

Medical school adds another layer of demand

The medical school is unlikely to transform the property market overnight, but it could provide another long-term source of demand in an already diverse market.

The university’s existing student population, established residential areas and investor market are now being joined by the potential growth associated with the medical school.

“The strength of [the city] is that it is not driven by a single demographic,” Coetzee says.

For property buyers and investors, this means the market ranges from affordable sectional-title accommodation and family homes to secure estates and higher-end lifestyle properties.

According to Coetzee, properties that combine affordability, security, good location and strong rental or resale potential are likely to remain among the strongest opportunities.

World.title: Special voting begins as thunderstorms threaten power and communication services
World.content:
Severe thunderstorms could disrupt power and communication services in parts of South Africa as special voting begins. Image: Pexels

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has warned that severe thunderstorms could cause localised disruptions to electricity and communication services in affected areas as special voting gets underway.

SAWS has issued a Yellow Level 1 warning for severe thunderstorms in several areas, including parts of Gauteng and the Free State.

The warning highlights possible localised flooding, damage to property and temporary structures, and disruptions to power supply and communications.



Which areas face severe thunderstorm warning?

According to SAWS, the Yellow Level 1 warning covers:

Southern parts of Gauteng.

Eastern parts of the Free State.

Extreme south-western parts of Mpumalanga.

Extreme north-eastern escarpment areas of the Eastern Cape.

Could thunderstorms affect special voting?

Special voting takes place on Monday, 2 November, and Tuesday, 3 November, ahead of the main voting day.

The warning raises concerns about possible interruptions to electricity and communication services in affected communities.

However, SAWS has not specifically warned that voting operations will be disrupted, and the weather warning does not mean polling stations will necessarily experience problems.

Why are power and communication services at risk?

Severe thunderstorms can damage electricity infrastructure when lightning strikes equipment or strong winds bring down trees and power lines.

Heavy rainfall can also flood electrical installations, while damaged infrastructure may interrupt mobile network services.



SAWS has identified these as possible impacts of Monday’s thunderstorms. However, the warning does not confirm that any outages have occurred.

What should voters know?

The IEC has approved more than 2.6 million applications for special voting, including voters who will cast their ballots at voting stations and those who qualify for home visits.

Voters should follow official weather updates and announcements from the IEC throughout the two-day special voting period.

Residents in affected areas should monitor SAWS warnings and updates from their municipalities.

Anyone who experiences an electricity or communication outage should report it to the relevant service provider.

The weather warning remains subject to updates as conditions change.

World.title: Fernando Da Cruz still believes Kaizer Chiefs can win the league
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head coach Fernando Da Cruz has refused to concede that his team is out of the title race.

This comes after Amakhosi‘s 2-1 defeat to Orlando Pirates in the Soweto Derby this past weekend. A loss sees Chiefs 11 points behind Pirates after nine matches played.

Da Cruz, though, feels there are still 21 matches to play and his team are not out of the title picture yet.



“I will say that it is more difficult today after this game but the PSL is a long journey so there is 21 fixtures remaining but when we recover our injured players, because we have been unlucky since the start of the season, we will have more consistency in our performance because we had a lot of draws this season but we deserved to win this game but because of our lack of expereince we didn’t win this game but it will turn in our favour when we recover our full squad,” said da Cruz as per SABC Sport.

Da Cruz takes lesson from Chiefs loss to Pirates

Da Cruz said the Soweto Derby was a good experiene for some of the younger players in the team.

“It’s a good question – we must use these types of games to grow players and to reach the next steps. The players must understand that even though we play well, it’s not enough – we must reach the next steps now. So, we must continue to work, but it takes time. We can’t achieve this overnight – we can’t gain experience from one day to the next. We must continue to learn from competitions of different levels.”

Da Cruz’s next task with Chiefs will be the Carling Knockout as he seeks to win his first trophy in South Africa.

World.title: South African company takes education investment to rural Zim
World.content:
A South African investment company has contributed to efforts to strengthen science education at a rural secondary school in Zimbabwe after partnering with a local foundation to deliver a fully equipped laboratory.

Afribiz Invest was involved in the construction of the science facility at Sojini Secondary School in Mbembesi Village, outside Bulawayo, which was officially handed over on Saturday, October 31, following a 14-day construction period.

The initiative was spearheaded by Zimbabwean businesswoman Zodwa Mkandla through the Zodwa Mkandla Foundation, highlighting the role of cross-border business partnerships and private-sector support in improving educational infrastructure.



According to The Herald, the laboratory has a capacity of 60 learners and is expected to give pupils greater opportunities to conduct practical experiments rather than rely exclusively on theoretical lessons.

The facility could also help learners interested in pursuing careers in science, technology, engineering and medicine.

Afribiz Invest is an infrastructure, property, construction and investment group founded in South Africa in 2005.



The company operates across several African markets, including Zimbabwe, where it established Afribiz Zimbabwe in 2013, according to its corporate website.

Its involvement in the Sojini project highlights the contribution that businesses operating across national borders can make to community development.

The laboratory initiative also received technical support from Laboratory Equipment and Consumables (Private) Limited, according to The Herald.



Zimbabwean businesswoman invests in former school

Mkandla’s involvement in the project carries a personal connection, as she attended Sojini Secondary School before returning to support learners from her former community.

Speaking at the handover ceremony, she said she wanted children from the area to have opportunities to become doctors, engineers, pharmacists and biologists.

The project also extended beyond education, with the foundation distributing food parcels, blankets and wheelchairs to vulnerable elderly residents.



Nearly 400 schoolgirls also received sanitary pads.

The handover was attended by senior government officials, including Primary and Secondary Education Minister Torerayi Moyo, who represented First Lady Auxillia Mnangagwa.

The laboratory’s long-term impact will depend on its accessibility to learners, the availability of qualified science teachers and the consistent provision of materials needed for practical lessons.

World.title: India's royals find new power in their past
World.content:
MUMBAI - In a sprawling palace in western India, the "queen" or Maharani of Baroda welcomes guests with fragrant rose petals, presenting torchlit dances of Hindu myths.

Dressed in glittering finery, Radhikaraje Gaekwad is a queen in name only, a modern businesswoman presiding over a world her ancestors once ruled.

"The key has been that we have adapted," 48-year-old Gaekwad told AFP in her vast Lakshmi Vilas Palace, describing how India's former royals have found new roles, from cultural ambassadors to politics.

"My work has always been to try and bring in change for what I feel would be for the betterment of society," said Gaekwad, who works to preserve art accumulated by generations of rulers.

"A glimpse of what was left behind... can bring that sense of identity and pride back in their roots, and help them in the future."

Under British rule, more than 565 princely states enjoyed nominal autonomy across roughly 40 percent of the land. Baroda, today Vadodara in Gujarat state, was among the most powerful.

World.title: Host of fresh faces in Australia white-ball squads to face England
World.content:
MELBOURNE - Australia named a host of fresh faces in new-look white-ball squads to face England, with exciting young quick Mahli Beardman and all-rounders Jack Edwards and Liam Scott among those getting call-ups.

Batting prospects Ollie Peake and Jake Fraser-McGurk were also included, as were wicketkeepers Lachlan Shaw and Sam Harper with Mitchell Marsh captaining both the one-day and Twenty20 sides.

"These ODI and T20 matches provide several players, many of whom have had opportunities on recent tours, with a great chance to further demonstrate their ability against very strong opposition," said chairman of selectors George Bailey.

Beardman, Peake, Edwards, Scott, Nikhil Chaudhary, and Joel Davies made their white-ball debuts in recent times. Harper and Shaw are the two uncapped players.

"They are good examples of players who have had an opportunity at the international level and have continued working on their game from what they learnt from those experiences," added Bailey.

Australia play three home ODIs against England between November 13-18 followed by five T20s.

They will provide an opportunity for Australia's next generation to stake their claims ahead of the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia.

With a home Test series against New Zealand to follow, star fast bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood are being rested after playing their part in Australia's 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa.

Fellow Test players Travis Head, Alex Carey, Matt Renshaw, Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and Cameron Green were named in the ODI squad, but will not play the T20s.

Following the New Zealand series, Australia travel to India for five Tests before a 150th anniversary clash in Melbourne against England then an Ashes campaign.

"We are in the middle of a highly demanding phase of our schedule," said Bailey, referring to Australia's Test players.

"To manage this workload, each player's build-up to the New Zealand series will be carefully planned and focused on individual's physical and mental preparation."

World.title: Violence after Germany's 'Gen Z' demos slammed by politicians
World.content:
BERLIN - Multiple German politicians on Sunday criticised clashes and looting the day before on the margins of youth-led demonstrations, though several also warned that the acts should not eclipse the protesters' demands.

Such "violent acts" were "totally unacceptable", the minister-president for the state of Hesse, Boris Rhein, said on X.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, speaking to the Bild daily, blamed the unrest on "leftist groups inclined to violence and troublemakers from migrant communities".

He said, however, that he viewed the disturbances as less severe "than those that took place in Paris".

On Saturday, tens of thousands of people participated in the protests organised by the group "GenZ regelt!" (Gen Z has got this!) to demand attention to youth priorities, ranging from the cost of living to education spending and budget cuts.

On the sidelines, masked rioters looted shops in Frankfurt, and violence broke out in major cities including Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. Police fired water cannons at youths hurling Molotov cocktails.

The demonstrations were inspired by similar movements in France and Italy.

The head of Germany's far-left Die Linke (The Left) party, Ines Schwerdtner, told the Rheinische Post daily that the demands made by those "demonstrating peacefully will not disappear because small angry groups followed up with acts of vandalism".

The co-head of the Greens party, Franziska Brantner, criticised the violence, which she told the same outlet "harmed the legitimate cause of many people who demonstrated peacefully".

The far-right AfD (Alternative for Germany) party blamed left-wing "extremism" and "uncontrolled migration" for the violence.

The "Gen Z regelt!" movement said on its website that it was calling for fresh demonstrations on November 14, calling them "just the start".

World.title: SA's AGOA future hangs in the balance as US reviews eligibility
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa maintains a trade surplus with the United States, a position that is not unique but is unusual for a developing country.

The benefits South Africa enjoys under the US African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) are particularly significant for the agricultural sector, including processed fruit, nuts, wine and other commodities.

Agricultural economist Wandile Sihlobo says the country’s citrus and nut industries are relatively resilient as South Africa awaits a US decision on its continued eligibility for AGOA.

South Africa is expected to find out on Monday whether it will retain preferential access to the American market under the Act.

Trade and Industry Minister Parks Tau says the government remains hopeful of a favourable outcome, following engagements with US officials over the past year.

World.title: Elections 2026 | President Ramaphosa calls for peaceful polls
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - President Cyril Ramaphosa has called on South Africans to ensure that this week’s local government elections are free from violence, following police warnings that 331 voting stations have been identified as high-risk areas.

In his weekly letter to the nation, Ramaphosa urged all registered voters to head to the polls on Wednesday and exercise their democratic right.

“I call on all registered voters to go out to the polling stations on Wednesday because local government is essential to improving the quality of life of citizens,” he wrote.

The President emphasised that the outcome of the elections will have a direct impact on the daily delivery of essential services to communities.

He also highlighted the importance of strengthening municipalities through the proposed White Paper on Local Government, which aims to improve their ability to fulfil their responsibilities.

Ramaphosa said the proposed reforms would focus on professionalising municipalities, building administrative capacity and ensuring that local government officials are appointed based on their qualifications and competence.

READ | Ekurhuleni pensioners endure 51 days of water woes as they cast special votes

He stressed that accountability must remain a priority, warning that those responsible for the misuse of public funds, manipulation of procurement processes and neglect of public duties must be held accountable.

“The White Paper recommends changes to professionalise municipalities and build their administrative capacity. Local government structures must be led and staffed by people appointed for their qualifications and competence. Those responsible must be held to account if public resources are stolen, procurement is manipulated or public duties are neglected.”

World.title: LIVESTREAM | AKA and Tibz murder trial resumes in Durban High Court
World.content:
DURBAN - The trial of seven men accused of the murders of award-winning rapper Kiernan “AKA” Forbes and his close friend, celebrity chef Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane resumes in the Durban High Court on Monday.

All seven accused have pleaded not guilty to the charges of murder and other related offences.

Proceedings are expected to focus on the cross-examination of car-tracking witness Carl Dreyer Rothman by the defence.

READ | CCTV footage takes centre stage in AKA and Tibz murder trial

The court has previously heard evidence relating to two rental vehicles allegedly used to track AKA and Tibz in the days leading up to their fatal shooting.

CCTV footage has also played a key role in the proceedings, with investigators using the recordings to piece together a timeline of events before the shooting.

World.title: Reporter Diaries | North West faces growing unemployment crisis
World.content:
MAHIKENG - North West is rich in minerals, but this is not translating into job creation.

Small businesses battle to grow despite the area's mining and agricultural potential.

The province has the highest labour underutilisation rate in the country, with unemployment climbing to 38%.

eNCA's Bafedile Moerane has more.

World.title: Elections 2026 | Police urged to focus on hotspots
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police have been urged to closely monitor areas identified as high-risk for election-related violence ahead of this week's Local Government Elections.

Security strategist Andy Mashaile says intelligence gathering and proactive policing will be critical to ensuring safe polls.

Police have identified 331 voting stations across the country as high-risk, with KwaZulu-Natal accounting for the highest number.

Mashaile says intelligence teams should pay particular attention to areas where political killings and tensions have been reported.

He cites Bekkersdal, particularly the X Section, as an area requiring close monitoring.

Mashaile says intelligence gathering should include examining political conflicts, councillor killings and organisational disputes that could heighten tensions around election day.

He says, however, that his engagements with communities suggest there is little appetite for violence, with residents keen to exercise their right to vote.

World.title: Activists move to court to stop Bayern Munich-Ajax match over Sh724.6m cost
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Six Kenyans have moved to court seeking to stop the planned Bayern Munich-Ajax friendly match at Talanta Stadium over concerns about the reported Sh724.6 million appearance fee and secrecy surrounding the Government's financing arrangements.

The petition filed at the Milimani High Court's Constitutional and Human Rights Division on Monday, November 1, 2026, challenges the proposed international friendly scheduled for January 5, 2027, at the Talanta Stadium, now named the Raila Odinga International Stadium.

The six petitioners, Erick Sayialel Mankuyu, Julius Kimani Kamau, Dickson Kimathi Muli, Nicholas Ochieng Oyoo, Mulinge Muteti and Collins Otieno want the court to restrain the Government from committing public funds or resources towards hosting the two European football giants pending determination of the case.

The petition, filed through lawyer John Mana Ndegwa on behalf of the petitioners, seeks orders restraining the Attorney General, Sports Cabinet Secretary, National Treasury Cabinet Secretary and Sports Kenya from committing public funds or resources, including personnel, security, transport and Talanta Stadium facilities, towards the proposed friendly match.

"The Petitioners therefore seek conservatory orders restraining the Respondents from authorising, allocating, releasing, committing or expending public funds towards the proposed event unless such expenditure is demonstrated to comply with the Constitution and applicable financial laws," Lawyer Ndegwa states.

In their petition, the activists argue that although President William Ruto announced that the match would be delivered through corporate partnerships and a self-sustaining commercial model, the Government has not disclosed the complete financial arrangements.

They are particularly concerned about reports that Bayern Munich would receive approximately five million euros (Sh724.6 million) in appearance fees, arguing that the figure and other associated costs require official verification.

In their supporting affidavit, they state: "We emphasise that the reported amount has not been independently verified by us and that we seek official disclosure and verification from the Respondents."

The petition further seeks orders compelling the Government to disclose the identities of the corporate sponsors, their respective financial contributions and obligations, as well as the detailed budget for appearance fees, travel, accommodation, security, insurance, hospitality and other logistical expenses.

The activists argue that describing the event as privately sponsored does not automatically establish that taxpayers will be shielded from financial obligations.

They want the respondents to disclose whether public funds, government guarantees, subsidies, indemnities, public personnel, security services, transport facilities or other government resources will be committed towards the match.

In their notice of motion, the activists are seeking an order restraining the respondents from committing public resources towards the match.

They also want the court to compel the respondents to produce, within seven days, complete sponsorship agreements, contracts and correspondence relating to the event.

In the application, the petitioners warn that unless the court intervenes, public resources could be committed before Kenyans are informed of the financial obligations arising from the match.

"Unless conservatory orders are granted, public resources, including Talanta Stadium facilities, a facility developed using public resources, public personnel, security, and transport, may be committed irreversibly, and financial records may be altered," the petitioners state in their certificate of urgency.

They argue that the Constitution requires public finance to be managed with openness, accountability and prudent use of public resources, insisting that Kenyans have a right to know how public institutions and taxpayer-funded infrastructure will be used.

President William Ruto announced the fixture on October 28, 2026, describing it as an event to be delivered through corporate partnerships and a self-sustaining commercial model.

However, the petitioners argue that describing the match as privately sponsored does not automatically rule out direct or indirect financial obligations on taxpayers.

They insist they are not opposed to international sporting events but want accountability over public resources, arguing that Talanta Stadium should also promote local sporting talent, employment and sustainable economic opportunities.

The petitioners want the matter certified urgent and heard on a priority basis ahead of the scheduled match.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.

World.title: Not so fast! Court blocks Bomas expansion
World.content:
Contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site. [File, Standard]

The Environment and Lands Court has blocked the government from continuing with the construction of a car park inside the Nairobi National Park.

Justice Grace Kemei, in her ruling, said that the contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.
