World.title: Function of Croatian Judiciary Facing Serious Problems Once Again
World.content:
November the 1st, 2026 – The very function of the Croatian judiciary is facing serious problems yet again due to some judges refusing to participate in proceedings if they’re recorded.

President of the Constitutional Court Frane Staničić stated that the Court will function with great difficulty due to the decision of some judges not to participate in sessions that are audio-recorded. Index reports that in an interview for RTL Danas he revealed that he is extremely sorry that individual judges, as he believes, have stopped providing protection to citizens within the judiciary system. These are judges Andrej Abramović, Sanja Bezbradica Jelavić and Lovorka Kušan, who oppose the way in which the audio recording of sessions was introduced. They claim that no appropriate decision of the Court was adopted and refuse to participate in sessions which, in their opinion, are being recorded unlawfully.

“we really tried hard to come to an agreement”

Staničić said that the judges during the past year invested great effort so that the Constitutional Court would function normally and protect the rights of citizens. As an example he cited decisions on politically sensitive laws, among which are the Act on Building Management and the Act on Local Taxes. He emphasised that the decisions on those laws were adopted by a large majority, with only one or two votes against. He added that the number of separate opinions has significantly decreased, which according to his interpretation shows that the judges sought to reach agreement. “Unfortunately, due to the refusal of certain colleagues to participate in the work of the constitutional court bodies because of the introduced audio recording, the system will function with great difficulty,” Staničić said.

When asked why he introduced recording without a decision of all the judges, Staničić confirmed that there was no formal decision of the Constitutional Court as a collegial body. He claims, however, that there was an informal agreement and that all judges were familiar with the procurement and installation of the equipment. “I warned the judges several times that we would buy the system, that we had procured it, installed it and that we were testing it. At the session on the 6th of October, which was also recorded, I said in front of everyone that from that day, in accordance with the agreement, the sessions are being recorded. No one reacted to that,” he explained. He also commented on the appearance of judge Andrej Abramović, who had been a guest on RTL the day before. Staničić believes that Abramović should have pointed out his disagreement before the conflict among the judges arose because of the recording.

the introduction of audio recording doesn’t require the permission of all judges

“He said in your programme that he practically knew that recording was taking place, or rather that recording would be introduced, but that I am neither his father nor mother, so he would not warn me that something is not good,” Staničić said. “I’d like to openly ask the public to judge – is it in accordance with the role of a Constitutional Court judge that if he considers that something is not good, he collegially warns the President of the Court that he considers that this should not be done, or that he remains silent and then on the basis of his unexpressed disagreement creates this problem that has now occurred?” he added.

Staničić claims that he did not need a special decision of all the judges to introduce audio recording because as President he has the authority to decide on the manner of establishing the minutes. As the main reason for introducing recording he cited earlier disagreements about the content of the minutes of the sessions.

“I introduced audio recording for a simple reason: we had a series of problems with establishing the authenticity of the minutes. It happened that colleagues claim that something stands in the minutes that should not stand and vice versa,” he explained. As a particularly problematic case he cited the events from May of this year, when the judges discussed the composition of the panels of the Constitutional Court. According to his words, it was precisely the judges who now oppose the recording who at that time contested the minutes.

“The judges who today contest the audio recording at that time contested the minutes that were signed by two minute-takers and whose accuracy was confirmed by five judges. In such circumstances there is no other way to ensure an authentic record that no one will be able to contest,” Staničić said.

should some sessions be completely open to the public?

The President of the Constitutional Court believes that audio recording should contribute to transparency and the possibility of verifying what was said at the sessions. He also announced that he wants to open a discussion on the possibility that part of the sessions of the Constitutional Court will in future be accessible to the public.

“I personally believe that the Court should be more open to the public in general. I can announce that I will initiate a serious discussion at the Constitutional Court on the Court becoming more open, that perhaps even part of the sessions will be public,” he stated. He emphasised that the main task of the Constitutional Court is the protection of citizens’ rights, but he believes that due to the current conflict that task has fallen into the background. He also rejected claims that the recordings of the sessions are his private documentation.

“This is official documentation created in official premises, with official equipment, and is stored on the official servers and information system of the Constitutional Court,” he said.

Staničić claims that every judge can access the recordings and listen to them. He rejected the claim of judge Abramović that access was denied to someone, but at the same time emphasised that a distinction must be made between the possibility of listening and obtaining one’s own copy of the recording. “I received a request for a copy of the recording. Here a distinction must be made between the possibility of listening, which is absolutely not disputed, and the question of copies. I replied only to the colleague who requested it that her request will be considered in terms of scope and possibilities. Therefore, such a request has by no means been rejected,” he stated.

no agreement has been reached at all

In order to resolve the dispute, Staničić proposed the establishment of a working group that would prepare rules on audio recording. It would include him, the Secretary General of the Constitutional Court and one of the judges who oppose the recording. “Unfortunately, I did not receive a positive answer because participation in the working group is conditioned on the cessation of audio recording. I have already explained that this is impossible, because it is the only way in which I can ensure authenticity,” he said.

Staničić stated that one of the three judges who opposed the recording nevertheless participated in a session, although she retained her opposition. He believes that the remaining two judges could have done the same so that the work of the Court would not be hindered. “Unfortunately, the other two judges did not want to follow that example. They could have retained their opposition, but we want to protect citizens. However, they chose the opposite – not to protect the rights of citizens, but to deepen the conflict, which is unnecessary,” he said.

a new session has been announced for november the 13th

The President of the Constitutional Court said that he has no mechanisms by which he could force the judges to participate in the work. Nevertheless, he hopes that everyone will accept the responsibility they have towards citizens and enable the continuation of regular work. He announced that he will schedule a new session as soon as the two judges who oppose the recording return from an official trip, which he expects to take place on or around the 13th of November. In the meantime the question remains open whether an agreement will be reached on the manner of recording the sessions.

Staničić also said that the Constitutional Court has received requests from GONG, the media and citizens for access to the audio recordings. He emphasised that this is sensitive documentation that may contain secret data and that he cannot make it public on his own. Due to the great public interest he announced that he will seek the consent of all constitutional judges for the publication of the recordings. If he obtains it, he is ready to publish them, and if someone opposes it, he announced that he will publicly say who was against.

“This is a very sensitive issue and secret data that I cannot just give out. However, given the extreme importance of the issue and the interest of the public, I will propose and seek a consensus of all judges that the recordings be given to the public. If a consensus is reached, I will give the recordings. If it is not reached, if even one judge is against, I will publicly announce which judges were against it,” Staničić concluded.

World.title: Russian citizen expelled to 'prevent activities' that 'threaten' Estonia
World.content:
Estonia's Internal Security Service (KAPO) said on Monday that a Russian citizen had been expelled from Estonia to "prevent and counter activities" that "threaten" Europe on its recommendation. The agency said he has links to the Russian intellegence services.

Kapo said it had recommended that Russian citizen Leonid Karabeshkin (Estonian spelling: Karabeškin) be sent out of Estonia and banned him from entering the Schengen area.

It posted the statement on X along with a video of a man being escorted by two police officers to the Russian border.

"The aim of the expulsion is to prevent and counter activities that threaten the security of Estonia and Europe more broadly," KAPO wrote.

@Politsei saatis KAPO ettepanekul Eestist välja Venemaa kodaniku Leonid Karabeskini ning kehtestas talle Schengeni sissesõidukeelu. Väljasaatmise eesmärk on ennetada ja tõkestada Eesti ning laiemalt Euroopa julgeolekut ohustavat tegevust. https://t.co/CQDTtZ7Jge — Kaitsepolitseiamet (@kaitsepolitsei) November 2, 2026

Links to Russian intellegence

Kapo spokesperson Marta Tuul told ERR that Karabeshkin had connections with Russian intelligence services and people working on their behalf.

"He regularly traveled to Russia and met with them there. Several of them have been sanctioned by the European Union and Ukraine for carrying out Russia's hostile influence activities. And he is linked to influence networks such as CIRP, RuBaltic and Regnum, as well as individuals associated with them," she said.

"In the case of Regnum, we are talking about Sergei Rekeda and also Sergei Rudnov. The latter is also on the United Kingdom's and Ukraine's sanctions lists. CIRP is the Center for International and Regional Policy of Russia, and he worked there as a project manager, while several people with FSB backgrounds have participated in events organized by the center," Tuul explained.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said Estonia will not turn a blind eye to threats to our security or that of Europe.

"Those with links to Russian intelligence services and hostile influence networks have no place exploiting our openness. One such individual has now been expelled from Estonia and barred from entering the Schengen area. Rightly so. We will not tolerate activities that undermine our security," he said.

World.title: Second-pillar fund withdrawers can start saving again this month
World.content:
People who withdrew their second-pillar pension savings following reforms can, five years on, start contributing again from this month, and experts urge them to do so.

Estonia's pension system rests on three pillars: the state-funded first pillar, the previously mandatory funded second paid from social tax and gross salary, and the voluntary third (private pensions plan).

Second-pillar contributions became voluntary in 2021, and about a third of savers withdrew their funds following the changes, with the first major wave in September that year.

Applications to resume contributions can be submitted and were open from November 1. Those who left in the first wave can begin making contributions in May 2027; the rule is that five years must elapse between leaving the pillar and restarting .

Commenting on how things have developed since 2021, Heidi Reinson, a researcher in economic behavior at the University of Tartu, said: "There were more people who had no other savings, such as a third pension pillar or other financial reserves. Among them were many people who had high-interest payday loans hanging over their heads, as well as large families. But what is perhaps most interesting is that trust in the state, the financial sector and the media was much lower among those who left the second pillar."

A third of the withdrawn money went on loan repayments, while nearly a fifth went straight into consumption. On the latter, Reinson recalled anecdotal stories of televisions bought at the Ülemiste mall which were too large to fit into taxis.

A year after the reforms, half the money was sitting in people's current accounts.

Pension fund assets currently total €8 billion, but without the withdrawals they would amount to €11 billion. Age Petter, head of Swedbank Investment Funds, noted someone earning the average salary had accumulated just over €8,000 by 2021 — but would now have seen that grow to around €20,000 had they not withdrawn.

Investor Kristjan Liivamägi said the state adds €80 for every €40 a person contributes. "If we take the average Estonian earning a gross salary of €2,000 a month, then two percent of their salary goes into their second pension pillar. That's about €40. The state adds another €80 from social tax," he said. A 45-year-old on that salary would accumulate around €63,000 by retirement, assuming no salary growth and returns of about 7 percent a year.

Reinson warned of a longer-term consequence: a wealth gap between savers and non-savers. "People regret not having saved, and then that wave of regret will be even stronger. Then you see that your colleague, who has been earning the same average salary as you, is in a much better position when they retire," she added.

World.title: Hackers raised freezer temperature at Estonian supermarket chain to +50°C
World.content:
An Estonian supermarket chain has been hit by a cyber attack which saw attackers access a computer controlling refrigeration, and setting a freezer to 50 degrees above zero.

Jann Mutso, CEO of Kitman Coldtech, which makes the affected tech, said one of its clients was attacked, adding that other Estonian clients have also been hit. The methods match similar attacks seen in France and the Netherlands last month.

Mutso declined to tell ERR which store's cooling system had been the victim, and said due to a swift response no wide-ranging damage was caused by the sudden temperature spike.

"One of our clients was attacked," Mutso said, describing the victim as a "large chain store". He continued: "More has happened. I don't know exactly yet, but other clients in Estonia have also been attacked, not only ours. This is very fresh, it happened this morning."

The attackers gained access to the control computer of an older type of Danfoss refrigeration system and raised its temperature to 50 degrees above zero, much as had happened in the incidents in France and the Netherlands recently.

"The signature is the same, but I can't comment further yet," Mutso said.

Mutso said it is normal in large food stores for refrigeration systems to be digital and connected to the network, but that the current attack had sought specific security holes. Supermarkets are tackling the issue, he said.

"All the store chains have started fighting this and have updated their controllers, but there are also places where the controllers are old and not updated, and it is those which are being targeted now," he continued.

He said he the current incident was responded to within 10 minutes of being reported, meaning no damage was caused. However, disrupting digital systems can directly impact on food safety and cause significant damage, Mutso added.

According to information on Kitman Coldtech's website, its clients include four major supermarket chains in Estonia: Selver, Rimi, Coop and Lidl.

World.title: Tartu's Christmas village takes shape ahead of First Advent opening
World.content:
Tartu is once again transforming Town Hall Square for the holidays, with an outdoor ice rink, Christmas tree and festive pavilions set to open November 29.

Construction of the public ice rink began Monday, marking the start of preparations for Tartu Christmas City 2026. As in previous years, festivities will officially kick off on the first Sunday of Advent.

This year, the city's official Christmas tree will arrive from the Peipsiääre Municipality village of Välgi on November 17.

Its owners, Roman Gelokhov and his family, decided to donate the nearly 15-meter-tall spruce after growing concerned that frequent strong winds in the area made its proximity to their house dangerous.

"We were worried that the tree could eventually fall on the house one day," Gelokhov said. "When the opportunity came up to give our spruce a new life as Tartu's Christmas tree, we thought it was a wonderful solution."

Tartu's Christmas village. November 30, 2024. Source: Airika Harrik/ERR

The family regularly spends time at Town Hall Square during the holiday season, but this year's festivities will now be especially meaningful.

"It'll be something special to see a tree that was once part of our home now decorate Tartu and bring holiday cheer to thousands of people," Gelokhov added.

More info to come

Meanwhile, work on the Christmas village pavilions and other infrastructure is scheduled to begin November 23, with cafes and skating equipment arriving afterward.

The public ice rink, built around Tartu's iconic Kissing Students statue and fountain, will be among the main attractions.

During construction, visitors are asked to take care when crossing the square, as the ice rink site is fenced off and construction equipment moves around the area.

More details and event info for the Christmas village will be published online in the coming weeks.

Overhead view of the Christmas village in Tartu's Town Hall Square. Source: Peeter Paaver

World.title: Põltsamaa school hires security amid ongoing student disruptions
World.content:
Põltsamaa Basic School is bringing in security patrols and equipping staff with panic buttons after repeated disruptions by a small group of students.

The school's Põltsamaa campus has 603 students, but a small handful of sixth- and seventh-graders has been causing ongoing problems with their conduct, said principal Henry Kallaste.

"They skip school, and when they do show up, they disrupt classes, run through the halls and kick trash cans," Kallaste said. This in turn distracts other students, even leaving some classmates frightened.

The final straw, he said, was when the students in question broke into the school building one evening.

Starting Monday, the school and municipality will bring in security guards and give staff panic buttons to summon security when needed. The goal, Kallaste explained, is to allow students to learn and teachers to teach in peace, while giving parents confidence that their children are safe.

Mayor Taavi Aas said the municipality had contacted police, but patrols are not always readily available in smaller towns. For now, Põltsamaa Municipality has hired private security through the end of the year, at a cost of a few thousand euros a month.

Põltsamaa Municipal Mayor Taavi Aas. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"It's not prohibitively expensive, but of course it will depend on how often staff use the panic buttons and how many calls security responds to," he added.

Mayor: Current measures 'don't work on everyone'

Aas said officials are continuing to work with the students to change their behavior, but the process can be a lengthy one, particularly for kids under 14. Seeking a court order for placement in a secure educational facility is a multi-step process requiring extensive evidence, he explained.

The municipal mayor added that the situation in Põltsamaa reflects a broader nationwide problem, arguing that a sense of impunity among kids under 14 can breed trouble in other municipalities as well.

"The only measures we can use to guide them are persuasion, talking to them and social programs," Aas said. "Unfortunately, that doesn't work on everyone."

He argued that some sort of disciplinary measure should be easier to impose, warning that delays in the current process allow disruptive behavior to continue and affect others.

World.title: Skater Niina Petrõkina sets PB to take silver in Canada
World.content:
Estonian figure skater Niina Petrõkina set a new personal best and finished second at the Grand Prix stage in Kelowna, British Columbia.

The reigning and two-time European champion placed third after the short program. She had had planned to open her free skate with a quadruple salchow — a jump she has landed well in training in Canada — but opted instead for a clean triple. Her other jumps landed well too, and her step sequence and spins were graded level four.

This brought her a score of 143.83 for the free skate, just below the PB she set at this year's European Championships, where she took gold with 145.53. Her combined total of 221.07 improved on the 216.14 she recorded in January, however, giving a new PB across both programs.

This is her second career Grand Prix medal, after third place at the US stage last season.

The result was also a great birthday present for Petrõkina's coach, Svetlana Varnavskaja.

Mao Shimad (Japan), the four-time junior world champion who turned 18 recently, won her first senior Grand Prix title, scoring 153.33 in the free skate for a combined 235.44.

American Isabeau Levito came third.

World.title: Soomaa farmers lose 150 cattle to wolves as court blocks hunting permit
World.content:
Farmers in Soomaa in southwest Estonia have been facing wolf attacks on livestock as well as bears destroying feed. Hunting permits were suspended soon after being issued.

While the Environmental Board issued hunting permits, following the attacks, courts suspended them within hours following a legal challenge. Wolf cull season starts in November in any case.

Farmer Tiit Soa, who raises cattle in Soomaa, told "Aktuaalne kaamera" he had never before seen wolf attacks on this scale, and even larger livestock like cows have not escaped the wolves. Soa says he has lost as many as 150 cattle, a quarter of his total herd, to wolf attacks.

The Environmental Board puts the number of cases of wolf attacks this year, up to October 30, at just one more than that – 151.

"The number of large predators needs to be brought under control, and common sense is needed," Soa said.

Some of Tiit Soa's cattle. Source: ERR

Soa estimates the economic loss resulting from the attacks to be around two hundred thousand euros. To qualify for compensation, however, owners must first have implemented all preventive measures, including the installation of electric fences.

However, as a boggy area, the natural conditions in Soomaa, a national park, are distinct, so much so that the large fluctuations in water levels make it almost impossible to install an electric fence which would meet the board's requirements, Soa said.

"The Environmental Board says you have to erect a fence. We built that fence, and the wolf came that very night and killed two calves straight away. The only thing that helps is physically standing guard over the herd, occasionally setting off fireworks rockets and driving around."

Soa has to effectively maintain guard on his livestock round the clock, which he said is starting to affect his health.

According to the Ministry of Climate, responsibility for the herd lies primarily with its owner.

"We must still focus on prevention, and if it is not possible to keep animals in a particular location, or if it is not possible to keep animals of a certain age there, then livestock farmers must also consider exactly where they keep their animals," said Aimar Rakko, head of hunting at the Ministry of Climate's forestry department.

A hay bale ripped open by a bear. Source: ERR

Tanel Türna, head of the Environmental Board's hunting and aquatic wildlife department, suggested a change of tactics.

"Perhaps the same manpower being used to drive around the area could instead be directed towards gathering the calves together in the evenings. It certainly wouldn't be an easy undertaking, but it would produce results. The alternative is that these wolves will keep coming back for as long as they have the opportunity to get hold of something somewhere," Türna said.

Bears have also appeared in Soomaa this year and while they have not reportedly slaughtered livestock, they have instead raided hay bales, stored as animal fodder. The Environmental Board has issued 64 hunting permits, 26 of which have been suspended by a court at the request of the Eesti Suurkiskjad (Large Carnivores) NGO. The latest permits were suspended within two hours the Friday before last, October 23.

The same NGO has successfully appealed to the courts in the past to suspend large predator culls. The wolf cull season usually runs from November 1 to the following February. Bear cull season runs in the fall and has just ended.

World.title: Latvia's insolvent Valka stops cooperation programs with Estonia's Valga
World.content:
Cross-border cooperation projects between Estonia's Valga and Latvia's Valka have been suspended as the Latvian municipality is insolvent and must undergo a financial restructuring process.

In Latvia, the size of a local budget depends on the number of residents. There are 8,000 people registered as living in Valka municipality, but another thousand or so have registered as residents of Valga municipality in southern Estonia over the years because benefits are higher and the healthcare system is better.

Another 500 people commute to work in Estonia every day. However, their taxes do not reach Valka, and they are not included in its population register either, even though their families continue to live on the Latvian side and use services there.

"We have the same obligations imposed by the state as a municipality with, for example, a thousand more residents. The tasks do not change – children's rights must still be protected, municipal policing and the prevention of cyberattacks must still be ensured. All this costs a lot and means that we can allocate less and less money to sports, culture and community events. This is not right," said Vents Armands Krauklis, chairman of Valka municipality.

Latvia's State Audit Office has criticized Valka for spending more money than it could guarantee in the budget, and for disorder in the heating and water supply sectors.

For many years, Valka municipality has operated as a property management company, through which residents paid their utility bills. However, many failed to pay, debts were not collected. Calculations by the State Audit Office show the tariffs did not reflect actual costs either. At the end of last year, residents owed the municipality more than €1 million.

"In our assessment, the reason for Valka's financial difficulties is weak financial management and insufficient internal controls. More revenue was planned in the budget than could realistically be collected. Obligations to implement European Union projects were also undertaken too optimistically, even though there was no certainty that these expenditures could be made at all," said Ilze Badere, a member of the council of Latvia's State Audit Office.

There are currently €400,000 in unpaid bills.

Valga-Valka Source: ERR/Helen Wright

The Pudrumäe recreation area connects the two countries and has been a joint development project. In the future, such projects with Valga will be put on hold. The Ministry of Finance will primarily focus on ensuring that Valka municipality fulfills the duties laid down in the constitution and other laws.

No one can say how long the process will last or if a long-term solution for the budget will be found.

"Valka does not directly owe Valga any money. At the same time, Valga municipal government has begun drafting the joint Valga-Valka strategy, which is a very important document for obtaining funding from the European Union, together with the Vidzeme Planning Region. It may be inevitable that Valka municipality will merge with a somewhat wealthier municipality in the region, be it Smiltene or Valmiera," said Valga municipal mayor Mart Kase.

World.title: Iraq clinches six world titles at 2026 WAMAS International Olympiad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq achieved a sweeping victory at the 2026 WAMAS International Olympiad in Turkey, securing six global titles—including two Super Champion honors and four Champion titles—across rigorous competitions spanning smart mathematics, coding, languages, and rapid mental arithmetic against more than 400 competitors from over 20 nations.

Guljan Berdibekova, President of the WAMAS International Rapid Mental Arithmetic Organization, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the Iraqi delegation delivered an extraordinary performance that stunned participating international teams.

The young Iraqi competitors swept the highest ranks after completing complex tasks across all four competitive disciplines with zero recorded errors, prompting evaluation committees to re-examine test submissions multiple times to confirm the flawless results. Berdibekova commended the Iraqi delegation’s technical leadership, professional organization, and collegiate assistance provided to fellow international participants.

The tournament featured in-person and remote competitors representing approximately 40 global specialized institutions across more than 20 countries, including the United Kingdom, China, Japan, Russia, Bulgaria, Romania, India, Iran, Armenia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Algeria, Tunisia, Lebanon, and host nation Turkey.

International trainer Shahad Al-Rubaie, head of the Iraqi delegation, affirmed to INA that the victory highlights the intellectual caliber of Iraqi youth on the global stage.

Al-Rubaie noted that the team navigated administrative and travel visa obstacles ahead of the tournament before securing the two prestigious Super Champion awards—a title reserved exclusively for competitors who achieve perfect, error-free scores across all four competition categories—alongside four global champion titles.

She urged domestic authorities to expand sponsorship, institutional patronage, and logistical support for gifted Iraqi children to facilitate broader participation in premier international STEM competitions.

World.title: Iraqi oil exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan port surge to 500,000 BPD
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Total Iraqi crude oil exports routed through Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal rose to 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) on Sunday evening, November 1, 2026, marking the highest export volume recorded since pipeline flows through Turkish territory were officially restored.

The surge reflects a substantial 150,000-bpd throughput expansion over the previous 350,000-bpd baseline, driven by the integration of southern crude from Basra into the northern pipeline network.

According to oil industry sources across production, the federal government achieved the 43% export expansion by trucking crude extracted from Basra fields north to the Khurmala junction. From Khurmala, the crude enters the primary Iraq–Turkey export pipeline traversing the Kurdistan Region toward the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.

The current 500,000-bpd export mix breaks down as follows:

Basra Fields: 200,000 bpd (40% of total northern pipeline flows), transported overland via tanker trucks to the Khurmala injection hub.

Kurdistan Region Fields: 175,000 bpd (35% of total flows).

Kirkuk Fields (North Oil Company): 125,000 bpd (25% of total flows).

The multi-field supply strategy transforms northern export dynamics, utilizing available spare capacity within the northern pipeline grid to diversify export conduits beyond southern offshore terminals and boost total federal crude commercialization.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt advance Basra–Haditha pipeline and petrochemical talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The tripartite cooperation team comprising Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt convened on Sunday, November 1, 2026, to examine the technical, engineering, and operational specifications of the strategic Basra–Haditha crude oil export pipeline, alongside joint ventures across petroleum refining, petrochemicals, and renewable energy.

According to a Ministry of Oil statement, Ali Warid Hammoud, Director General of the Oil Projects Company (SCOP), chaired the second virtual session of the Iraqi working team monitoring projects sponsored under the Iraqi-Jordanian-Egyptian Trilateral Coordination Council.

The deliberations focused extensively on the engineering parameters of the Basra–Haditha pipeline corridor, assessing pipeline diameters, throughput capacity, and targeted transit volumes for domestic distribution and export routing.

The meeting detailed route alignments, interconnecting branches, and logistical integration frameworks designed to serve tripartite energy security. The Iraqi delegation provided comprehensive technical clarifications addressing inquiries submitted by Jordanian and Egyptian counterparts regarding pipeline hookups and flow economics.

The trilateral agenda also covered the development of a joint petrochemical complex, assessing feedstock allocations of crude oil, intermediate petroleum cuts, and industrial raw materials required to sustain the downstream hub.

Discussions further evaluated the construction of strategic storage depots, refining expansion plans, and the creation of alternative Iraqi export outlets opening onto the Red Sea and the Mediterranean Basin.

Participants reviewed several industrial initiatives proposed by the Egyptian delegation, including delayed coking unit projects, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production facilities, and potential EPC engagements by specialized Egyptian petroleum firms. The delegations also explored joint technological cooperation in clean hydrogen generation.

Hammoud emphasized the necessity of maintaining regular technical coordination and data-sharing among relevant ministries across Baghdad, Amman, and Cairo to expedite feasibility evaluations, address technical parameters, and transition cross-border infrastructure initiatives from planning frameworks into operational implementation.

The virtual session included the Director General of the Studies, Planning, and Follow-up Directorate, alongside delegates from the Ministry of Oil, the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Industry and Minerals, and their respective Jordanian and Egyptian counterparts.

World.title: UNDP helps Iraqi farmers secure water more efficiently
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Agriculture is getting more difficult for farmers in southern Iraq. Rural households whose earnings rely on the land are under a great deal of strain due to water scarcity, rising temperatures, and rising production costs.

When Iraqi farmers irrigate their farms with traditional diesel-powered pumps, they also have to deal with ongoing fuel costs, frequent failures, necessary repair, and pollution.

To assist farmers in securing water more effectively and lessen their reliance on diesel, a solar-powered irrigation system and modern irrigation technology were installed in cooperation with the Japanese government through a UNDP program.

The initiative reduces fuel expenses and equipment maintenance costs, leading to savings that can better support the incomes of farmers and their families, as well as enhance agricultural activities.

The program has improved the effective use of water resources, which are becoming more limited. When used in conjunction with modern sprinkler irrigation, the solar system enables more precise water application, minimizing needless losses and promoting agricultural output.

The impact on the land is evident. Other farmers are being encouraged to reconsider the future of their farms, as areas that previously struggled with water shortages are now being cultivated again.

Water shortages, soil salinity, land degradation, and energy insecurity pose a danger to agricultural livelihoods, food security, and community stability in southern Iraq. The program addresses these growing climatic challenges.

World.title: Iraq to keep oil output unchanged in December 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – During a virtual meeting on Sunday, seven OPEC+ nations, including Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman, agreed to maintain their required September 2026 production levels through December 2026.

Iraq’s required allocation remains unchanged at 4.43 million barrels per day.

The decision comes as OPEC+ seeks to maintain market stability amid regional disruptions.

Iraq has been working to push for higher production baselines—including ambitions toward a six million barrels per day baseline in future negotiations—while balancing export flows through alternative routes.

The group is scheduled to hold its next review meeting on November 29, 2026.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Iraq is a founding member of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), which was established in Baghdad in September 1960.

Iraq currently ranks as the second-largest crude oil producer in OPEC after Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Iraq, Saudi Arabia to revive joint oil export pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Saudi Arabia has given preliminary approval to revive the joint oil export pipeline project with Iraq, sources told local news outlet Shafaq News on Saturday.

The original 1,568-kilometer pipeline—which runs from Iraq’s Zubair oilfield in Basra to the Saudi Red Sea port of Yanbu and has been idle since 1990.

Riyadh argues that rehabilitation would cost nearly as much as constructing a new line, and Iraq would have to cover part of the cost for its section.

Understandings with Saudi Arabia have emerged as one of the most significant paths through which Iraq intends to revive a historic pipeline that has been idle for more than three decades. The step is part of a larger effort to increase the country’s oil export flexibility.

The pipeline passes through key stations in Saudi Arabia, making it one of the longest oil pipelines in the region.

Following the Gulf War, the pipeline was shut down in August 1990. It remained out of operation for decades, despite Iraq’s several attempts to restart it.

According to reports, the project initially cost over $2.6 billion and features an advanced infrastructure of storage tanks and loading terminals. The infrastructure makes it a compelling option for reuse, contingent upon an agreement between the two parties.

This pipeline is a strategic option to export oil through the Red Sea, lessening Iraq’s dependency on the Strait of Hormuz and providing more flexibility in regulating export flows.

The revival of the pipeline may boost economic connections between Iraq and Saudi Arabia and offer new options for collaboration in the energy industry, given the rising demand for secure and dependable export routes.

World.title: Iran’s gas supplies to Iraq fall to 10.5 million cubic meters
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iran’s gas supplies to Iraq have fallen to 10.5 million cubic meters per day—a development likely to exacerbate the challenges facing the electricity sector in the country.

An Iraqi source told Attaqa News that Iranian gas supplies to the southern region have ceased, with flows now limited exclusively to the central region.

Iranian gas flows to Iraq are currently less than 20 million cubic meters per day, as reported roughly a month ago.

The decline in supplies comes at a time when Iraq’s electricity sector relies on Iranian gas to operate several power plants—a situation complicated by pressure from Washington on Baghdad to halt these imports.

A month ago, gas supplies from Tehran ranged between 15 and 20 million cubic meters per day before dropping to their current level—a decline attributed to Iran’s rising gas demand amid falling temperatures.

Tehran is facing a domestic supply shortage, which has compelled it to reduce export volumes, particularly during cold weather.

The decline in supplies to Iraq affects several provinces, as Tehran typically meets between 30 and 40 percent of the requirements for several Iraqi power plants.

Gas supplies have experienced frequent interruptions in 2026, compelling the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity to implement emergency measures.

These measures include utilizing domestic gas and working with the Ministry of Oil to get alternative fuels, such as red diesel.

In March 2026, the suspension of Iranian gas supplies to Iraq—following an attack on the South Pars field—resulted in the loss of approximately 3,100 megawatts of power capacity.

According to agreements between Baghdad and Tehran, supply levels must be between 25 and 35 million cubic meters per day in the winter and around 55 million cubic meters per day in the summer.

World.title: IMF prepares new lending program for Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is preparing a new lending program for Iraq after starting formal discussions with authorities in Baghdad.

IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva confirmed that Iraq submitted an official request for a new support program during the IMF’s annual meetings in Bangkok.

The IMF forecasts that Iraq’s economy will contract by 16 percent in 2026, heavily impacted by regional conflict and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, which constrains its vital energy exports.

IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack stated that the fund is engaging directly with Iraqi authorities to understand their economic priorities, address structural vulnerabilities, and shape the structure of the financial support package.

Iraq’s last formal program with the IMF concluded in 2019, and the country is scheduled to pay approximately $428 million in interest to the institution through 2030.

Since the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East on February 28, Tehran has almost completely restricted navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran now mandates that vessels follow specific routes, occasionally targeting those that attempt to pass without prior coordination. In response, Washington has imposed a blockade on Iranian ports.

The Iraqi economy relies heavily on energy exports, most of which transit through this strait.

World.title: '2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season.

Chamber of Trade & Industry (CTI) chairman Brijesh Goyal said nearly 80% of the approximately three lakh shops in markets surrounding the rally venue remained shut amid concerns over traffic restrictions, congestion and the expected arrival of large crowds.

The disruption also affected the movement of customers, suppliers and dealers from towns surrounding the national capital. According to Goyal, around three lakh to four lakh people who regularly travel to Delhi for business did not arrive, while approximately 5,000 vehicles, including tempos and trucks, could not transport goods to markets in Old Delhi and Central Delhi.

âDue to the rally held at Ramlila Maidan today, about 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity were affected. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groupsâcomprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)âabout 80% of these shopsâroughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000âremained closed today,â he said.





Goyal added that loading and unloading operations were disrupted, affecting wholesale and retail businesses during one of the busiest periods of the year.

âThe movement of goodsâloading and unloadingâwas completely disrupted. During the peak Diwali season, these markets with individual turnovers collectively generate business worth approximately 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees. Even where shops remained open, sales were virtually non-existent; there were simply no customers,â he said.

Putting the estimated losses at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, Goyal questioned who would compensate traders for the business disruption.

âThe question now arises: who will compensate for this loss, or who will make up for itâwill the organisers do so?â he said.

He said the timing of the rally had compounded the impact, as traders were preparing for the festive rush ahead of Dhanteras, scheduled four days later. Businesses in the affected markets depend heavily on the movement of customers and goods during this period.

Traders had warned of business losses ahead of rally

Ahead of the gathering, traders across several major commercial hubs in Delhi had opposed holding the rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season. They warned that traffic congestion and restrictions could disrupt wholesale markets and affect the livelihoods of thousands of daily-wage workers.

The Automotive Parts Merchant Association (APMA), based at Kashmere Gate, said the rally's location could affect commercial activity across a three-kilometre radius, covering several major trading hubs in the capital.

APMA president Vinay Narang said traders were not opposed to democratic protests but objected to the timing and choice of venue.

"We are not aligned with any political party, nor are we against democratic protests. But the timing and the venue are completely wrong. Ramlila Maidan is located in the middle of Asiaâs largest commercial zoneâwith major markets like Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Daryaganj, Mori Gate, and Kashmere Gate within a three-kilometre radius," Narang said.

Rahul's video appeal for participants to shop from local traders

Amid concerns raised by traders' associations, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people travelling to Delhi for the rally to support local businesses by shopping from their stores during the festive season.

In a video message posted on X on Saturday, Gandhi urged participants to combine their participation in the protest with shopping from small businesses.

âTomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March.

It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,â Gandhi said.

âProtest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,â he added.

The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha also accused the BJP of spreading rumours about the rally's potential economic impact.

âI know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours,â he said, adding, âBut let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders.â

INDIA bloc holds rally against SIR, alleged electoral irregularities

The INDIA bloc held the rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging irregularities in the exercise.

Several Opposition leaders attended the gathering, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Protesters also raised slogans such as "Vote chor, gaddi chhod", demanding accountability over alleged electoral irregularities.

'Business boomed': Jairam Ramesh hits back at BJP over traders' loss claims

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Monday rejected claims that the INDIA bloc rally disrupted business in Delhi, alleging that the BJP's campaign warning of economic losses had been contradicted by increased shopping in local markets.

In a post on X, Ramesh accused the BJP of spreading fear among traders and discouraging people from travelling to the national capital ahead of the rally. He said people arriving from different parts of the country were also expected to shop, benefiting businesses across Delhi.

"Every business operating in Delhi would benefit, directly or indirectly," he said.

Ramesh alleged that the campaign was aimed at diverting attention from the Opposition's allegations of "vote theft" and protecting Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"But the exact opposite happened," he said.

Claiming that Rahul Gandhi's appeal had received a positive response, Ramesh said wholesale markets in Old Delhi had opened and business had picked up, while small shopkeepers and street vendors had also benefited.

"The people of Delhi and those who came from across the country responded to this smear campaign in their own way. In response to Rahul Gandhi ji's appeal, people went shopping in Delhi's markets.

Shops in the wholesale markets of Old Delhi opened, and business boomed. On top of that, people bought goods in abundance from small shopkeepers and street vendors too. Newspaper reports themselves are exposing the falsehood of this fake narrative," he said.

Thanking traders, shopkeepers and Delhi residents, Ramesh said they had supported local businesses alongside the democratic protest.

"The BJP should understand that the voice of democracy cannot be suppressed by fear or smear campaigns," he said.

His remarks came in contrast to the estimates shared by CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal, who claimed that traders had suffered losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, with around 2.5 lakh shops remaining closed.

Amit Shah questions timing of rally, Rahul alleges shops shut in Delhi

Earlier, Union Home Minister Amit Shah had criticised the Opposition over holding the rally during the festive shopping season, saying traders had repeatedly requested a postponement until after Diwali.

"Traders in Delhi pleaded with them, explaining that they have only one week in the entire year when the bulk of their business takes place.

'If we stock up on sweets and they don't sell, what happens? We suffer a loss. If we stock up on firecrackers and they don't sell, what happens? We suffer a loss...'" Shah said.

"The traders held press conferences--not once, but three times--wrote letters, and implored them to hold their rally after Diwali. But noâthey insisted on holding their rally on that very dayâthe same dark day when the anti-Sikh riots, the Sikh massacre, took place," the Home Minister remarked.
